## 💰 Shimmer / site — **ONE PURSE PER ACCOUNT: the marks split** (2026-08-23, hub) · *Last touched 2026-08-23 (hub) — shipped, deployed, prod-verified*

### Left off — SHIPPED `6a53989`, deployed, pushed, 26-check browser probe green on prod
**Alex ruled it:** two people on one machine sharing a coin balance is wrong, and nothing recorded who
earned a coin. `ather:save:wallet` and `ather:save:magii` were the last one-per-browser slots — #682
scoped `shimmer` because it UPLOADS and left these two on the grounds their damage is contained.
Contained is not the same as right.
- `gameSlot(game, owner)` covers the family; `adoptAnonSlots` moves the anonymous purse in on first
  sign-in. **Without adoption, scoping shows every existing player a balance of ZERO** on ship day with
  their coins one key over. For a world save that reads as "my garden is gone"; for a currency it reads
  as theft, because the player can name the number.
- `SaveOwnerBoot` answers "who is playing" once for the whole site, because the purse has no boot gate
  and never could — SiteNav renders the balance on every page. ⚠ **Deliberately not a cookie read in the
  server layout**: that opts the ENTIRE site out of static rendering to learn a name only the purse
  needs. The answer lands a few frames late and the live readouts re-read on `SAVE_OWNER_EVENT`.
- Signing out clears the owner — **sign-out does not reload the page**, so without it the tab keeps
  writing into the account that just left.

### Decisions
- ★★★ **The one-word change that would confiscate every wallet is now an assert.** `ather-epoch.ts`
  deletes every key starting with `SAVE_KEY_PREFIX` on a world bump, and that constant is
  `ather:save:shimmer`. Generalising it to `ather:save:` to "cover the family" reads as tidying and
  would empty every purse on the next reset, against the epoch's own promise that Marks survive one.
  Four asserts: shimmer slots IN the sweep, wallet slots OUT, both scopings.
- ★ **A claim key here, an in-blob stamp for shimmer, and they are not interchangeable.** Shimmer's
  stamp must survive a round trip through the SERVER so the server can refuse a foreign blob. But a
  stamp only survives if every writer preserves it, and both of these blobs are rewritten WHOLESALE on
  every change — a stamp would be erased by the first coin earned, silently re-opening the slot to a
  second account. Neither uploads, so neither needs the server half.
- **Adoption is per-game and never overwrites a balance the account already has** — their own purse is
  the newer claim, and adopting over it destroys coins rather than misfiling them.
- ★★ **WHAT WAS NOT PROVED, RECORDED AS NOT PROVED.** Two gates hold "nothing may act on a balance
  before the owner is known" (`useWallet().loading`, the card page's load gate). **Removing BOTH left
  the browser probe green** — the welcome stake is really held by the persisted `seeded` flag inside the
  per-account card save, so neither gate was the thing standing in the way. Kept as defence in depth and
  **labelled untested in both files** rather than dressed up as verified. Hunting the reachable case
  found a real one (the card save read before the owner is known, which only bites an account whose
  adoption LOCKED) and even that leaves no trace in storage, so the probe cannot see it either.
- **Verified:** save-slot 50 asserts · wallet 35 · 8 mutations, 6 red (the two survivors are the labelled
  gates). The wallet's includes the module-constant trap — **a slot cached at import pins the tab to the
  anonymous purse, which is this bug wearing the fix as a disguise.** Then end to end on the real page:
  240 anonymous marks adopted to the coin, B inherits none, A survives B, returning as A re-grants nothing.
- **Housekeeping, flagged by the play window:** a stray 0-byte `accounts.db` at the repo root (mine — a
  mistyped sqlite3 path creates a file wherever you point it and never says so) removed, and `.gitignore`
  widened from `/data/` to `*.db`/`*-wal`/`*-shm`/`*.sqlite*` **anywhere**. This repo is PUBLIC and
  `data/accounts.db` holds emails and google subject ids; one `git add -A` from any of four windows was
  the failure mode.

### Files
`lib/save-slot.ts` · `lib/save-slot.test.ts` · `lib/wallet.ts` · `lib/wallet.test.ts` · `lib/use-wallet.ts` ·
`lib/use-cloud-save.ts` · `lib/accounts/use-account.ts` · `_components/SaveOwnerBoot.tsx` ·
`_components/SiteNav.tsx` · `layout.tsx` · `magii/page.tsx` · `scripts/save-owner-probe.mts` · `.gitignore`

## 🌱 Shimmer — **SAPLING ICON: the bag read a glow mask as a cutout** (2026-08-23, hub) · *Last touched 2026-08-23 (hub, late)*

### Left off — SHIPPED `5c15074`, deployed + pushed
Alex, holding the sapling play fixed that morning: *"the sapling is just a green 2d rectangle."* It was.
**A THIRD texture disagreeing** — `crossIcon` sampled `paintFor`, and every painter in `tiles.ts` writes
through `put()`, whose alpha argument **defaults to 0**. Alpha is a **GLOW mask** there, not transparency
(`rasterIcon` says so in its own header), so the tile is a full sheet of leaf noise with no silhouette,
and forcing every texel opaque was the CORRECT reading of a glow-masked sheet. **Not an oversight — right
about the wrong texture.** The world draws saplings with `leafPixels` + `alphaTest: 0.5`, tinted per
species by `vertexColors`. Bag and ground derived one plant from two sources; the shape lived in the one
the icon never read. `leafCutout` now multiplies `leafPixels` by the species tint and `crossIcon` honours
source alpha. Measured 296→140 opaque of 2304; colours 13 → 25/20/35/37. Rendered before/after and looked.

### Decisions
- ⚠⚠ **The first regression guard was DECORATION and passed with the bug restored.** It asked for holes
  inside the bounding box — but the two quads are OFFSET, so the corners are empty however solid the quads
  are. It could not fail for any input. Replaced with: force the same source opaque, require the picture to
  get bigger. **Two derivations of one source, no threshold to nudge.** Verified red (296 vs 296).
- Guard ⑤ was green throughout the bug: a solid cross really does cover less than a cube. *"Smaller than a
  cube"* and *"shaped like a plant"* are different claims.

### Next
- **ART CALL, ALEX'S:** it reads as a leafy sprig, not a seedling with a stem — the silhouette is inherited
  from the canopy leaf mask. A hand-painted icon in the existing `painted` tier is the cheapest fix.
- **3D-rendered icons** (offscreen render target from real geometry, cached like today's data URLs) — its own
  piece, would upgrade the whole hotbar. ⚠ picaso/Blender pre-render is the OTHER route but collides with the
  art-medium law: living things stay live glow.
- ⚠ **`scripts/icon-sheet.mts` calls `iconPixels` (the cube), not `iconPixelsFor`** — so the contact sheet
  renders a cube for every sapling and structurally CANNOT show this class of bug. Route it through the game's
  entry point.

### Files
`voxel3d/tex/item-icon.ts` · `voxel3d/tex/icon-source.test.ts`

## 🌉 Shimmer voxel3d — **BRIDGES: plank · trestle · viaduct; ribbon deck, timber bents, fence railings** (2026-08-22, world) · *Last touched 2026-08-22 (world, night — railings as pieces)*
> **★★★ SLICE 5 — THE RAILING IS `fence` PIECES, NOT VOXELS (`a0ecfe6` + hub host wiring `3a34b4a`, GENVER 30, live).** Alex: *"we are still trying to use whole blocks on the railings when it should actually be more like the fences.. idk if we should make a whole new item called railings ..what do u think?"* **Answer: NO NEW ITEM — what he described already exists and is already load-bearing elsewhere.** `pieces.ts` › `fence` is a 0.18 centre post whose ARMS are derived per connected side at sync (*"connection is a question you ask neighbours, never a thing you store"*), and **`holds.ts` has emitted it as a GENERATED wall-top parapet since 08-08**, gen ids and tombstones included. ⚠ The clincher is not the draw count: **a fence occupies its full cell for COLLISION on purpose while drawing thin** — exactly a bridge railing, stops you walking off, does not read as a wall.
> - **★★ THE PATTERN OF THE WHOLE EVENING, NAMED: a thing that is geometrically CORRECT and semantically the WRONG OBJECT.** Solid pier that was a wall · solid parapet that was a kerb · deck that was the accidental shape of an intersection · railing built from the wrong vocabulary. Every one passed its tests, because the tests asked *"is this well-formed"* and never *"is this the thing it is supposed to be"*. **Alex's eye caught all four before any assert did.** The holds' own line is the fix: a structure *"reads as something a builder could have made, because it literally is made of the same catalogue"* — inventing a bespoke railing would make bridges the one structure assembled from parts nobody can hold.
> - **ONE POST PER CELL, not every third** — fence arms come from ADJACENCY, so spaced posts grow no rail between them and read as lonely stakes (mutation-tested). The bridge now emits **nothing** above the deck; a block back at `yc+1` is the kerb returning.
> - **2103 asserts.** The sweep runs `bridgeGenPiecesForCol` in column-sized tiles **exactly as the host does**, so it exercises the bbox filter rather than the flat list behind it: no piece claimed by two columns · every post on a deck edge at deck height · every post adjacent to a neighbour · ids stable across a rebuild.
> - **★ TWO ASSERT CORRECTIONS.** The kerb check asks the **BRIDGE**, not the world — `materialAt` also reports bank ground at the abutment, and conflating them turns a correct abutment into a red (**second time that exact confusion produced a wrong red tonight**). And the id-stability check compares the id **SETS**, not their count: a mutation that reshaped every id kept the count identical and walked through.
> - ⚠ **LABELLED, NOT CLAIMED:** id stability is proven WITHIN a build, never across versions. Keying on crossing + world CELL is what protects tombstones from a geometry change; **no in-build test can catch that**, so the id's shape is the guard and is spelled out in code.
> - ⚠ **HUB'S HOST-SIDE GUARD TOOK FOUR ATTEMPTS**, three wrong for the wrong reason — a text scan that found its own marker in the comment explaining the marker, a windowed scan that moved its target out of the window (**false GREEN, the direction that ships**), and a brace-bounded scan satisfied by a warning that NAMED the function. **All three caused by comments that were correct: the better the documentation, the more convincing the decoy.** Comments are stripped before scanning now, which `purity.test.ts` already did.

The `worldSolid` fallback gives the LOWER post an arm into the riser; the upper post cannot answer it. **155 steps remain, concentrated on the RAMPS — flat crowns are continuous runs.** Photographed: the crown reads as a handrail, the ramps read as stepped segments. ★ **This is where a dedicated `railing` piece would finally earn its place** — one that can express a slope, which `fence` structurally cannot. A constant bay is the same defect slice 1 removed from the deck height: **a number that does not know the span it is spanning.** So bay LENGTH is derived and bay COUNT stays roughly constant, which is the way round real crossings work; piers divide the span evenly so none can crowd a bank.

- **The bug was the altitude of the abstraction.** A bridge was three parity tests inside `materialAt`: flat deck at `table + 1`, stone wherever `x%4==0 && z%4==0`, rail off a neighbour `roadAt` probe. All three are statements about a COLUMN, so the rule could never know a bridge was happening — deck skimmed the water with nothing passing under, piers stood on a world grid unrelated to the span (bunched, or absent on the wrong parity), and a 4-block creek generated identically to a 149-block river. `voxel/bridges.ts` surveys the spine once per seed on the `holds.ts` pattern (11 crossings, 99ms cold, 0ms after). Materials pass in as arguments — depth.ts↔attrs.ts is a cycle.
- **★★ THE ARCH IS STRUCTURAL, NOT DECORATIVE.** `height.ts:368` pins river banks at `table + 1`, which is exactly why the old deck sat there: it met the bank flush with no ramp logic. Lift a FLAT deck for clearance and you owe abutment ramps at both ends. An arch springs from `table + 1` at both banks and rises over the middle, so the join stays free and the clearance lands where it is wanted — and a creek keeps its flat plank because its arch rounds to nothing. **Span-typing arriving out of one formula instead of a switch.**
- **★★ AND IT MUST CLIMB IN HALF-STEPS.** `STEP_CAPTURE` 0.55 walks a +0.5 rise; a full +1 "stays out of reach and stays a vault". A whole-block arch is a bridge you MANTLE across. Slabs are a real material since 08-11, so the deck climbs in `HALF_BIT` courses and needs **zero** new locomotion. `RISE_PER_4` exists to hold that invariant and nothing else — measured steepest step on both seeds: exactly 0.50.
- **Three defects the oracle caught, each shipped-looking:** (1) the caller's y-gate was `RIVER_DEPTH + 4` = 7 and an arch wants 10 — it would have **decapitated every crossing in the world**, silently, since a clipped deck still reads as a deck from the bank. `BRIDGE_REACH` is now derived from the geometry constants and asserted against the real corridor. (2) a rail is a row's outermost cell, so on a **2-cell row both cells are rail** and the row becomes a wall — at the bridge MOUTH specifically, because the waterline cuts the road diagonally. Every crossing on both seeds was walled at one end or both → `RAIL_MIN_WIDTH`. (3) `pierBed >= bed` **is satisfied by equality**, so collapsing every pier onto the crossing minimum passed all 440 asserts; a mutation sweep found it and the oracle now RE-DERIVES each bed from worldgen via `pierPos`. ⚠ Compare derivations, not values.
- **★★ A PICTURE ASKS THE QUESTION, THE GENERATOR ANSWERS IT (now in PATTERNS).** The in-world shot showed bright gaps in the deck that read exactly like missing geometry, against 456 green asserts. **Believing either would have been wrong.** An ASCII cross-section out of the real `materialAt` settled it: water y121, air y122–123, deck y124 — the gaps were the river under the arch, the feature photographed. It also confirmed two things invisible from the bank: piers run bed-to-deck, and the 2-wide footing course is there at y119.
- **No hand-written fixture anywhere in the oracle** — a bridge is something worldgen FINDS, so a literal would be a mirror agreeing with the survey while both went stale. Mutation-swept 6/6: flat deck · constant rise · whole-block arch · rail guard removed · collapsed pier beds · pier margin removed.

**Next:**
1. **ALEX WALKS ONE.** Still the open item — the camera says both read, nobody has felt a deck underfoot or tested a mouth. `/tp -149 -755` + `/look 257` = the trestle; `/tp -600 -1601` = the viaduct. ⚠ `/tp` needs the `/` sent on its own first or the line goes to CHAT.
2. ✅ **DONE — the trestle stands on a BENT** (`5c901c2`, GENVER 28, verified in-world). Its pier was a solid block up to 5 cells wide under a 7-cell deck **in the deck's own timber**, so support and roadway merged into one mass and it read as a wall with a road on top. ⚠ **The viaduct looked right for a reason that had nothing to do with its geometry being right** — stone contrasts with the deck, so the contrast did the separating, and that made it false evidence that the trestle was fine. Now two mirrored posts + a cap beam + a sill at the bed: `.D...D.` under `.DDDDD.` with water running between the legs. **You cannot quarry a 5-wide block of wood.**
   - **★★★ SYMMETRY WAS THE TELL FOR THREE BUGS AND THERE WAS NO SYMMETRY ASSERT.** All three were one root — *a continuous coordinate placed across a rasterised grid* — in three costumes: placing across the deck by `|s|` caught two cells on one flank and none on the other (`.D.DDD.`, masonry off-centre); the post course chosen by per-cell along-span distance produced a **single lonely post** (`.#.....`) because cells sharing a visual row carry different `t`; and a centre post **cannot be centred on an even row** (`(n-1)>>1` = 3 of 8, mirror 4). Everything across the deck is placed by **row INDEX** now. One cheap invariant caught the first and then caught the next two *as they were fixed*, and it prints the offending row as ASCII rather than a boolean. ⚠ **For anything mirrored by construction, assert the mirror — it costs one comparison and fails on defects you have not thought of yet.**
3. **⚠ THE OBLIQUE CROSSING IS UNTOUCHED AND IS THE BIGGER HALF OF ALEX'S COMPLAINT.** Measured at the viaduct midpoint: the water is **147 blocks along the road axis and 74 at the narrowest bearing — 2.0× longer than a square crossing.** *"Crosses the water in the longest way possible"* is literally accurate. No bridge change fixes it; the ROAD has to bend to cross square and bend back, which is `story-path` and also carries waystones and hold gates. **Needs Alex's yes before anyone goes near it.**
4. ✅ **DONE — `gloview-village-3` is a viaduct now** (5 piers, 24.8-block bays, level running deck). Remaining span question: whether `trestle` should reach further than 55 blocks, since 63 and 73 are stone today and might read better as timber.

The distinction canon had been using since 08-18 without writing down: **a tuft yields a SEED, a ground grows a PLANT.** You pick a Violetbloom where it grows; you do not get its seed out of grass. **So the grass-tuft ruling is untouched and `isMeadowCrop`'s `tier === 1` needed no edit** — it was right.

> **🌊 THE WATER SHEET WAS INERT IN THE GAME FOR AN HOUR, WITH 166 ASSERTS GREEN (`6740b35` + `19c7edb`, DEPLOYED).** Alex asked to pull it up in Chrome — which is the only reason this was found.
> - **★★★ EVERY ORACLE REACHES A COLUMN THROUGH `generateColumn`. THE GAME DOES NOT.** The worker generates and posts raw **VOXELS**; `VoxelWorld` builds a **fresh `Column`** and refills it. I stamped `genSeed` inside `generateColumn` (which runs in the worker), so it never reached the live path, `buildWaterSurface` returned `null`, and **the entire feature was a no-op on prod while every test passed.** ⚠ The warning is written **ten lines above** the code I needed to change — recorded when the slump mask *"passed its whole oracle and did nothing in the actual game."* **Second costume, one feature later.** Same family as prebuilt-worker-vs-source: **two ways into one object, and the tests only ever take one of them.**
> - **★★ FIXED THREE WAYS, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS ABOUT MEMORY.** (1) stamp it at the adoption site, beside the slump rebuild where the warning lives. (2) **SPLIT THE DEPENDENCY SO A MISSED STAMP DEGRADES INSTEAD OF DISAPPEARING** — `tops` comes from CELLS and needs no seed, so wall suppression works on any column with voxels; only the SLOPE needs the table. A seedless column now renders a flat sheet with no walls rather than nothing. (3) **test the column the HOST builds** — `column.test.ts` meshes an ADOPTED column (fresh Column, voxels copied, nothing else carried). Mutation-tested by re-gating on the seed: red.
> - **★★ AND THE CLAMP I ADDED AS A GUARD WAS ITSELF THE BUG (`4cca7e8`).** Corners were clamped into `[fallback-1, fallback]` where `fallback` is **the asking quad's** lattice height — so a corner's height depended on **which quad asked**. At a step the upper quad took the true table and the lower clamped a block down: every step became a cliff between two sheets. **The design's one load-bearing property is that a corner is a pure function of position** — I rejected Minecraft's cell-averaging for breaking it, then broke it myself three lines later with something that looked like hygiene. ★ **No assert about the clamp could catch it, because the clamp did exactly what it claimed.** Replaced with the PROPERTY (a corner shared across levels gets ONE height), mutation-verified by restoring the clamp.
> - **★ THE RIM HAD TO BE PULLED ONTO THE SHEET TOO (`19c7edb`).** Surviving edge faces sat on the BLOCK top while the sheet sits on the true table, so every shoreline grew a lip and the lake read as a row of boxes. **The two heights disagree for a nameable reason:** the sheet samples the RAW table, the blocks were placed from `waterSurfaceAt`, which **clamps a perimeter column to its dry neighbour's ground** — so the mismatch is worst exactly where a player stands. Top pair only, downward only, never more than one block.
> - **⚠ My first rim sweep had TWO survivors** because a flat-pond fixture cannot distinguish direction or which vertices move; added fixtures that can. **One survivor is LABELLED rather than tested around** — dropping the `!== top` guard survives because the direction guard already spares every bottom vertex. *A guard that cannot fail must say so.*
> - **⚠ AND A FALSE ALARM I ALMOST RAISED:** `ls node_modules` came back EMPTY and I nearly reported the install destroyed by the disk incident. My shell was simply `cd`'d into a subdirectory. **Check `pwd` before believing a relative path.**

> **🌊 THE WALLS OF WATER — AND THE OBVIOUS CULPRIT WAS THE SMALLEST ONE (`5f4dccb` + worker `3753519b66`, play lane, DEPLOYED).** Alex: *"its showing the walls of the water blocks underwater."* `greedy.test.ts` **158 → 165 asserts**, **7/7 mutations red on their own**, suite **62/63**, canon **10 CLEAN**.
> - **★★★ MEASURED BEFORE FIXING, AND THE MEASUREMENT OVERTURNED THE PLAN.** 9 real river columns, 118 vertical water faces: **91 SUBMERGED PLANTS · 11 STEP RISERS · 16 GENUINE EDGES.** Reeds on a riverbed are `isPlant`, so `fillSlice` reads them as AIR — the same exemption that lets terrain draw behind a leaf — and the water around one **cuts a face into its cell**: a blue panel standing INSIDE the water, seen through the plant's own crossed quads. **The staircase everyone would blame (and that my approved plan named as the root cause) is the SMALLEST of the three.** I built the steps-only fix first: it moves 118 → **107** and looks like a failed fix.
> - **★★ ONE INEQUALITY COVERS TWO CASES AND SPARES THE THIRD:** is the empty cell across this face at or below the neighbouring column's own water surface? Then it is INSIDE the body of water and no face belongs there. A dry column has no entry, so **the rim is never suppressed** — the over-fix (suppress every water|air face) lets you see straight into the water body, and is a mutation the oracle now catches. **118 → 16.**
> - **★★ THE SHEET SLOPES NOW.** `waterLevelAt` was `Math.floor` of a smooth bilinear table — **the floor is what turns a surface into a staircase**. `waterTableAt` (new, `height.ts`) exposes the pre-floor value and `waterLevelAt` is literally its floor, so it returns the identical number it always did. Surface quad corners sit on the true table instead of the block top.
> - **★★★ A CORNER'S HEIGHT MUST BE A PURE FUNCTION OF WORLD POSITION — THIS REVERSED THE APPROVED PLAN AND THE REVERSAL IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART.** Minecraft averages the four fluid cells touching a corner; **that cannot work here.** A column sees its four edge-neighbours but **not its diagonals** (`Neighbours` = negX/posX/negZ/posZ), so at each of a column's four corners the two sides average different sets, land up to a quarter block apart, and **open a crack where four quads meet**. Sampling the table BY POSITION removes the neighbourhood from the question, so continuity is structural rather than maintained.
> - **★ Data is handed to the mesher, never asked as a predicate** — `greedy.ts`'s own measurement: a per-cell callback cost **22.2ms/column against a 10.5 baseline**. Seed is stamped on the `Column` by `generateColumn` rather than threaded through five `meshColumn` call sites; **undefined is legal** and means no sloped water, so ungenerated fixtures mesh exactly as before.
> - **Differential, working tree vs a `git worktree` at HEAD, 9 real river columns:** **NON-WATER faces 20136 → 20136, BYTE-IDENTICAL including AO** · water 373 → 271. **Worldgen OUTPUT unchanged — no voxel moved**, which is what let the hub window tell Alex the basin would look *better and different* without hedging.

> **🕳️ THE X-RAY UNDER EVERY RIVER — WATER WAS HIDING WHAT IT COVERED, SINCE 08-07 (`dab681e` + worker `77c12e0330` in `ea2af5c`, play lane, DEPLOYED).** Alex saw through the ground underwater. `greedy.test.ts` **147 → 158 asserts**, **6 of 6 mutations red on their own**, suite **62/63**, canon **10 CLEAN**.
> - **★★★ WATER PASSED THE VISIBILITY SWEEP AS AN OPAQUE CUBE, SO WATER|STONE EMITTED NOTHING ON EITHER SIDE.** The rule is *"a face is visible only where exactly one side is solid"* (`greedy.ts:15`), and `:303` made `sol` 1 for water. So **every riverbed and channel wall in the world had no geometry where it met water**: a ray entered the ground, found no interior faces (correctly culled) and left wherever terrain next touched air. **★ The tell was three lines above the bug** — leaves, logs, plants and saplings are each explicitly pulled OUT of the sweep with the reason written down (*a leaf "must neither be merged as a cube nor hide the faces of whatever is behind it"*). **Water wanted the second half of that exemption and not the first, and never got either.**
> - **★★ IT SURVIVED TWO WEEKS BECAUSE ITS COVER WAS ANOTHER BUG'S ABSENCE.** You only ever saw it through a 0.78-opacity surface at a shallow angle, where a missing bed reads convincingly as *deep water*. Going under puts you on the wrong side of the one thing hiding it. **The x-ray is not new; the underwater view removed its cover.** ⚠ Generalises: a defect can be invisible because of where the camera has always been, not because it is small.
> - **★★ THE OBVIOUS FIX IS THE WRONG ONE.** Exempting water the way leaves are exempted makes water|air non-solid on BOTH sides and **deletes the river's own surface** — a missing bed traded for a missing river. So **RANK, not boolean**: air 0 < water 1 < opaque 2, face belongs to the higher side. Generalises to the next translucent material (glass, ice) instead of naming water in the hot loop.
> - **⚠⚠ AND THE RANK CANNOT LIVE IN `sol` — the hub window caught this BEFORE a line was written, and it would have been ugly.** `sol` is not only the face test: **AO does arithmetic on it** (`3 - (s1+s2+corner)`), so an opaque occluder contributing 2 drives AO to **−3** and moves every shadow in the world; and the mask test reads `=== 1`, so opaque cells would **simultaneously stop emitting faces at all**. Neither throws. The lighting half would have surfaced as *an unrelated AO regression that appeared the same day* — the worst possible way to find it. Rank lives in a SECOND array.
> - **★★ EXISTING AO IS UNCHANGED BY CONSTRUCTION, NOT BY CARE.** Every pre-existing face had AIR on its open side, so the open-rank branch picks the same array on the same side; the new branch is **unreachable from an old face**. And for the NEW faces water must NOT occlude, or the bed's eight samples are all occluders and every river gets a **pitch-black floor** — full darkness arriving as a shadow rather than as an error.
> - **Proved on real terrain, old mesher vs new on identical sections** (faces matched by material + centroid + normal): **AO values moved 0 · faces removed 0 · faces added 685, of which NOT water-adjacent 0 · quads 23940 → 24625 (+2.86%)**. ⚠ The "dry" control columns gained faces too — they hold **330 water cells** (sea-level basins). The label was wrong, not the fix; **a control has to be verified, not named.**
> - **⚠ ONE MUTATION SURVIVED THE FIRST SWEEP, AND IT WAS THE ONE THAT MATTERS:** *"AO always reads the opaque-only array"* — the mutation that MOVES existing AO. No fixture could see it because none had water merely **BESIDE** an air-open face; every fixture had water absent or directly covering. **A preservation constraint needs a fixture where the two candidate readings DIFFER**, and "water beside, not above" is that fixture. It exists now.
> - **⚠ `npx tsx` RAN A TEST THAT `tsc` REJECTS.** `MAT.LEAVES` does not exist — the leaf control was passing on `undefined` cells. Green under the runner, red under the typechecker. **The runner is not the gate; run both.**
> - **⚠⚠ A CONCURRENT MUTATION SWEEP CONTAMINATED A BACKGROUND SUITE RUN.** The sweep rewrites `greedy.ts` in place and restores at the end; a full-suite run started earlier was still reading that file and reported `greedy.test.ts` RED. **A red that was real would look identical.** Re-ran with nothing concurrent: 62/63. **Never run a mutation sweep and a suite over the same tree at once** — on a single shared working tree that includes another window's runs.
> - **⏭ THE FIX EXPOSED A DIAL THAT WAS NEVER EXERCISED — ALEX'S CALL, NOT A REGRESSION.** With the bed present, `UNDER.fogFar` 26 leaves a floor two or three blocks below the eye **~10% fogged**, so it renders as bright dry stone: **the water now reads CLEARER than before the fix**. Before this, every underwater pixel was a hole showing something distant, which fogged to full teal — **the tint was doing the right thing for the wrong reason.** ★ Linear distance fog cannot tint a surface at arm's length without collapsing sight distance to ~6 blocks, so this is a **mechanism** question, not a nudge: tint the AMBIENT light as well (only the hemisphere is tinted today) and cut the sun harder, then let fog carry distance alone.
> - **⚠⚠ DEPLOYED FROM AN UNCOMMITTED TREE, AND MY FIRST ACCOUNT OF IT WAS WRONG.** Hub ran `coord build` without `git status`; the build bundled `greedy.ts` while it was still ` M`. I asserted the files had been committed first — **`.coord/last-deploy` 20:47:51 vs `dab681e` 20:48:31 says otherwise, forty seconds the other way.** I reconstructed the order from knowing my own work was finished, and *the memory of doing the work stood in for a record of when it landed*. **The content was ready and the outcome benign, but "ready" and "committed" are different facts and only the second makes a build safe.** ★ The counterfactual is the keeper: one more save inside that window ships a half-edit **and every test still passes, because the suite runs against the TREE and not against what the bundler grabbed.** So: **the lock protects you from other windows and says nothing about your own tree; the suite describes your tree and says nothing about what shipped.** `git status` before the build is the only thing sitting in that gap. Hub's own dirty-tree warning fired one line too late — placement, not failure.

> **🌊 UNDERWATER VIEW SHIPPED 2026-08-20 (`321537c`, play lane) — hole #4 closed.** `voxel3d/underwater.ts` + `underwater.test.ts` **42 asserts / 13 of 13 mutations red on their own**, a third lever on the atmosphere rig, suite **62/63** (merge.test.ts red at HEAD too), canon **10 CLEAN**, tsc clean. ⚠ committed, NOT yet deployed — hub holds the lock.
> - **★★ THE EYE IS NOT THE BODY, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE MODULE.** `locomotion`'s `submerged` is CHEST (py+1.0) AND FEET (py+0.2); the eye rides at py+`EYE_STAND` 1.62. They disagree across a ~0.6-block band, and that band is exactly **treading** — how you swim to a bank and hop out. Driving a screen effect off `submerged` tints the world with your face in the air. The rig samples `camera.position`, which IS the eye, so it asks the right question **by construction** rather than by care; `underwater.ts` is handed an eye height and two cell readings and is **never handed a player**, so the wrong question cannot be asked through the door. Same defect family as the `columnHeight` ground probe: *a measurement that answers a nearby question, used for the one you asked.*
> - **★★ WATER REPLACES THE MEDIUM; GLOOM AND MIST ONLY MODULATE IT.** Those two pull fog **multiplicatively** and compose, which is right for thicker air. Water is a different substance: it **lerps to an absolute and lands last**. Get it wrong and the water inherits its neighbours — swimming at midnight under the Thicket becomes a visibly different pond from the same pond at noon in a meadow, and the deepest water in the game is wherever the trees are. Asserted directly against hostile inputs (§4).
> - **★★ NEITHER CELL PROBE CAN SAY "I DON'T KNOW" — AND A SPRINTER OUTRUNS GENERATION AT 22 u/s.** `voxel()` returns AIR for an ungenerated column (raycast must see no phantom solids); `voxelSolid()` returns PACKED_CLOUD (a body must not fall out of the world). Each is right for its caller and **both answer "not water"** for ground that has not arrived, so either alone blinks the water off at the frontier. ★ **The two lies DISAGREE, which is what makes the truth recoverable:** a real packed-cloud block reads PACKED_CLOUD through *both*, an unloaded column reads AIR through one and PACKED_CLOUD through the other. `Cell` is a three-state and `submersion` returns **null = hold**. Do not simplify it to a boolean; the boolean IS the bug.
> - **★★ THE SKY DOME IS `fog: false`, SO PULLING FOG DOES NOT HIDE IT.** Gloom and mist get away with that because you are still under open sky. Underwater it is the one thing that reads as a **renderer fault** rather than as water: the world closed to arm's length under a bright blue dome. Veiled in the shader, over everything including the sun disc.
> - **⚠⚠ MEASURED, NOT DEDUCED — ONE FRAME HELD THE SAME COLOUR TWICE.** The dome is a raw `ShaderMaterial` writing `gl_FragColor` itself, so three never appends `colorspace_fragment` and its colours reach the framebuffer **LINEAR and un-encoded**; scene fog paints the same water colour through built-in materials, which DO encode. Counted in one shot: **39,750 px of dome at (6,41,58) against 2,292 px of fogged geometry at (43,111,131)** — one logical colour, two visible colours, the wrong one covering most of the screen. Looking up at NOON was a near-black void, i.e. the brightest direction rendered as the darkest thing in frame. Veil colour now goes in **pre-encoded**.
> - **★ AND THE ENCODE GAP ITSELF IS PRE-EXISTING AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED.** It has been true since the dome shipped 08-08, which means **the sky's effective palette IS the linear one** — noon renders (82,126,184) where the `#6f9fd0` zenith would give (111,159,208). **Alex judged and approved the sky as it actually renders**, so "correcting" the encode would silently restyle a ruled look. Dry-sky pixels verified **identical** before/after the fix. His call, not a bug to fix in passing.
> - **⚠ A VACUOUS ASSERT, CAUGHT BY THE SWEEP AND NOT BY THE SUITE.** "A full wash at t=0 moves nothing" passed a mutation that **ungated the wash entirely** — `fogUnder` short-circuits at exactly `t===0` and never reaches the term under test, so the assert was proving the guard, not the gating. Rivers are uniformly `RIVER_DEPTH` **3** deep, so `tp 680 168` (bed 122, surface 125) is a known-good underwater fixture.
> - **⏭ ALEX'S EYE (three dials, one constant each):** `UNDER.fogFar` **26** trades near-object tint against how far you can see — at 5 blocks a surface is only ~18% fogged, so nearby cliffs stay their own grey. · `UNDER.water` **#2b6f83** and `UNDER.sky` **#5fb9c9** (skylight is LIFTED not cut, per canon's *"still, luminescent, and peaceful"* and the mist dust-storm lesson). · the crossing wash strength `surgePull` **0.45**.
> - **⏭ AND ONE STRUCTURAL GAP LEFT ON PURPOSE, NOW WITH A PICTURE:** the water material is `MeshLambertMaterial` with default `side: FrontSide`, so **from below the surface quads are not drawn at all** — looking up gives a flat wall of colour with no rippling ceiling to swim toward. Flipping to `DoubleSide` is a transparent-pass change with double-blend risk on the side quads and has no business riding along on a fog patch. **Its own item, not this one's.**

> Session scope call by Alex: *"the way it flows, whats in it, how the player swims through it, and lastly rinning."* Surveyed, not built. This block is the pin so the read isn't re-derived.

### Left off — what EXISTS today

- **Terrain water: built, and the most-iterated system in the voxel world.** Rivers are their own noise field with a zero-line (`RIVER_FULL 0.012` / `RIVER_EDGE 0.035` / `RIVER_DEPTH 3`). The load-bearing idea is **the water table**: a body of water has ONE level, sampled on a 96-block lattice and bilinearly blended — a property of the PLACE, not the column. Third model; the first two were "banks−1 per column" (Alex: *"there shouldn't be highs and lows in a pond"*) and clamp-to-terrain (*"a hill of blue jello"*). Land generates **around** the water; `RIVER_APPROACH 0.10` widens the shore blend ~7× so you walk down to a river instead of off a levee. Sea level 20 below datum; `basin`/`shore` are real biome labels. Guarded by `rivers.test.ts` (ponds flat · no dry ditches · no walls of water · no trunks in the channel).
- **Swimming: built 2026-08-08, oracle-tested, and it feels right.** Submerged = chest AND feet in water → the swim physics own the whole tick and **every ground verb stands down** (no slide, vault or bhop through a pond). `SWIM_SPEED 3.4` (half a run — drag country) · Space climbs · crouch dives · hands-off drifts down at `SWIM_IDLE_SINK 0.5` because *"water is patient, not a floor."* Feet-only = **treading**: normal physics, water caps the fall, and it counts as perpetual coyote ground — which is exactly what makes "swim to the bank and hop out" a plain jump.
- **Rinning: fully built — on play3d.** `engine/rinning.ts` + nodes (`small_pond` L1 / `stream` L4 / `lake` L7 in `world/resources.ts`) + strike + `rin-fx.ts` + tool crafting + a NodeEditor category.

### The four holes, in the order they hurt

1. **★★ RINNING IS ON THE WRONG SURFACE, AND THE BUILD ALREADY ADMITS IT.** On `/shimmer` — the front door — rinning exists as a **tool family and an icon only**: the rinstick ladder sits in `voxel/registry.ts`, `VoxelWorld` draws a rod-and-line glyph, and there is **nothing in the voxel world to fish**. `voxel/recipes.test.ts` documents it honestly rather than papering over it — `shimmerscale`/`clickclaw`/`glowfin_scale`/`moonkoi_scale` are unobtainable, so **the rinstick tiers cannot be crafted on the surface that ships**, and the sweep excludes rinning *with its reason*. Same shape as the alchemy-bench hole (08-18): a chain whose middle lives only on the other surface.
2. **★★ THE BUILT MINIGAME CONTRADICTS A CANON RULING — and no gate catches it.** `engine/rinning.ts` is a reaction test: line out, `!` pops at 0.9–3.0s, strike inside a 1s window or it slips. Canon refuses this **twice, with a stated in-world reason** — `game/shimmer-skilling.md` §Skill 4: *"Rinn are caught by simply waiting — there's no minigame"*; §Rinsticks: *"Rinsticks are built from rinn — kin calls to kin. That is the canon reason rinning has no minigame and rewards patience: **you are asking a rinn, not tricking one.**"* A strike window is precisely tricking one. **Same class as the EvolutionOverlay free-pick: a mechanic built on the premise canon refuses.** All 10 drift gates are lore-TABLE gates; none look at skill mechanics, which is why this shipped quiet.
3. **THE WATER IS EMPTY, AND CANON'S LARDER IS FULL.** Zero fish, zero creatures, zero nodes in voxel3d. Meanwhile `world/rinn.md` is a complete bestiary across five ocean zones, and skilling already ruled a clean 4-tier catch ladder with XP: shimmerscale/clickclaw (15) → glowfin/ribboneel (45) → moonkoi/pearlshell (120) → **crystal rinn (350)**, *"catching one feels like holding a wish."* **Nothing to invent, nothing to file** — the same "no canon gap, just build it" position slice ② of #262 was in.
4. **GOING UNDER LOOKS IDENTICAL TO STANDING IN AIR.** No breath, no drowning, no underwater view — nothing tints or fogs when submerged. Water is one transparent pass with `depthWrite` off and there is **no camera-in-water case at all**. The swim physics underneath are good; the screen never tells you you're wet, which is the biggest "this isn't water" tell in the game.

### Decisions

- **FLOW IS PROBABLY NOT A FEATURE — CHECK CANON BEFORE BUILDING CURRENT.** There is no fluid sim, no current, no downstream; water is a static fill to the table and the motion is two uv-scrolled samples of one tile (`mesh-bridge.ts`: *"one texture reads as a conveyor belt; two read as water"*). Waterfalls only happen incidentally where the zero-line crosses a bench edge. **But `shimmer-skilling.md` rules the Ather's waters are *"still, luminescent, and peaceful"*** — so "still" may be the correct answer rather than a missing system. Decide that before anyone writes a flow solver.
- **⚠ FLOW IS ALSO THE ONE PART WE CANNOT TOUCH RIGHT NOW.** River/water terrain lives in `voxel/height.ts` + `voxel/depth.ts`, and the hub window was inside `depth.ts` on worldgen when this was surveyed (08-19 afternoon). Any flow work collides head-on. Hand it to hub or wait for the lane.
- **Drowning is Rule-3 territory, not a free choice.** `CANON_GAPS.md` (08-13) binds the build: peril stays in-world, **no real cruelty on the page**, a foe that wounds the player breaks the cozy line's tone. A drowning DEATH is the world killing the keeper. A soft breath meter that pushes you to surface is probably fine; killing them is a canon call, not a tuning dial.

## 🏛️ Shimmer — **BUILDING IS THE DIFFERENTIATOR: blocks build the shell, pieces dress it** (Alex, 2026-08-06) · *Last touched 2026-08-07*

> **★★★ THE `planking` TIER WAS CUT 2026-08-22 (`543912b`), AND IT REVERSES ALEX'S OWN 08-13 RULING — READ THIS BEFORE "FIXING" IT BACK.**
> - **What created it:** Alex, 08-13, quoted in `registry.ts`: *"which get turned into planks .. actual planks not the block, not placeable, but can be used to craft materials to build with."* Planks became pure currency; `planking` became the thing you spent them on. `recipes.test.ts` pinned it as `materialForItem('goldwood_plank') === undefined`.
> - **What killed it:** Alex, 08-22, playing: *"i also noticed the craftable item planking.. its a bit out of place when each tree gives logs that can already be turned into planks."* **He was asked twice and confirmed twice**, because cutting the tier necessarily reverses the ruling — remove the intermediate and the plank is the only candidate for the wooden surface, which is exactly what 08-13 forbade. There is no version that leaves both standing.
> - **★★ `pieces.ts` HAD BEEN AGREEING WITH HIM IN SILENCE, and that grep is what settled it rather than taste.** Doorway · window · roof slope · roof cap · beam · fence · half slab **all spend RAW planks, in two species**. The build's carpentry grammar was already *spend planks*; `planking` was an orphan with two consumers (sawmill, stonecutter) that **hardcoded goldwood** — so shimmeroak could roof a house and could not wall one.
> - **Now:** three walls, one per plank species (goldwood 12 · shimmeroak 74 · dawnwood 75), starwillow absent because it yields branches. **One painter keyed off `material`** = three colour entries and no new art. Sawmill 6 planking → 12 planks, stonecutter 4 → 8. Each wall drops the plank that built it, so no farm and no loss.
> - **⚠ UNTUNED SIDE EFFECT: wood is now 2× cheaper to build in** (1 log → 4 placed, was 4 planks → 2 panels). It only widens the wood-beats-stone asymmetry `recipes.test.ts` §7 defends, so that assert passes for the right reason — but it is a real balance shift nobody dialled. §7 is the dial if timber feels too cheap against a quarry.
> - **⚠ `workshop.test.ts` PINNED THE "assembly gets no station bonus" RULE TO `planking` AS ITS EXEMPLAR**, so cutting the id took the guard down with it. One id standing in for a rule dies when the exemplar does — re-derived over every assembly row, which is what it always meant.

> **The call, in Alex's words:** *"here's the thing that sets our game apart from minecraft.. the building.. the material cost comes from blocks but the look will be more like Sims so we don't have to have blocky buildings."* Full spec: **`STRUCTURE-LAYER.md`**.
>
> **Left off:** direction recorded + spec written. Nothing implemented. Persistence and trees are still ahead of it.
>
> **Next:** ① persistence (a structure layer with no save is a demo) ② six-piece catalogue — **door, window, roof slope, roof cap, stair, beam/trim** (floors and walls are BLOCKS now, not pieces) and prove the *placement loop* ③ the save-template verb, which is the authoring tool AND the generator's input ④ then the rest of the catalogue.
>
> ### Decisions
> - **★ REVISED SAME DAY — SIMS WAS THE WRONG SCALE, AND ALEX CAUGHT IT.** He said *"the more I think about it this Sims building is going to look off"* and the reason is **foundations**: The Sims looks clean because **lots are flat**, and our terrain steps up to 3 voxels between adjacent columns. A room-scale wall on that floats, sinks, or clips — fixable only by flattening terrain before every build, which I had deferred as "not v1" and which was in fact load-bearing. **Once flattening is mandatory the differentiator has been spent on a chore.** The idea was right, the SCALE was wrong.
> - **★ THE REFERENCE IS VALHEIM, NOT THE SIMS.** Not voxel, not blocky, and its buildings read beautifully — because its pieces are grid-aligned and roughly **block-thick**, so they sit *with* terrain instead of fighting it, while still being real geometry rather than cubes.
> - **★ THE MODEL: BLOCKS BUILD THE SHELL, PIECES DRESS IT.** One stack, not two competing systems. **Blocks are structure** (walls, floors, foundations — the flat surfaces nobody looks at; they meet uneven ground the way terrain does, so **no flattening is needed at all**). **Pieces are the look** (door, window, roof slope, stair, beam, trim — exactly the elements that are *ugly as cubes*). This also settles the raw-block question BETTER than the first version: blocks are not a loophole that collapses this into Minecraft, they are **half of it** — what makes it not-Minecraft is that the elements carrying the look are designed geometry.
> - **★ GENERATION: HAND-BUILT TEMPLATES, AND THEY ARE THE SAME PIECES.** Alex asked how buildings would be generated. Yes, pre-built — that is the standard answer, not a compromise (Minecraft villages are hand-authored segments assembled under placement rules). **The payoff: the player and the generator use the SAME piece system, so anything Alex builds by hand becomes a template the generator can place.** Build one Gloview cottage in-game, save it, the world scatters variations. **The 8 canon holds, Gloview and the tutorial glade get authored BY PLAYING**, not by writing data. Variation from a small template set + rules, never from generating architecture from nothing — that is what always looks generated.
> - **★ THE TRICK THAT KEEPS IT CHEAP (unchanged by the revision): a placed piece writes OCCUPANCY into the voxel grid while rendering as a mesh.** Collision stays the cheap voxel lookup already built (`voxelSolid`, the capsule check) — Sims-looking buildings with **no second collision system**. This is the whole reason the idea is affordable.
> - **★ `InstancedMesh` PER PIECE TYPE, NON-NEGOTIABLE.** One geometry + one material, thousands of copies. A mesh-and-material per placed wall is exactly the allocation that got this page BLOCKED from WebGL on 08-06; `render-audit.test.ts` would catch it, but it should never be written.
> - **Storage is nearly free** — a placement list (id, position, rotation), not voxels. Composes directly with the ruled persistence rule (a chunk is stored only if it holds player edits).
> - **★ THIS MAKES THE CARTOON DIRECTION LOAD-BEARING, NOT DECORATIVE.** Blocky terrain beside clean architecture is jarring under realistic shading; under flat-toned, outlined, stylised shading they reconcile, because everything reads as *drawn* rather than *simulated*. The two 08-06 calls reinforce each other more than either does alone.
> - **The 3D pipeline already exists** — `world/prop-models.tsx` loads GLTF with DRACO + preload. Building pieces use that path, not the voxel one. The old `world/structures.ts` (2D tile stamps) retires with the tile world.
> - **⛔ MESHY IS STILL NOT THE ANSWER, for a different reason than flora.** Building pieces ARE a bounded, hand-designed set of dead-grey architectural props — the pre-render lane the art-medium law already scopes, so the *pipeline* is right. But modular snap-together pieces need **clean, precise, dimension-exact** geometry, and Meshy makes *organic* meshes. This is the **picaso / headless-Blender** path. (Correcting the earlier flora answer only in scope: the lane fits, the tool still does not.)
> - **Honest cost:** a piece catalogue is real art work. **Six pieces first**, prove placement/snapping/rotation/cost, then commission the rest. Do not model forty pieces against an unproven loop.
>
> **Files:** `STRUCTURE-LAYER.md` (spec) · `world/prop-models.tsx` (the GLTF path) · `voxel/registry.ts` (material costs) · `voxel3d/` (host) · ⛔ `world/structures.ts` (retires).

A hole in a bank asserts nothing. A hole in a bank that hands you a friend rules an open gap by shipping.

I sized the bank rule at *a fall of 5 across 3* because the word **bank** makes you picture a terrace face. **Measured: 0.5% of columns qualify, `dell` and `tableland` have literally ZERO, and the feature realised at one den per ~450 chunks** — rarer than the story road and unfindable. The steep-looking country is terraced by the **SLUMP layer, which is a half-block lip and not a fall at all.** Curve at probe 4: `>=2` **23.3%** · `>=3` **9.4%** · `>=4` **4.0%** · `>=5` **1.7%**. ⚠ **Any future feature gated on slope will silently realise at a fraction of its intended rate.** Retuned to probe 4 / minDrop 3.
> - **★★ carve.ts WROTE THE BRIEF A MONTH AGO AND DID NOT BUILD IT.** `surfaceClearance: 3` exists because *"an invisible single-voxel hole you drop 40 blocks down is not a cave mouth — it is a bug that reads as one. Cave entrances should be a DELIBERATE FEATURE (a widened, visible mouth), not a side effect."* A den is that feature: the only thing in the generator allowed to open ground sky-side, and it earns it by being placed against a bank instead of getting lucky with one.
> - **★★ CARVED STAGE, NOT VEGETATION, AND THE ORDER IS THE SAFETY ARGUMENT.** Post-carve ore is dealt around a den for free (`discardOnAirExposure` sees its walls like a tunnel's). In Vegetation it would be **DELETING already-placed ore** — strictly worse than the boulder bug, because a boulder on an element crystal at least leaves stone behind and a den leaves **nothing to notice**. Each element gates ten canon second forms. **An ordering cannot be forgotten by the next person who writes into that stage; a guard can.** Also before sites/waystones/hold walls, so a den can never hole a ruin or Brack's curtain. **The home plot needs no guard at all** — `plot-column.ts` is a separate generator and the continent's stages never run there.
> - **★★ THE STRICT NO-SKYLIGHT RULE ALONE MAKES NO DEN, IT MAKES A SEALED CAVITY.** `y < surface` everywhere is airtight and useless: the floor sits at the outside ground level, so one step in on this world's gentle slopes the ground has climbed into the floor row and the turf plugs the passage — every den invisible, unreachable, and green on any assert that counts cells. So the mouth cuts a bounded **notch** (throat only, within `apronSteps` of the mouth, `headroom` rows only), and the notch is asserted by **exact set membership**, not a distance tolerance.
> - **Measured, chunks per den:** meadow **1/17** · highland 1/26 · woodland 1/31 · deepwood 1/40 · crag 1/68 · dell 1/93 · marsh 1/179 · tableland 1/238 · barrens 1/240. ⚠ The dial scales **attempts**, not dens — realised rate is `denK × how banked that land is`, and uplands are banked, so highland reads high on a **0.30** dial while meadow needs **1.60**.
> - **★★ FOUR MUTATION SURVIVORS, AND EVERY ONE TAUGHT SOMETHING THE ASSERTS COULD NOT:** (1) **a real bug** — every chamber in the world warped by an *identical* pattern, a literal `0` where the den's seed belonged. Deterministic, seam-safe, 47 asserts green. **Variation is a claim, and an unstated claim is unprotected** — the fix must compare whole cell SETS, since identically-warped dens differ in COUNT anyway from where they land. Same hole existed in `boulders.ts`; play closed it (`5e8a3f2`). (2) **A warning imported from `boulders.ts` that is FALSE here** — a den's cells derive entirely from its plan, so it is alignment-independent *by construction*, not by how the warp is salted. **The warning travels, the reason does not.** Demoted to a guard; play added an applicability test at the source (`943097f`). (3) **A bound that lied by two** — the notch was keyed to the throat's step index, but each step reaches `tr` cells along its own axis, so it declared a 3-step mouth and cut a 5-step one. **A tolerance wide enough to absorb the discrepancy is how it hid.** (4) **An UNFALSIFIABLE guard** — hold pads are flat, so the bank rule refuses before the hold rule is consulted; deleting it changed nothing. Needed a synthetic bank to fail against.
> - **★ AND ONE SURVIVOR THAT SHOULD SURVIVE, NOW LABELLED AS SUCH.** The anchor's waterline check is *provably dominated* by the mouth's (the mouth is the den's lowest point), so it is a pure early-out saving eight `surfaceAt` calls on lake-bed columns. **A guard that cannot fail must say so** — unlabelled it is indistinguishable from the hold guard above, which looked identical and was a genuine hole.
> - **⚠⚠ SEVENTH INSTRUMENT FAILURE OF THE ROUND, AND IT INVERTS THE RULE.** My suite runner reported **31/43, twelve regressions** in files I never touched. The runner was wrong: this suite has **two** success markers (`✅ …` and `N passed, 0 failed`) and it grepped for one — only **21 of 103** shimmer test files use `✅`, so that harness reports 82 red on a healthy tree. **Exit code is the only contract all 103 share.** Every previous instrument failure today failed toward *"you found something"*; this one failed toward *"everything is broken"* — and that is not the safer direction. **The hazard is the direction that gets ACTED ON, and alarm gets acted on harder than discovery**: a false discovery costs an investigation, a false alarm invites a revert. One impulse from stashing a clean feature to bisect twelve phantom regressions.
> - **⚠ A MUTATION RUNNER MUST RESTORE ON A HANDLER, NOT ON ITS LAST LINE.** A 2-minute timeout killed the first sweep *mid-mutation* and left `dens.ts` with the roof check stubbed to `if (false)`; den rates read 70% high and I nearly believed them. > **🔭 `findLands` SCORES THE NEIGHBOURHOOD, NOT THE POINT (`c566199`, deployed :3200, `character.test.ts` **288**, 40 voxel files green, canon **10 CLEAN**, pushed).** The fix for the ring below, and the reason it needed one: **a nearest-search against a hard exclusion always answers on its boundary.** `interiorAt` samples two rings around a candidate and asks how much of them is still the same land, keeping an **excluded probe in the denominator**; `findLands` scores interior minus a mild distance cost over a sample taken from the front of the pool **and spread across it** — scoring the nearest N would have re-created the bug, because for a common land the nearest N are all on the same fringe. Sites went from 8-of-9 pinned at 735b to a spread of **821-2441b at 83-100% interior**.
> - **★ `examine` = 400 IS MEASURED, NOT PICKED.** At 40 the worst site scores **58%** interior; at 400 it scores **83%** — for the **same ~310ms**, because phase 1's grid scan is the cost and phase 2 disappears into it (800 is where it shows, 494ms). The budget that looked frugal was buying a fringe woodland at full price.
> - **★★ AND ONE MUTATION CAME BACK GREEN, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING.** The comment claimed the excluded-probe rule was *the mechanism* that unpins the search from the boundary. Mutating it to drop excluded probes from the denominator left **the entire suite green** — what actually does the work is scoring the neighbourhood at all, plus spreading the sample. So the comment was demoted from mechanism to **guard** and the line is now pinned directly on `interiorAt` (§15e). **A comment claiming a mechanism no test can feel is decoration**, and this file has had to delete that kind of sentence before.
> - **⚠⚠ AND THEN I CALLED A CATASTROPHIC PROD REGRESSION THAT DID NOT EXIST — the most useful thing in this block.** Verifying my own deploy, :3200 came back with terrain and trees rendering and **no ground cover anywhere**: no grass, flowers, tufts, mushrooms or rocks. Generation probed fine, the block-target reticle **named a "Grass Tuft" over apparently bare ground**, there were no console errors, and it reproduced at spawn with no teleport. Every piece of that was accurate and **none of it meant what it looked like.**
>   - **GROUND COVER AND TERRAIN ARE TWO PIPELINES.** Trees and terrain bake into the greedy CHUNK mesh and arrive with the column; grass/flowers/scatter are a **separate instanced renderer** synced off `floraDirty`, and it trails badly — spawn at 10s is `cols=24 spots=853`, at 30s `cols=117 spots=7546`. An under-settled shot therefore gives *terrain + trees + zero ground cover*, **precisely and every time**. That is not a symptom that narrows to a bug; it is the shape of a half-loaded world. The reticle survives it because the raycast reads the generated **voxel** while its instance has not synced.

> - **★★ SCATTER IS SHED, NOT GROWN, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE DESIGN.** Slice ② asked what GROWS here, right for grass because grass is a property of the ground. Nothing here is: deadfall fell off a TREE, a mushroom needs shade or damp, a stone is what bare country has instead of soil cover. So every kind is `per-land dial × the field that PRODUCED it`, never the dial alone — slice ②'s `treeK` lesson restated one layer up. Get it wrong and you ship deadfall on a bald tableland, which looks like a bug though every density in the table is defensible.
> - **★★ A FALLEN LOG IS A RUN, NOT A CELL, AND NO DENSITY ASSERT CAN TELL YOU THAT.** Per-cell placement makes a floating pebble wearing a log's name and it passes EVERY density bound while doing it — the accent-chessboard failure exactly. So a log has an anchor, a length and an axis, and the oracle is **MEAN MAX RUN**: the chessboard as a number. Measured, same density, only the mechanism differing — **per-cell control 1.06, log mechanism 3.4.** Axis-aligned because a voxel log at 30° is a staircase of single blocks, which is the pebble with extra steps. *(hub supplied the metric; it is the single most useful thing anyone handed me this session.)*
> - **★ THE TABLE LIVES IN `scatter.ts`, NOT `character.ts`** — the `trees.ts` shape (SPECIES lives with the feature, character supplies a factor), not `flora.ts`'s. `LandCharacter` is already 8 fields and the at-a-glance scan its own header argues for is what three more columns cost. **The drift risk that normally forces one table is compiler-enforced away:** both are `Record<LandId, …>`, so a tenth land fails to typecheck in BOTH places.
> - **★ BELOW THE HERB, ABOVE THE GRASS, and the ordering reaches further than looks.** The four element herbs' densities were compensated against a MEASURED land share, and **each element gates ten canon second forms through its infusion** — so anything winning their cell moves the rarity of *a third of the evolution grid* with nothing looking wrong anywhere. A stone displaces a tuft, never a Violetbloom.
> - **★ SCATTER DOES NOT ASK `TURF`, deliberately.** TURF answers *"can a plant GROW here"*; a stone and a branch LIE on whatever is beneath them and a mushroom comes up on wet mud — which is outside TURF on purpose. Gating on it would strip mushrooms from ~a third of the marsh, the second land they most belong to. ⚠ **Do not "fix" this by widening TURF; that predicate has now been reached for wrongly three times.**

The probe's kind chain ended `: FLORA.FLOWER` → unrecognised materials render as **pink blooms** (how four plants nearly shipped that way). Generating without rendering writes them into saves regardless: real in the file, invisible in play, found weeks later. Same shape as the submerged tufts.

Real geometry, plain Lambert, no alphaTest, FrontSide. A log is turned to its **run's axis and nothing else** (the shared transform's random Y turn would have broken every trunk into scattered sticks — the pebble bug rebuilt in the renderer after the field avoided it), geometry exactly one cell long so runs butt up, and **the axis comes from the neighbouring VOXEL** because the world already holds the answer.

Per-chunk starts + a scan radius, the same shape as `treeStartsAt`/`treeScanRadius` because the problem is identical. A "boulder" that fits the h+1 slot is a rock with a bigger name, which is exactly what the small end of the first size band turned out to be.
> - **★ `MAT.STONE` — NO NEW MATERIAL, NO NEW BLOCK ROW.** It already carries `ground: true`, `minTier: 1`, drops rubble. So a boulder is a **prospecting node in open country**, feeding the stone economy rather than opening a second one — the same call the two quarried-stone rows make. The "set `ground` on every new surface-reaching material" trap has nothing to catch here.
> - **★★ THE WARP HASHES ON THE OFFSET FROM THE BOULDER'S OWN CENTRE, never world position** — taken from `trees.ts`, and the one rule here that is not a preference. Both column alignments must compute an identical warp for an identical voxel or every boulder straddling a chunk boundary grows a crack.
> - **★★ AND IT MUST NOT EAT ORE — found by the hub window, and it was live.** The stage order (`depth → pre-ore → carve → post-ore → VEGETATION`) is what protects boulders FROM ore, and is precisely what exposes ore TO boulders: several batches ship `discardOnAirExposure: 0`, tier-4 `ather_crystal` deliberately so carvers slice it open. A boulder on an outcrop silently converts an **element crystal** into stone that drops rubble — and each element gates **ten canon second forms**, so a worldgen ORDERING decision would move the rarity of a third of the evolution grid with no error and no wrong pixel. `put` refuses ore, logs and leaves; `isOre` is now named in `ore.ts` so there is one definition.

I had written a non-vacuity check for exactly this and **it was vacuous in a different place**: it proved boulders write SOMEWHERE, not HERE. **THE FIX IS TO MAKE THE COLLISION A PRECONDITION, NOT A HOPE** — find a window boulders demonstrably fill, then run preservation in THAT window with the protected material in a checkerboard, so the assert cannot pass unless the collision happens.

> **🌲 SLICE ② — WHAT GROWS, AND THE SCREENSHOT THAT OVERRULED THE ORACLES (`a1fe129`, deployed :3200, canon **10 CLEAN**, `character.test.ts` **225**, suite green, 7 mutations each red on its own assert, pushed).** Trees and ground cover now read the land: nine `treeK` / species-weight / `floraK` / `flowerK` / `tallK` sets. **meadow** 0.19 trunks/col at 25% cover · **deepwood** 1.94 at 7% · **barrens** 0.06 at 10% · **dell** 33% starwillow · **marsh** 45% starwillow and 36% tall grass · **tableland/highland** 75-80% goldwood · **crag** nothing at all.
> - **★★ DENSITIES BLEND, THEY DO NOT ROLL, and that buys a strictly stronger property than the ground has.** A block is discrete so `surfaceBlockAt` rolls and the dither carries the border; a density is continuous, so it eases from 1.18 in a wood core to 0.15 in a barrens with **no border at all, not even a dithered one**. ⚠ The assert for that is that the gradient **SCALES WITH THE SAMPLE SPACING** — a step's jump is identical however finely you sample across it, a ramp's shrinks in proportion. A `|delta| < 0.35` threshold went red the moment the blend was sharpened, correctly reporting a steeper ramp and wrongly calling it a seam; the scaling formulation cannot make that mistake.
> - **★★ ONE DISTRIBUTION, READ TWO WAYS — a real dilution, not a tidy-up.** The roll sharpened and the blend did not, so a dell took its GROUND from a confident distribution and its CHARACTER from a diluted one: `tallK` 3.0 arriving on the ground as **~1.6**, a marsh reading as slightly long grass instead of reeds. Measured: dell, marsh, highland and crag **never cleared 0.62 dominance anywhere in a 240×240-chunk window** on raw weights. `landMix` is now the single vector both read — and sharpening costs the blend nothing, because `wᵏ/Σwᵏ` is smooth in w.
> - **★★ GRASS TAKES ITS COLOUR FROM THE GROUND IT GROWS IN.** Flower heads (by variant) and herbs (by material) have been tinted since they shipped; tufts and tall grass shared **one blade texture with no instance colour**, so the grass on a barrens' straw was the same green as the grass in a wet dell — which quietly undid much of what slice ① bought, since you would walk from green turf to straw turf and the thing standing ON it never changed. `PlantProbe` now returns the `ground` it had **already resolved** one line earlier. ⚠ The tints are **TARGET colours divided by BLADE_GREEN**, not multipliers: the blade texture is painted green with an additive shade, so no product of it will ever look like straw. **Topsoil's target IS BLADE_GREEN**, so its multiplier is exactly (1,1,1) and the world's most common ground is byte-identical to before — a change meant to add variety must not restyle the 45% case as a side effect.
> - **★★★ AND THE RENDER OVERRULED A GREEN SUITE, TWICE. Both are worth keeping.**
>   - **ACCENTS WERE DECIDED PER COLUMN, so they landed as ISOLATED SINGLE BLOCKS.** The marsh rendered as a **lino floor** and the barrens as a **chessboard** — 225 asserts green throughout, because every one of them measured *how much* accent and none measured *what shape*. Ground does not vary block by block; it varies in patches. Accents are now a threshold on a smooth field with a hash-frayed boundary (the same division of labour `greySurfaceAt` uses), and the oracle now measures **MEAN RUN LENGTH**: a per-block roll gives **1.28 blocks**, which is the chessboard stated as a number.

Four tree species mixed everywhere with three mild weight nudges, three flora kinds at one rate. The eight generic biomes were **names nothing read**.

Hanging the dressing off it changes the grass along a **contour line**, which is the pre-1.18 seam mistake in its third disguise and the exact thing `height.ts` is arranged to refuse. So `character.ts` asks **how much of each land is here**, as products of soft bands over the fields height already reads: continuous properties blend, discrete ones (which block, later which tree) roll a **sharpened weighted die** against a per-column hash. Interiors come out pure, borders interleave. That die is the mechanism `greySurfaceAt` already ships and Alex already judged.

What canon forbids is a **gate** (*"no gates, no locks, no keep-out"*) — so there is no frame, no lintel, no leaf and **nothing drawn on the ground**: one continuous body of wall-material with a hole in it. ⚠ *"No caves"* in `plot.ts`'s header is a different rule (`spawn-board.ts`: no ore, nothing that refills) and this drops nothing and is `hardness: Infinity`.

> **🚪 THE PASSAGE PASS — a door you can see, a ring on the map, and you arrive facing it (`29b64b5` + worker `fdec733`, deployed :3200, seam 55 / bubble 36, map-check + greg-check CLEAN, canon **10 CLEAN**, pushed).** Alex: *"the passage between the home plot and the wilds .. it needs to be more visible maybe with a marker on the map as well rn it blends too well and in the homeplot you dont even start off in front of the passage."* Three separate things, one door.

Two arrivals, two spots, and only one of them is a doorway.
> - **★★ AND THE SIGNS SHIPPED BACKWARDS FIRST.** A three.js YXZ camera looks along **(-sin yaw, 0, -cos yaw)** — its rest direction is **-Z, not +Z** — so the natural-looking `atan2(dx, dz)` aims the keeper at exactly **180°** from the thing you meant. It deployed, and the screenshot was a keeper standing at their own door looking away from it across an empty field: **the original bug, arrived at by a sign.** Same convention now drives `/look`.

> **🫧 #594 — THE CAULDRON: THE FRONT DOOR CAN BREW (`d918e65`, deployed :3200, canon **10 CLEAN**, `brew.test.ts` 49 NEW, `scripts/brew-check.mts` page harness CLEAN, pushed).** The voxel world had the alchemy chain at **both ends and nothing in the middle**: the ore seams drop all four element crystals, the trees give amber sap, and the grimoire already pours an infusion into a spirit and evolves it at 34 — with nowhere to make the bottle. The grimoire's own refusal said it out loud: *"no storm infusion in your satchel — brew one first"*, in a world with no brewing. Brewing was wired only into play3d; `engine/alchemy.ts` was shared and unreachable from here.
> - **★ IT IS A CAULDRON, AND THE WORD IS CANON'S.** `game/alchemy.md` says brewing happens in a *"shared cauldron"*, so the block takes canon's own noun rather than an invented "alchemy bench". ⚠ **Fired clay, never iron** — `design-briefs/shimmer-alchemy-vessels.md` locks the substance law for everything alchemy touches (*"No metal… hand-blown glass, fired clay, cork, wax, cord and cloth. Metal belongs to the collar and the Mint."*). A black iron pot on three legs is the default image of a cauldron and it is the one look this block may not have, so the painter actively refuses it: clay basin, stone hearth course, dark unlit brew. **Placeholder INSIDE the law — the final read is Alex's call.**
> - **★ IT GATES BREWING, AND THAT DOES NOT CONTRADICT `recipes.ts`'s "mining is the gate, not furniture".** That rule protects a verb the player already has everywhere — hand-refining is instant, free and unlimited, so a bench gating it would be *taking something away*. Brewing has never existed in this world at all: the cauldron is the verb ARRIVING, not a toll booth on a free one. Canon puts brewing in a vessel by name, and the whole gate costs 8 subsoil + 4 cut stone — dirt you already walk over. The gate a player feels is the INGREDIENTS, which is where that file says it belongs.
> - **★★ `absent` IS THE REFUSAL THIS WORLD NEEDED, AND THE PAGE HARNESS CAUGHT ITS ORDER.** The potion table is shared with play3d, which farms, fishes and shops; this world has ore, trees and a pot. So most of canon's 17 brews name an ingredient that **cannot be obtained here at all** — including all four flagship Infusions, whose element herbs are farm crops. A red `violetbloom petal 0/2` is indistinguishable from *"go and find some"*. I checked `level` first (the obvious order) and the harness proved it wrong: Infusions are visible at alchemy **7** and gated at **10**, so a keeper at 7 was told *"alchemy 10 — you are 7"* — **a promise still false at 10**, worth ~500 XP of grinding toward nothing. **A refusal that survives being fixed must be said first.**
> - **⚠ IT IS DERIVED, NEVER HAND-KEPT.** `WORLD_ITEMS` = block drops ∪ recipe outputs (the same set `/give` validates against), so **the day the herbs arrive the warning disappears by itself** and all four rows go live untouched. Measured today: the crystals and the sap are already here — **the herb is the only thing standing between this world and an evolved spirit.**
> - **★★ `doBrew` DELIBERATELY DOES NOT CALL `brewPotion`.** The engine's brew ends in `engine/inventory.addItems`, which reads the **2D game's** stack table and **discards the leftover it returns** — the exact 08-11 bug where `addItems(inv,'block_topsoil',64)` filled 24 slots and destroyed 40 in silence. A brew is four gathered ingredients and a mana cost, so losing the bottle to a full bag would be the most expensive version of that bug in the game. The run is assembled from the same pure pieces in this world's order — ask, take, drain, **`give`**, pay XP — and `room` is a refusal checked **before anything is spent** (the chest pass's rule: *a payout that fits nowhere REFUSES rather than commits*).
> - **NOT a workshop station, and asserted so.** `voxel/workshop.ts` is built on *work happening while you are away*; brewing spends the KEEPER's mana and pays the KEEPER's XP, so it can never be a standing job. Its own intent (`'brew'`), its own panel, and an oracle that fails if `MAT.CAULDRON` ever lands in `STATION_MAT`.
> - **`/brew` (owner) exists because the click cannot be driven.** Opening the panel needs a right-click, a right-click needs pointer lock, and headless Chrome will not grant one — so without a console door the panel, the refusals and the spend path could only ever be checked by hand on every future change. Same argument `/foes` makes. ⚠ **The physical right-click on a placed cauldron is therefore NOT harness-verified** — intent oracle + three lines of dispatch is all that stands behind it. **Alex's hands.**
> - **A potion stacks to 10, derived from `MAX_INFUSIONS_PER_ELEMENT` (9): one spirit's worth of one element, with a bottle spare.** The chests' rule — a magic number that SAYS something beats one that balances something.
> - **What is brewable here TODAY: 3 of 17** — Mana Draught (lv1), Shard Tonic (lv1), Crystal Elixir (lv7). ⚠ **The XP road is un-playtested:** alchemy 10 (the infusion gate) is ~58 shard tonics ≈ **174 shards + 116 bark**. Nobody has felt that. It is a dial, not a design.

> **🦋 #262 SLICE ④ — THE THRESHOLD GETS A CALL SITE, AND THE OVERLAY STOPS ASKING. ROW CLOSED (`c50452c`, deployed :3200, canon **10 CLEAN**, `evolution.test.ts` 26 new / alchemy 95 / potion-effects 83 / farming 57, full-chain page harness green, pushed).** Canon's complaint — *"the build announces 'ready to evolve!' and then nothing happens"* — was written against a line in `Shimmer3D` that said in its own words *"we just celebrate the threshold here"*. That is only correct if the answer is always available at the instant of crossing, which was true under the premise this slice deletes: the old overlay let the player PICK, so crossing always resolved. Canon sets the form by **dominant infusion**, so a spirit can cross 34 with **no lean** or with a **tie** and have no form to take yet — and under an edge rule that spirit is base **FOREVER**, because `prevStage === newStage` on every later level and no amount of pouring afterwards can fire it again. **The keeper does everything right and nothing happens.** `spirits/evolution.ts` asks *"is this spirit owed a form RIGHT NOW"*, answerable after a pour, after a fight, or on load. **Mutation-verified:** making it fire only *at* 34 reds exactly the late-infusion assert.
> - **`evolutionBlocker` returns `settled` / `too-young` / `no-infusions` / `tied`, not a boolean.** `tied` is the one a keeper would otherwise read as a bug — bar full, level there, spirit stubbornly base. The grimoire prints *"pulled two ways — no form"* instead of nothing.
> - **`evolveSpirit` writes ONLY `element`** (stage is derived from level, stats from stage, moves per element) — asserted, and idempotent so a re-render or two racing callers cannot double-apply. **`secondFormName` falls back to the species name, never a composed string:** `SECOND_FORM_NAMES` is canon's 40-cell grid, and inventing *"Storm Fox"* would put an unruled name in front of a player at the most memorable moment in the game.
> - **`addXP` no longer announces a form the spirit cannot take** — it now requires a dominant infusion. That announcement **is** the sentence canon quoted. **Awakened (67) is deliberately absent:** it needs a `branch` field `Spirit` does not have, and guessing one is accidental canon across 160 ruled forms.
> - **★★ THE OVERLAY: CHOOSE → REVEAL.** It was fully written, **mounted nowhere**, and built on the premise canon refuses — *"Choose an element for {spirit}"*, a free pick of all four. **A menu at the moment of evolution does not tune that rule, it deletes it:** the herbs, the brews and every pour become decoration for a choice made at the end anyway. `farming.ts` had already written the same lesson about blooms — letting the player pick *"contradicts the world rather than tuning it."* It also drops a bug: the grid mapped `ELEMENTS`, which included `'base'`, so the free pick offered **five** options, one of them *"evolve into no element"*.
> - **The overlay does not evolve anything** — the caller applies and persists FIRST, then shows it. A component that both decides and animates is one dismissed dialog away from a spirit announced as evolved that never was. **`sprites` is now optional:** it was written for the archived 2D tilemap game and **neither live surface loads that pipeline**, so it degrades to a lit cube in the element's colour — grimoire-tab's own call, *"the world's own visual language, needing no art to exist."*
> - **Both surfaces sweep the WHOLE PARTY** (after a fight's XP, after a spar, after a pour), not just whoever levelled. The voxel world has no overlay, so it says it plainly on the say channel — a silent form change is worse than a plain sentence. **A settled spirit is offered no more pours** on either surface: another bottle changes nothing a keeper can see.
