A keeper on `/shimmer` can pour and now evolve, but cannot **make** an infusion. An alchemy bench in the voxel world wants Alex's call.

> **🧪 #262 SLICE ③ — `addInfusion` FINALLY HAS A CALLER (`1c5faad`, deployed :3200, canon **10 CLEAN**, alchemy oracle 65 → **95**, page harness `scripts/infuse-check.mts` new, pushed).** The call that was missing. Canon named its absence as *the* reason no spirit could evolve: a second form is set at level 34 by the **dominant** infusion, `element` was written `'base'` at creation and never written again, so `dominantInfusion()` returned null forever and **all forty ruled second forms were unreachable**. Slice ① grew the herbs, ② brewed the bottles, and the middle was still missing.
> - **★★ ASK FIRST, SPEND SECOND — the whole function.** `addInfusion` refuses at the caps (11 total / 9 per element). Consuming the bottle and *then* discovering the refusal destroys a tier-2 brew — four gathered ingredients and a farming cycle — and reads as *"the button sometimes doesn't work"*. Nothing leaves the bag on any path that does not also add a point. **Mutation-verified:** moving `removeItems` above the cap checks reds exactly the two *"still in the bag"* asserts.
> - **★ TYPED REFUSALS, NOT A BARE BOOLEAN.** `none-in-bag` / `element-full` / `spirit-full` / `not-an-infusion` are four different sentences to a keeper, and a `false` that means all of them is how a panel ends up saying nothing at all.
> - **★ NO LEVEL GATE, DELIBERATELY.** Infusing is how the form is **steered**; level 34 is when the world *reads* the ledger, not when you may write to it. Gating application behind 34 would make the choice after the announcement — the same inversion slice ④ has to fix in `EvolutionOverlay`.
> - **Named `applyInfusion`, not `useInfusion`** — a `useX` free function called from an event handler inside a component is precisely what rules-of-hooks forbids.
> - **TWO SURFACES, BECAUSE THE LOOP IS SPLIT ACROSS THEM.** voxel3d's **grimoire → Yours** (canon rules the grimoire *"the first instrument for STUDYING spirits"*, and steering a form is study, not storage) shows the ledger — `n/11`, *"leaning storm"* or *"tied — no form yet"* — plus four pours. play3d's **PartyPanel** gets them too because **brewing lives there**. Pours **hide** once `element` is settled (after 34 a control that can no longer change anything is a worse lie than no control) and stay **visible-but-disabled** before then, with the count you hold.
> - **`/give` now knows `POTION_IDS`.** It validated against block drops + voxel recipe outputs only, so **no potion was conjurable** and nothing downstream of a brew could be tested by an owner at all. Caught by the page harness on its first run.
> - **`scripts/infuse-check.mts` is a PAGE test on purpose** — the oracle proves `applyInfusion` works; it cannot prove the grimoire **calls** it, that the button is reachable, or that the pour is **written**. It asserts the save afterwards, because a pour that vanishes on reload is strictly worse than a refusal.
> - **⚠⚠ THE REAL REMAINING HOLE, AND IT IS BIGGER THAN A SLICE: THE FRONT DOOR CANNOT BREW.** `engine/alchemy.ts` is wired into **play3d only**; voxel3d's crafting is `voxel/recipes.ts` (`hand`/`crafting_table`), a separate system with **no alchemy in it** — before this commit voxel3d did not import `engine/alchemy` at all. So on the surface `/shimmer` actually opens, a keeper can **pour** an infusion but cannot **make** one, and the Exchange Booth that sells the herb seeds is play3d's too. The full chain **farm → brew → pour → evolve** exists on **no single surface today**. An alchemy bench in the voxel world is its own row and wants Alex's call on where it stands and what it looks like.
> - **⏭️ SLICE ④** — the level-34 trigger + rewriting `EvolutionOverlay` from **CHOOSE** to **REVEAL** (it is fully written, mounted nowhere, and built on the free-pick premise canon refuses).

> **⛰️ THE GARDEN'S GROUND CLOSED OVER A SAVED KEEPER — FIXED 2026-08-18 (`f89bd77`, deployed :3200, canon 9 CLEAN, plot oracle 57, pushed).** Alex, this morning: *"my player is stuck in the home plot unable to move."* Real bug this time, reproduced from **his actual save** and root-caused in one pass. ⚠ Compare the 08-15 report two blocks down (*"stuck in the OLD VERSION of the home plot"*) which was a layout description — the lesson there was *ask instead of guessing*; the lesson here is that the same sentence can be literal.
> - **★★ THE CAUSE IS AN 08-16 RULING MEETING AN ABSOLUTE STORED `y`, AND THE RULING IS RIGHT.** `plotHeight` was made **additive** that day — *"the surface only ever rises as the coast moves out ... no cell that was solid becomes air"* — because canon forbids expansion dropping a keeper's build out from under them (*"a player who learns that expanding costs them their base stops expanding"*). Nobody costed the mirror case: a keeper's position is stored as an **absolute y**, so ground that rises under a saved standing spot **closes over the keeper**. His save had feet at **y97 in a column where `plotHeight` now answers 97** — one block inside his own topsoil. Collision then refuses every direction, so he could not walk, jump *or* fall. **Do not "fix" the additive rule; it is the load-bearing half.**
> - **★★ AND THE RESTORE COULD NOT HEAL IT, WHICH IS WHAT MADE IT A TRAP RATHER THAN A GLITCH.** The host applied **no clamp** to a plot position, having correctly rejected the CONTINENT's clamp (it would drag a garden position up to Wilds altitude ~130) and then concluded that meant *no clamp at all*. **Declining the wrong clamp is not the same as needing none** — the garden has its own height field. The autosave wrote the buried position straight back every few seconds, so **no reload could escape it**: the same self-perpetuating shape as the 08-15 save that stored a position without its space, and it wanted the same answer — fix it where the stale number meets the live terrain.
> - **`plotStandY` (voxel/plot.ts) + one call at the restore site.** `Math.max`, never an assignment: a keeper saved mid-jump, mid-fall or in flight is **above** their ground and must stay there — that is the half a naive "snap to the surface" fix destroys silently. Outside the island the stored y is returned **untouched on purpose**: `hasFallenOut` + the soft return already own that fall and are tested for it, and a second rescue would give one fall two owners. **No announcement** — the other rescues speak because they move you 500 blocks; this moves you one, and a message would be noise about something the keeper never saw go wrong.
> - **★ EXISTING SAVES HEAL THEMSELVES.** The lift lands before the first autosave, which writes the good y back. Verified on Alex's live browser: stored `y` went **97 → 98 on one load**, HUD 99 → 100.
> - **★ THE ORACLE IS SPLIT ON PURPOSE, AND THE SPLIT IS THE POINT.** `plot.test.ts` +8 asserts (4 mutations, each red on its own: no clamp / off-by-one / assignment instead of max / rescuing the void case too; the island-wide sweep is the assert, because a spot check passes on a function that only works where it was sampled). But a unit test **cannot prove the restore still CALLS it** — the exact gap that let a hardcoded MoveBook row ship over a working system. So `scripts/move-check.mts` (new) is a **page** test: Wilds walks, garden walks, and **Alex's save verbatim walks — 0.00 blocks before this commit, 8.2 after.**
> - **⚠ THE MID-SESSION HALF — ANSWERED BY ALEX THE SAME MORNING, AND THE ANSWER MAKES IT TRACTABLE (`e26cf8c`, doc only).** I left this as a vague worry (*"can a growing fold bury a keeper mid-session?"*); Alex: *"the home plot island should not grow on its own but instead greg should make the boundary larger."* **That is standing canon, not a new call** — he ruled it 2026-08-16 and it lives in `game/shimmer-geography.md` › *The grimoire is what Greg reads*: **the grimoire raises the CAP, the keeper's blocks fill it in**, knowing buys extent, materials build on ground already won, and **Greg reads the book**. Nothing to file. **Because growth is a DISCRETE Greg-brokered event rather than anything emergent, the burial has exactly ONE call site instead of being a continuous hazard** — wire the `plotStandY` lift in the same breath as the raise. Unreachable today (`capRadius` is a constant, the ledger is UNBUILT). ⚠ **And the build's own `capRadius` note still called that question "live" two days after it was ruled** — the handoff-sort/Faro lie-family, and the way someone eventually ships emergent growth because nothing told them not to. Corrected in place.

Both now fade **from the coast in blocks** through one `coastT`, so everything more than `keel` blocks inland is bit-identical and **expansion is additive**. ⚠ Costs the lens on a big plot (flat-bottomed disc with a rounded rim) — written down at the dial rather than rediscovered.

That is Alex's own verb: *reveals*.

> **☁️ THE FOLD'S WALL IS A PILE OF CLOUDS — SHIPPED 2026-08-16 (`fbb47dd`, jin-cc, world lane; Alex: *"im thinking like a pile of clouds"*).** The shell shipped as a near-perfect cylinder with a dead-flat lid: `wobble` 0.01 is **±5 blocks over a 3km circumference**, which is not a wobble, and every scrap of cloud character lived in `paintCloudWall`'s texture. **At 170 blocks tall a player reads the SILHOUETTE long before the tile, and the silhouette said tank.** So the fix is shape, in the pure core, and it is three numbers plus one idea.
> - **★★ THE IDEA: THE BULGE AND THE CROWN ARE THE SAME FIELD.** `lobeAt` is read once; `shellRadiusAt` bulges off it and the new `shellCapTop` crowns off it, so **a puff that pushes out also stands taller** and the eye groups them into discrete heaps. Drive the cap from its own independent noise and every assert still passes while the wall stops reading as cloud — it becomes a bumpy wall wearing an unrelated bumpy hat. That is the claim most likely to rot silently in a refactor, so it is asserted directly (see the ordering assert below).

A bulwark at reach 1.30 standing on the far side of a **one-block** wall pressed through it in precisely the same way, for precisely the same reason. **The rule belongs on pressing, not on a posture** — the oracle asserts it on the bulwark specifically, at 1.2 blocks so the wall is the only thing deciding it (a version of that assert at 4.8 would have been green because he was out of reach, the wrong-reason trap `stuck` already documents in this file).
> - **★★ THE FIX IS TWO HALVES AND THE FIRST ALONE IS A NEW BUG.** Deny the press and stop there, and a channeler behind a wall stands at its standoff pressing nothing **forever** — the encounter quietly ends, which is the same failure mode the `blocked` slide exists to prevent one line down (*"a foe that parks on the first tree reads as a failed spawn"*). So **losing the line also drops the standoff**: it closes until it can see you again, sliding along the wall as it goes, which is what makes it come *around* the wall rather than stare at it. **Cover buys a reprieve — break contact, let the guard come back — never immunity**, and canon already wants disengaging to be the answer instead of geometry being one.
> - **`sightClear()` marches an injected `opaque(x, z, t)` probe**, half a cell at a time, **endpoints excluded** (a foe with its shoulder to a wall, or a keeper in a doorway, must not blind themselves with the cell they stand in). Same shape as `blocked`: only the world knows what a wall is here, and **omitting the probe is exactly today's behaviour**, so every other caller keeps working. `t` runs 0 at the Moglin's head to 1 at the keeper's eye so the host lerps the height — **a flat height reads the hillside between two bodies on a slope as a wall, or misses one entirely.** Host probes `isSolid(voxelSolid(...))`, the same solidity collision and light use, which is why a leaf canopy covers you and a tuft does not.

Asserted by sweeping every wall offset at every distance out to 8 (the coarse-step mutation reds it with 82 misses). The only line that slips through clips a corner, which is the generous direction: it presses you when you are *barely* covered rather than sparing you when you plainly are not.

Pre-existing (walk up to one today and it holds), but this fix makes it routine. Kiting back out to standoff 7 on regaining sight would preserve the *"never closes"* identity — and would also make the posture harder to walk up to and hit, which is a feel change, not a bug fix. **Not built; Alex's call.**

Closed form verified against the simulation to within 0.2s.
> - **★★ THE FIND UNDERNEATH: MOST OF THE CLOCK IS WALKING, NOT PRESSING.** That is why re-pointing dps barely moved it — **+125% dps bought 19% off the clock** — and why `meet` turned out to own the encounter's whole shape. At 34 a patrol did not arrive, it **trickled**: three separate encounters spread over ~7s, which reads as three unrelated things wandering over, not as *"a patrol comes out to meet you"*, the line the game actually says. **34 → 22** lands them 1.5s (Thistle) to 4.2s (Vetch) apart. A mutation pins the comparison so a later pass reaches for the right dial.
> - **PRESSURE REDISTRIBUTED ALONG THE RISK AXIS, NOT RAISED — sum unchanged at 19.** The rule: *what a posture costs the keeper must be paid for by what it risks getting there.* channeler **9 → 7** (highest pressure on the safest posture — holds at standoff 7, never closes, presses for free from 8 blocks) · bulwark **6 → 9** (slowest, longest walk, arrives last, and at 6 the one who plants himself in the road was a formality) · skirmisher **4 → 6** (lands first and alone, and at 4 was a non-event for the seconds it owned the fight).
> - **RECOVERY MUST NOT COST MORE THAN THE LOSS.** calm 5 → 3, regen 9 → 15: recovery was **16.1s against a fight lost in 10-13s**, so the cheapest play was to disengage and stand in a field, and the loss was taxed twice. The real penalty is the collar staying on him and the walk back; **a refilling bar is not a penalty, it is a wait.** Now 9.7s, just under the fastest hold's 10.0s, and asserted so a later pass cannot silently invert it.
> - **Where it lands:** stand still and do nothing → thistle **10.0s** · vetch **11.0s** · brack **12.7s** (was 17.1/19.2/21.0). Walk in and then stand → ~7.3/8.1/9.6s. **Walk away → never caught, at any dial** — nothing out-runs a keeper, by the rule at the top of `collar-foes.ts`.
> - **⚠⚠ THE BACKWARDS SPINE SURVIVES THIS PASS AND NO DIAL CAN FIX IT.** Thistle 10.0 < Vetch 11.0 < Brack 12.7 — **the first hold is the hardest and the looming endgame hold is the softest**, in every scenario tested. Cause is structural: `rollPatrol` draws size (`2 + floor(roll*2)`) and composition purely from the hold's coordinates, with **no spine axis at all** — Thistle happened to roll 3 (two skirmishers = early pressure), Brack rolled 2. **The escalation axis exists everywhere else and this one roll ignores it**: `hold.half` is 10/12/14 (*"Brack looms"*) and `collar-raid.ts` tiers integrity 70/120/200. Fix is `rollPatrol` taking the hold's index and escalating size — Jin's call (team size is a build TBD, not canon), not built, next.
> - **⏭️ NEXT:** Alex plays it and calls whether losing is now reachable without being cheap · then the spine escalation above.

> **⛓️ #294 — THE SEND-BACK: LOSING THE ENCOUNTER DESTROYED IT (2026-08-16, jin-cc hub lane).** `d4c652c`, deployed :3200, canon 7 CLEAN, pushed. **⚠ The numbers in this block ("thistle 5.9s · vetch 6.3s · brack 7.7s", "recovery is 16.1s, more than twice the time it took to lose") are the ARITHMETIC FLOOR, not the clock — corrected by the 08-17 pass above.**
> - **★★★ `PlayerSave.patrolled` RECORDED THE WRONG EVENT.** Written when a patrol **SPAWNED**, read as *"this encounter is resolved"*. So being **sent back** — the losing state the whole encounter is designed around — consumed the hold as permanently as freeing everybody did, **in a save file**, with the nearest hold **1237 blocks** from the glade. Canon's penalty is *"the collar stays on him."* The build's was *"and you may never go back."* The feature could be playtested **once per world.**
> - **★ THE DOC ARGUED FOR IT AND COVERED HALF:** *"must not re-roll a fight the keeper declined any more than it should undo one they won."* The second clause is canon; the first is a save-scum worry about a fight with **no reward to farm**. One clause was load-bearing, both were enforced with one flag.
> - **NOW: freeing is permanent, failing is not.** A **count of who was freed** per hold; the patrol is a **PREFIX of its own deterministic roll** (same Moglins, same spots, minus the ones you let go, at full collar). Count reaches patrol size → that hold is done forever.
> - **★★ THE PREFIX SKIP MUST CONSUME ITS ROLLS.** Skip without drawing and the **survivor inherits the freed one's posture and spot** — right count, wrong fight. **Mutation-verified: the count assert stays GREEN through it; only the identity assert catches it.** `rollPatrol` pulled pure + oracled (47 → 66) because the old rule could only be checked by walking 1237 blocks and losing on purpose.
> - **★★ THE NUMBERS, MEASURED. *"A full guard is ~12s"* was the REGEN clock, not the drain.** Real: **thistle 5.9s · vetch 6.3s · brack 7.7s** — and **difficulty runs BACKWARDS along the spine**, the first hold being the hardest. Recovery is 16.1s, more than twice the time it took to lose.
> - **`/press` (owner-only): the eight guesses live at runtime**, printing seconds-to-send-back rather than `dps` (unreadable as feel — three of them stack). Not persisted, on purpose: what a session decides is written back into the file by hand so the shipped numbers stay reviewable.
> - **Guard restored on waking at the glade** (`wake` dial). ⚠ Two bugs found in passing: despawn leaked the **spirit + leash** meshes (only the Moglin was removed), and the **channeler presses through walls** (reach 8, no occlusion test — flagged, not fixed).

> **⚔️ #294 IS PLAYABLE — BOTH COLLAR RULINGS BUILT (2026-08-16, jin-cc hub lane).** `867864b` `037560f` `9d7c275`, deployed :3200, canon 7 CLEAN. Two `[OPEN]` gaps filed and both ruled the same evening (`c2376b1` `61e19c5` `c772036`).
> - **★★ THE FOE MODEL WAS WRONG AND THE FILE'S OWN HEADER KNEW.** A Moglin **never wears the collar** — its power is *spirit-only* and every canon instance has him **holding the leash**. The encounter is a Moglin WITH a collared spirit: you defeat the SPIRIT, and he deflates because his bravery was **borrowed**. `collar-foes.ts` has said *"the posture belongs to the spirit, not the Moglin"* since the day it was written; only the bar was on the wrong body. Root cause was an ambiguous compound — **`collar-Moglin` = a Moglin OF the collar** — now pinned in canon. **When a file's prose and its types disagree, the prose is often the older and truer one.**
> - **★ `integrity` IS THE COLLAR'S GRIP, NEVER THE SPIRIT'S HEALTH** — pinned on `strike()` with a rename warning. That single sentence is what makes a *cutting projectile* tonally safe on a cozy line: breaking a grip is dispossession, *"no wound, no death"*, and the freed spirit walks away **whole**. ⚠ The moment that number means injury, a dart stops being allowed and the whole ruling gets re-fought.
> - **THE FOUR CUTTING PROJECTILES OPEN A COLLAR** (ice-dart · gale-cutter · pressure-lance · tidal-arms) — not a loophole: the collar is an **object**, the contested party is **not a body**, and the body in the scene is the **Moglin's**, which is what the guard protects. **11+ of 19 runes viable, up from 4.**
> - **THREE TELLS, EACH CATCHING WHAT THE ONE BEFORE CLEARS.** ① Rule-3 cruelty — ⚠ the test is what a move **RENDERS**, not what its mechanism is made of (*"stone, water, wind and light are not a licence; they're just what the cruelty is made of"*). ② Thematic control — *"a move that takes someone's choice cannot be the thing that gives a choice back"*, and it catches **gentle** moves. ③ **★ CAN HE STILL LEAVE?** — the win is dispossession and *"he can go"*; a foe sealed on all six faces *"has not been sent back, he has been put somewhere"*. **Containment leaves a person present in the world; a tomb removes them from it.** Each refusal says its own line in-world — one flat "that didn't work" teaches nothing.
> - **★★ AND THE ANTI-ROT RULE IS THE PIECE THAT PAID FASTEST: the principle is canon, the CLASSIFICATION TRAVELS WITH THE MOVE, and unclassified is REFUSED.** A field where the move is authored + `answerCollar` defaulting to refuse + an oracle that reds on any unclassified castable move. **It caught three moves ninety seconds after it existed** (`flash-freeze`, `pillar-tomb`, `living-fortress`) — a hand-built table that had decayed *before it shipped*. Same fail-closed shape as `WILDS_SWALLOW_EXEMPT` and `focus_active`.
> - **⛔ A heal or a launch never opens a collar.** Canon's verb is *defeating*; a move that never enters the contest cannot win it. They stay legitimate parts of winning.
> - **★ RATIFIED AS CANON, AND IT GENERALISES: WHEN IT IS A JUDGMENT CALL, REFUSE.** *A wrongly-refused move is a build note; a wrongly-cleared one is a cruelty shipped inside the cozy line.* The costs are not symmetric, so doubt resolves one way.
> - **⏭️ NEXT:** Alex playtests the feel (3 postures, ~12s guard, the send-back — all first guesses) · whether Still-Breath earns an efficiency bonus · collared bodies are blockouts and want a design brief.

> **⚔️ #294 REGION FOES — SLICE 1 IS IN AND PLAYABLE, AND THE PAYOFF IS BLOCKED ON A CONTENT DECISION (2026-08-16, jin-cc, hub lane).** `93c5e1d` `a79e248` `51f4613`, deployed :3200.
> - **THE NOTE SAID "ONLY THE WIRING IS LEFT" AND THAT WAS WRONG BY ONE MODULE.** The four engine halves knew what a foe IS and what freeing one DOES; nothing could move one. `stepFoe` (pure, intent-returning) was the gap — same shape as `bubbleSwallows` that morning: done, green, called by nobody. **Grep for the caller before believing "wired".**
> - **WHAT SHIPPED:** patrols keyed to the three story holds (Hollows are weather, a collared Moglin was SENT and has an address), once per hold per session (a respawning patrol turns freeing someone into farming, and canon spends that once), deterministic from the hold's own coordinates. Pressure, never damage — Rule 3 in code; guard broken is **dispossession**, sent back to the glade with the collar still on him. Guard recovers only OUT of contact, so disengaging is the answer canon already wants.
> - **★★ `shots.frequency` IS THE MECHANIC.** A cast bolt and a gun round shared a pool since the port — right for a Hollow, which either disperses. A collared Moglin splits them: lead is absorbed, opens nothing, and the world says *"it is a rune he needs, not a bullet"*. **That one field is why "runes ARE the combat" is a mechanic and not a claim.**
> - **★★ THE DECISION ALEX OWES: ONLY 4 OF 19 BIRTH RUNES CAN FREE ANYONE TODAY.** A collar opens to a PROJECTILE, and only **breeze (gale-cutter) · freeze (ice-dart) · hydro (pressure-lance) · fluid (tidal-arms)** start with one. Eight runes have no castable starter at all (manalic, enchant, lightning, tempest, gem, magma, dust, mist, vapor); seven start with something that is not a projectile (barrier=stance, star=field, life=restore, static=surge, illuminate/metalergy=status, stone=terrain). `scroll-market.ts` already documents the underlying gap and refuses to invent moves. **The open question is canon's, not balance: canon's own named answer is Still-Breath — *"honest calm, no harm"* — which is not a dart at all. Does a collar open to any frequency that reaches it (a status, a field), or only to specific moves? A Firewall freeing a person by burning them reads wrong.** Until that is ruled, 15 of 19 keepers meet a patrol they cannot answer.
> - **`/foes` (owner-only, full) — the instrument, and it paid for itself twice.** The encounter is otherwise unverifiable: by the time a patrol closes, everyone is standing ON the keeper and below the frame. It immediately caught **(a) the patrols not moving at all** — the walk probe asked `columnHeight`, but a hold RAISES A PAD over it, so the probe sampled a cell inside the ground and every step read as blocked (*the `/goto garden` bug wearing a different hat, same day*); and **(b) a knife-edge hitbox** — one sphere at body centre, eye 0.65 above it, radius 0.71, connecting by six hundredths of a block. Bodies are capsules now, `FOE_HEIGHT` matched to the blockout meshes.
> - **★ AND THE LESSON THAT COST THE MOST: A RULE THAT CAN ONLY BE TESTED BY HITTING SOMETHING IS A RULE NOBODY WILL TEST.** Five browser runs "disproving" the collar mechanic were all my own aim — misses of 1.4 to 16.8 blocks against a 0.71 radius, including a pitch command that silently undid a 90° turn because drei reads `movementX` as a delta from the last cursor x. `answerCollar` now lives in the pure module with an oracle and two mutations red. **The harness says what it cannot answer instead of failing loudly about it** — whether a bolt aimed BY EYE connects is a playtest question and always was.
> - **⏭️ NEXT:** the ruling above · Alex plays it (three postures, ~12s guard, the send-back — every number is a first guess of mine) · bodies are blockouts by the art-medium law and want a design brief before they get a look.

> **🔒 FLY IS KEEPER-OF-THE-REALM ONLY, 2026-08-16 (`36de6d8`, Alex: *"id rather not give players the ability to fly around"*).** It was always a debug convenience wearing a player key, and it is the one verb that can put a keeper somewhere the world does not exist — the shell caps at y190 in a 256-block world, so flying over the wall drops you into the 1000-block hole. **This removes that hazard today without pre-empting the interior decision below.** Gated in TWO places deliberately: the `V` binding decides whether fly can be turned ON, the frame loop decides whether it is IN EFFECT — so the ability is bound to the PERMISSION, not to a press that happened while the permission was held (a lapsed cookie puts the keeper back on their feet next frame). HUD stops listing the key for non-owners: a hint that does nothing reads as a broken game, not a locked door. ⚠ **The owner bit crosses into `World` as a REF, never the prop's value** — `isOwner` arrives from an async fetch and the key listener is bound once at mount, so a captured boolean reads `false` forever, for the owner too (the same trap the Q-throw binding documents). `void-check.mts` §3 covers both sides, and measures **"are they still up after letting go"** rather than climb rate: this box runs SwiftShader at a few fps with `dt` clamped to 0.05, so a working fly climbs 4 blocks where the speed implies 50 — a rate threshold would be a threshold on the frame rate. Gravity is the frame-rate-independent difference. **Fly also quietly answered questions the game is meant to ask** (how far, how long the walk, is the climb worth it), so this is a design win as well as a safety one.

> **✅ ALL FOUR VOID FIXES SHIPPED 2026-08-16 (jin-cc, hub lane) — the diagnosis below is now closed.** `/goto garden` routes to the fold's DOOR instead of its hollow centre, and the settle gate is structurally incapable of holding physics forever. Verified in the real page, not read off the source: `/goto garden` lands at (-117, 129, -499) on solid ground and the world settles; `/tp 0 0` — straight into the void — announces *"there is no ground inside your own fold"* and puts the keeper back at the glade inside two seconds. Harness: `scripts/void-check.mts` (new, committed).
> - **① `/goto <zone>` ASKS THE GUARD, IT DOES NOT SPECIAL-CASE `garden`.** `bubbleSwallows` fed the real anchor IS the question "is this centre standable", so any future anchor swallowed by any future fold routes to a door rather than shipping the same hang again. New pure helper `passageApproach()` (bubble.ts) derives the landing from the door's own bearing: shell radius + thickness + `APPROACH_STANDOFF` (10). ⚠ The standoff must clear the CROSSING TRIGGER, not just the wall — at 1-2 blocks the keeper is carried straight through the door they were brought to look at.
> - **② THE SETTLE GATE CAN NO LONGER WAIT FOREVER, AND IT HAS TWO WAYS OUT.** (a) GEOMETRY, known with nothing streamed: inside the shell there is no ground at any altitude, so waiting is a promise that cannot be kept → rescue immediately. (b) A patience budget (`SETTLE_PATIENCE` 6s) that only runs ONCE the player's own column has arrived — while it is still streaming, waiting is exactly right. ⚠ Counted in CLAMPED FRAME TIME, not wall clock: a backgrounded tab has its rAF throttled to a crawl, and a wall-clock budget would fire on a healthy stream — the exact confusion that got a real bug retracted as "throttling" on 08-15. **One rescue, then release** — if home itself will not settle, hopping the keeper forever is the same disease with more steps, and visibly falling can at least be reported.
> - **★★ AND THE FIX'S OWN BUG, CAUGHT BY THE HARNESS AND NOT BY READING IT: A COORDINATE THAT HAS NOT BEEN SET YET IS NOT A COORDINATE.** The first version asked the CAMERA where the keeper was. R3F's camera defaults to `[0, 0, 5]` — the world origin, dead centre of the fold — so the void test fired on frame one of EVERY boot, spent the single rescue before the player had moved, and told someone standing in the glade there was no ground inside their own fold. The next real void then took the second branch and released the gate into a free fall. Both tests now ask `loco` (the walker, constructed AT the spawn point). Same family as the save that stored a position without its space: the numbers were always there and never meant a thing.
> - **③④ `bubbleSwallows` GETS THE REGISTRY AND A LIVE CALLER.** Third param `exempt`, and `WILDS_SWALLOW_EXEMPT = ['garden']` is DECLARED in column.ts with its reason (the bubble IS the garden's outside). Its first live caller is `/goto` above. ⚠ **The routing call passes NO exemption on purpose** — the list answers *"is this a bug"*, and garden is on it; it is still not somewhere a keeper can stand. Pass the list there and the one anchor that needs the routing is the one that would not get it. `bubble-wiring.test.ts` §7 now asserts against the real `ZONE_ANCHORS` (garden is the only thing swallowed, and its column really does have 0 solid cells); §8 asserts the approach is on ground, outside the wall, clear of the trigger and on the door's bearing. The wiring test's own hand-typed `!== 'garden'` filter now reads the exemption list. 38 asserts green, canon 7 CLEAN.
> - **⚠⚠ SEPARATE FIND, AND IT INVALIDATES OLD ARTEFACTS: `WORLD_GOTO` IN `scripts/world-shot.mts` HAS NEVER TELEPORTED ANYTHING.** `/goto <zone>`'s teleport half is owner-gated and a headless profile carries no owner cookie, so every run typed the command, got a polite bearing back, and photographed **the glade** — the precise failure that flag's own header says it exists to prevent. Nothing errored; the filename said `twilight-thicket`. **Any zone shot taken before 2026-08-16 is a picture of the glade, and any perf number read off one is a glade number** (measured after the fix: thicket 23 draws / 39k tris vs glade 55 / 177k). Fixed by visiting `/owner?key=$OWNER_KEY` first, and it now EXITS rather than quietly hand back the wrong place. ★ **A COMMAND THAT ANSWERS IS NOT A COMMAND THAT RAN** — third time in two days.
> - **⏭️ STILL OPEN:** the interior void itself needs a decision (floor / ceiling above y190 / leave it as the honest consequence of a fold being elsewhere) — `V` fly still lets a keeper over a y190 shell into a 1000-block-wide hole, and the y<-20 spawn backstop is what catches them.

> **🔎 THE "/tp STREAM STALL" IS DIAGNOSED AND IT IS NOT A STREAM BUG — it is `/goto garden` walking into the fold's interior (2026-08-16, jin-cc, world lane; DIAGNOSIS ONLY, no code changed).** Carried as *undiagnosed* since 08-15, where it was blocking the only cheap route to the seam. Proven with a throwaway probe against the real generator, not read off the source.
> - **★ THE MECHANISM.** The `garden` ZONE_ANCHOR sits at **(0,0)** — the exact centre of `WILDS_BUBBLE` (cx 0, cz 0, r 500). The bubble generates its interior as **AIR for the full 256-block height on purpose** (*"unreachable by construction, so nothing is spent on it"*); measured **solid-cells-in-column = 0**. `/goto` hands `tp` a landing computed from `columnHeight` — the **CONTINENT** rule, which knows nothing about the bubble — so you arrive at y134 in a column with no ground anywhere. The settle gate probes `py - 3`, gets AIR, and **returns early every frame forever**. All 7 other anchors settle; garden is the only one, and `/goto` is listed, tab-completable and owner-gated.
> - **★★ A SLOW GENERATOR AND AN UNGENERABLE DESTINATION PRINT THE IDENTICAL HUD LINE.** `N columns · generating…` is why this read as a streaming failure for a day, and it is the second time this exact string has misnamed its own cause (see `bubbleMaterialAt`'s header for the first, which genuinely *was* slow generation). **The HUD asserts a cause it never checked.**
> - **★★ ROOT CAUSE IS ONE LEVEL UP, AND IT IS THE BETTER FIND: `bubbleSwallows` IS CORRECT AND IS FED THE WRONG INPUT.** `bubble.test.ts` asserts *"the shipped bubble swallows nothing"* against a hand-written 3-item `STORY_LANDMARKS` **literal** that omits the garden anchor. Feed the same guard the real `ZONE_ANCHORS` registry and it returns **`[{id:'garden', dist:0}]`**. The assert's own comment calls it *"the thing that will actually protect the world"* — it does not, because it checks a literal instead of the registry. Same family as the handoff-sort and Faro lies: **the test asserted a scope it never checked.** `bubbleSwallows` also has **no live caller** — test-only.
> - **⚠ GARDEN@0 IS INTENDED** (the bubble *is* the garden's outside) — but it must be a **DECLARED exception**, not an accidental omission from a literal. The omission is precisely what let `/goto garden` ship as a hang.
> - **⏭️ NEXT (fixes 1+2 land in `voxel3d/VoxelWorld.tsx` = HUB's file, so they are not the world lane's to make):** **(1)** `/goto garden` must not tp into the void — route it to a **passage approach** on real ground outside the wall, which is also the cheap route to the seam. **(2)** the settle gate must be **incapable of waiting forever** — any groundless destination hangs it; bail with a true message. **(3)** feed `bubbleSwallows` the real `ZONE_ANCHORS` with garden as a declared exception *(world/voxel lane, safe to take)*. **(4)** give `bubbleSwallows` a live caller.

> **✨ THE SEAM HAS A LOOK — the keeper's front door is a PARTING, not a gate (2026-08-15, jin-cc, sprites lane; `deffe14`, approved by Alex).** The passages layer shipped 08-15 with the seam's visual flagged as owed and Alex's to call. Canon settles the ownership in the same breath it describes the thing: *"a soft seam in the cloud, a shimmer in the air, ground that simply continues. No gates, no locks, no keep-out"* — and *"How the seam **renders**… = Jin's build."* `bubbleMaterialAt` defers to it in so many words: *"What the seam LOOKS like is a render question."*
> - **★ THREE CANON CLAUSES, THREE KILLED FIRST DRAFTS.** *"ground that simply continues"* ⇒ **nothing is drawn on the ground** — no pad, no ring, no glowing doorstep. *"no gates"* ⇒ no frame, no arch, and **no visible rectangle**: a 10×7 lit slab IS the doorway silhouette canon calls the misreading, so the quad is a CANVAS and the alpha falls to zero at all four edges. *"a soft seam"* ⇒ **a parting, not a lamp**: the wall behind is pale pressed cloud and a bright additive glow on pale washes into a smear, so it reads as a narrow cool-dark slit (seeing INTO the fold) with two bright breathing lips. That gives the one thing a glow cannot — depth, which is the claim the mechanic makes.
> - **★ IT WIDENS AS THE KEEPER COMES TO IT**, which is canon's other half (*"to any other hand, the fold lies flat… there is no door there for you"*) doing double duty as the honest tell that the crossing is about to fire. At 20m it is a hairline you could take for a crack in the cloud; at 3m it is open. A guest gets `uNear` pinned at 0 and sees flat wall, with no other change to the file.
> - **⚠⚠ THE HONESTY RULE IS THE ONLY THING HERE THAT CAN SHIP A BUG: the drawn seam must sit strictly inside what `inPassageVolume` accepts.** A shimmer one block wider than the trigger is a keeper walking into their own front door and having nothing happen — no throw, no log, nothing to distinguish it from a broken save. Asserted against the REAL predicate on six seeds, never a copy of its numbers.
> - **★★ AND THAT ASSERT KILLED THE FLAT QUAD — it failed on 2 of 6 seeds, by more than a block.** Two independent causes: the shell's radius **wobbles further across the doorway** than the trigger's one-block outer margin allows (no flat placement is inside the band at both ends on every seed), and **the ground under the door is not level** (a flat-bottomed quad buries one end and floats the other — and a floating seam reads exactly like the hole in the wall canon forbids, arrived at by accident). **A margin cannot fix a shape error; it only picks which seeds it fails on.** Now a curved terrain-following ribbon placed rib-by-rib against its own column's radius and ground, so the rule holds **by construction**.
> - **★★ LOOKING AT IT CAUGHT WHAT READING IT COULD NOT.** First shader rendered as a **pale fog smear** — no crease, no depth, no door. Cause: the bright lips' Gaussian was still at **0.67 in the middle of the seam**, so they painted over the dark parting they existed to flank. It reads perfectly fine in the source. Same lesson the masonry palette learned in July: **a procedural pattern must be checked against the pixels it produces.**
> - **★ `cfg` IS A REQUIRED ARGUMENT, NO DEFAULT.** `DEFAULT_BUBBLE` puts the door at bearing 0; the live `WILDS_BUBBLE` aims it at the glade. A defaulted parameter lets a call site draw the keeper's front door **on the far side of a 3km wall** by saying nothing at all, visible only by walking a shell that is featureless in both directions. **Third time this repo has ruled that shape** (`runMs` → `milledYield` → `Impair`). Assert §7 proves the two configs answer >100 blocks apart and that the default's doorway is plain wall in the shipped world.
> - **★ THE TWO SIDES ARE DIFFERENT SIZES ON PURPOSE.** The Wilds door is an arc and its trigger accepts ~6 blocks either side of the bearing; the plot's threshold opens the waymark panel within **1.6 blocks of one spot**. Same shader, same look, sizes set by their own triggers — drawing them alike would make one of them lie. The plot's yaw-billboards (a fold's opening is a POINT with no surface to be parallel to, and a fixed quad vanishing edge-on would lose the keeper their only way out); the Wilds' is fixed, because there the wall has a face.
> - **`dev/seam` preview page** mounts the shipped pass rather than re-deriving it (`icon-sheet.mts`'s rule: a preview that re-derives can be correct while the game is wrong). `?space=&dist=&frozen=1` so a look is reproducible and citable instead of "drag the slider until it looks like it did".
> - 55 asserts, **seven mutations red**, render-audit 78/78, tsc at the 13 pre-existing. ⚠ The preview's pale backdrop is a **stand-in** for pressed cloud — judge contrast there, judge the seam in-world.

> **☁️ THE FOLD STANDS IN THE WILDS — the shell is generated, and the door faces the player (2026-08-15, jin-cc, hub lane; `a112895` + `d0a04a1`, deployed :3200).** Alex: *"the cloud bubble in the wilds that has a passage entrance to the home plot so I can finally check it out."* It had shipped 08-15 as pure geometry with a 25-assert oracle — **and then nothing called it.** Two independent reasons it was unreachable, either one sufficient.
> - **★★ THE SHELL DID NOT EXIST. `bubbleMaterialAt` was imported by NOBODY.** `bubble.test.ts` proved the geometry closed and flood-proof the entire time, which is exactly how this survived: **a pure-core oracle is defined not to see its own wiring.** The crossing trigger was firing in open countryside with no wall in sight. New `bubble-wiring.test.ts` (31 asserts) exists specifically to cover that blind spot — it asserts against the REAL generator and the REAL save baseline, not against the geometry.
> - **★ WIRED INTO `generatedAt`, NOT THE TERRAIN STAGE, and the placement is the point.** `generatedAt` is the ONE definition of *what the generator would have put here*: the terrain stage writes it and `recordEdit` diffs against it. One level lower and every wall voxel disagrees with the save baseline — the 79.3%-phantom-edit trap the plot lane caught, one space over. Asserted: 0/28k cells disagree on a shell column.
> - **★ RE-ASSERTED AFTER THE FIVE LATER STAGES, and it costs the save nothing.** None of carve/ore/trees/sites/waystones has heard of a bubble. **The carver is the one that matters** — a cave through the cloud-wall is a hole, a hole is the silhouette canon names as the misreading, and behind it is 500 blocks of ungenerated nothing. Free because `bare` (the post-terrain snapshot) already holds the bubble, so restoring those cells matches what the diff already expects.
> - **★★ THE DOOR FACED NOWHERE.** `passageBearing: 0`, while bubble.ts's own header says *"a single opening in a 6.3km circumference is undiscoverable by exploration, so the build must put the player's arrival AT it. Nothing here picks that spot."* Nothing did. It is now **DERIVED from the glade** (so it follows spawn if spawn moves): the door lands **157 blocks due SOUTH of where the keeper wakes up**, wall standing **69 blocks** above that ground. `/tp -114 -487`.
> - **★ ONE LIVE CONFIG, `WILDS_BUBBLE`** (column.ts), read by the generator AND the host. The default's placeholder `wall: 1` would have built the fold out of stone, and its bearing would have put the trigger and the doorway in two different places.
> - **★★ THE PERF BUG I SHIPPED AND THEN CAUGHT — worth more than the feature.** `bubbleMaterialAt` called `shellRadiusAt` (a 3-octave fbm) **twice per voxel**, and it is called **once per voxel by the whole world's generator** — 65,536 calls per column, every column anyone walks to. So every voxel in the Wilds, ten thousand blocks away, paid two noise evaluations to be told it was nowhere near a bubble. **Self-concealing at the worst moment: the columns nearest a keeper standing AT the wall are the shell's own, so the slowest columns in the world are the ones the player is waiting on.** The settle gate holds physics until there is ground, so the symptom was not a frame dip — it was hanging in the air over an ungenerated world with the HUD reading "generating…" forever. **A slow generator does not look slow, it looks broken.** Fix: one hypot against the widest the shell can reach BEFORE any noise; one `shellRadiusAt` instead of two; the re-assert asks per (x,z) not per voxel. Shell column 57ms vs 38-60ms for ordinary terrain; the fold's interior is now the cheapest column in the world at 22ms.
> - **GENERATOR_VERSION 17 → 18** — the largest terrain change the world has taken: it does not nudge a surface, it replaces a region.
> - **⚠ TWO OTHER SUITES SAMPLED INSIDE THE NEW FOOTPRINT — moved, not silenced.** `plants.test.ts` sampled the **`garden` anchor**, which canon says **IS the Home Plot** — now its own coordinate space, so that ground is gone by design; it samples the glade instead. `trees.test.ts` sampled [384,192] (429 out); [-576,384] replaces it (forestness 1.00, 106 wood on the seam).
> - **⚠ THE INTERIOR IS A TRUE VOID — measured, topmost solid = -1.** No ground at any y across ~785k columns. Unreachable by construction *unless you fly*: the shell caps at y190 and the world is 256 tall, so **V-fly over the top drops you into a 1000-block-wide bottomless hole.** Pre-existing consequence of the world lane's design, not introduced here, but it is now reachable and Alex will find it.
> - **⚠ NOT VERIFIED LIVE: the crossing actually firing.** The wall is confirmed standing in-game (screenshots) and the trigger is proven by oracle at a standable spot (real ground at y122, `inPassageVolume` true). But every attempt to stand there came via `/tp`, and a teleport into that region left the player unsettled with the stream stalling at 9 columns. Not diagnosed — **walking there normally streams progressively and is the untested-but-expected path.**
> - **★★ ALEX'S FIRST WALK THROUGH BROKE, AND IT WAS THREE BUGS WEARING ONE SYMPTOM** (`d52af91` `0287a1d` `2b7160c`). *"Floating in the void and all that's visible is the grass and flowers."* The plot was fine throughout. Each was something that had to CROSS with the keeper and didn't: **(1) the flora** — `enterSpace` clears eleven voxel caches and flora wasn't one, so the Wilds' tufts hung in the garden's sky (⚠ marking it dirty is not enough — plot column "0,0" wears the same key as Wilds "0,0", so `sync`'s prune sees the stale entry as live; needed `invalidateAll`). **(2) the camera** — the body moved to the threshold and the eye stayed in the Wilds, and since **the settle gate reads the camera**, it probed 35 blocks up in open sky, found air and held physics forever, with the early `return` preventing any recovery. Affected `/space` too, so **the plot had never once been enterable from a standing start.** **(3) the space itself** — `PlayerSave` stored x/y/z and not which world they were in, so an autosave in the garden reloaded into the Wilds at those numbers: 12 blocks from the origin, inside the shell, in the void. **Self-sustaining** — the autosave writes it back, so reloading never escapes. ⚠ **I armed that one**: before the fold, the origin held ordinary terrain and the same bug landed you safely mid-map. **Making a region void makes every latent wrong-coordinates bug that points there fatal.** Rescue added for saves already written (geometric test, not a ground probe — no column is loaded at restore time).

> **🧰 CHESTS: TWO BAGFULS, A FOLD THAT HOLDS ONLY SO MANY, AND BENCHES THAT REACH INTO THEM (2026-08-15, jin-cc, hub lane; `ec67721`, deployed :3200).** Alex's three-part spec from the geometry session's Next list — *"10 per plot + station-attached"*, with the slot count called out as a trap.
> - **Left off:** all three parts shipped and live. Chest oracle 94 green, plot oracle 47 green, canon gate 7 CLEAN, prod 200, world boots clean in a browser.
> - **★ 48 SLOTS, AND THE REASON IS A SENTENCE, NOT A NUMBER.** It was 24 because *"a chest holds a bagful"* is something a player can feel. **36 would have bought half a row and spent the only phrase the number had**; 48 doubles it and the sentence survives — two bagfuls. `CHEST_BAGFULS` is derived from the grid so the prose in the panel cannot drift from it. Any future change to this number has to answer the same question: *what does the new number SAY?*
> - **★ THE MIGRATION NEVER TRUNCATES.** Every chest on disk is 24 long. `adoptChest` pads on load — a raw hand-off would give the panel a grid whose back three rows are `undefined`, indistinguishable from a slot until something writes to it. And if the count ever goes DOWN it **compacts forward instead of slicing**: a config change must not be able to delete a keeper's stack. Junk off disk is discarded rather than trusted (a console can write that store).
> - **★ TEN CHESTS PER FOLD, RIDING `capRadius`** — one per three blocks: 10 at the starting cap, 24 fully grown. **Storage is not a second reward track to balance; it is the same number that decides how far you may build**, so whatever raises your ground raises what you can keep on it, in one motion with nothing to keep in sync. Agnostic about what raises it (same note `capRadius` itself carries), so it survives whichever way the live ground-vs-resources gap is ruled.
> - **★★ THE CENSUS IS A DISK SCAN, NOT A LEDGER — the design call of the session.** At the endgame cap **the island is wider than the load ring**, so counting resident columns would hand out free chests to anyone who walked to the far side of their own garden. The obvious fix (a stored list of chest positions) is a **second source of truth about something the world already knows**, and it drifts the first time a chest leaves by a path nobody hooked. There is no need for one: **a chest is never generated, so every chest that exists IS an edit, and the edits are already on disk.** Counted once at `enterSpace` — the one instant nothing is dirty and no plot column is resident — then kept by ±1 at `setVoxel`, the single funnel every world write goes through. ⚠ The scan's result is **ADDED, not assigned**, or a placement racing it gets erased and the keeper is one over the cap forever.
> - **★ STATION-ATTACHED = THE FOUR HORIZONTAL NEIGHBOURS, NEVER ABOVE OR BELOW.** A chest on a shelf or in the floor is not a thing anyone builds on purpose, and it would attach **silently** — a bench eating out of storage you never meant to connect. Beside it is the arrangement you would build anyway, and it is legible across the garden: *the workshop is the bench and the chests you set around it.*
> - **★ BAG FIRST, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.** `have`, the spend, and the payout all read the bag before the chests: what is in your hand is what you meant to use, so a keeper who picked up eight logs to mill does not watch the bench drain the stack he was saving. **The payout half is the one that matters** — a workshop's real failure was never "not enough material", it was coming back to a finished job with a full bag and having the station sit on it. ⚠ A payout that fits **nowhere** now REFUSES rather than committing: `collect` has already cleared those runs, so committing would delete the goods and the job at once.
> - **Decisions:** *(a)* the cap is **plot-only** — the Wilds is uncapped, because the scarcity that makes a bigger fold worth having is the fold's. *(b)* attached chests **count against the cap** like any other (the "+ station-attached" phrasing could also read as *extra*, which is exploitable — a bench beside every chest = unlimited storage; **Alex's call to overrule**). *(c)* the chest mode gets the **taller of two frame sizes**, both still stated once in `keeper-panel.tsx` — six rows above the satchel overflowed the fixed body, and a grid whose bottom rows are below the fold turns every put-away into a scroll-and-aim.
> - **⏭️ Next:** Alex's hands on the feel — is 10 the right scarcity, do 48 slots read as generous or as clutter, does a bench beside a chest explain itself. Then: tie the cap to a real tier once liberation exists (today it rides `capRadius` directly), and a chest label/rename.

> - **★ IT PAYS NOTHING, AND THAT IS THE WILDS LOOP.** No ore, no caves, nothing that refills — `spawn-board.ts` already ruled it and Alex reversed the first cut to get there: *"HOME is where you grow things, WILD is where you gather them."* The emitted material set is asserted **CLOSED**, so adding ore has to argue with a failing test rather than slip in as a generator tweak.
> - **★★ THE SAVE BASELINE TRAP — the find of the session, caught before it shipped.** `column.ts`'s `generatedVoxel` falls back to the **CONTINENT's** depth rule, and `recordEdit` diffs against exactly that. Measured on one column: **5888 of 7424 cells (79.3%) would have been stored as phantom edits on first load, before the keeper touched anything.** Two costs and the second is worse — the save balloons by the whole island, and the plot's shape **FREEZES** behind a save asserting the old shape was deliberate. Same family as the chopped-trees bug, larger and pointing the other way. `plotGeneratedVoxel` is the fix; the test asserts the invariant AND counts the damage the wrong baseline would do, so it stays a number.
> - **★ THE SEAM IS A VOLUME, NOT A CUT — canon reversed my own geometry.** I had cut a doorway clean through the bubble's shell. `shimmer-geography.md:272`: a threshold is *"a soft seam in the cloud… ground that simply continues. No gates, no locks, no keep-out"* and *"a build that puts a locked gate on a plot has misread the world."* **A hole is a gate.** It also leads nowhere — the plot is a separate coordinate space and the interior is never generated — so a failed trigger would walk a keeper into the void. And it made the shell's own invariant conditional: the flood test had to **seal the door** to prove the wall holds, so the shipped arrangement was the one never tested. `inPassageVolume` is the trigger; the wall is unbroken.
> - **★ THE SOFT RETURN IS GEOMETRY.** Canon 08-15: over the edge is *"falling through their own fold, which returns them to their threshold. No death, no fall damage… never a penalty."* So `plotThreshold` must ALWAYS be safe to stand on and must exist before any save does. **Derived, not stored** — a stored coord disagrees with the terrain the first time a constant moves, and returns the keeper into rock. `hasFallenOut` reads **altitude, not footprint**: a keeper over unbuilt ground inside the cap has not fallen, and snatching them back would make expansion feel like a wall.
> - **Decisions:** *(a)* **materials are PARAMETERS, not imports** (the `plantWaystones` precedent) — it shipped before `MAT.CLOUD_WALL` existed, which mattered because that registration was in four files hub was live in. *(b)* **`capRadius` is agnostic about what raises it** — the liberation-vs-resources question was live; raising the cap is asserted to leave every generated voxel untouched. *(c)* **bubble is a SHELL, not a body** — at r1000 a solid one is ~4.2B voxels whose interior no player can reach. *(d)* **`null` never `AIR`** where the bubble has no opinion; AIR would punch holes in Wilds terrain. *(e)* **radius 1000 → 500** (below).

At 500 the wall stands **157 blocks off the glade's doorstep, inside the view slider** — so the keeper's fold is on the skyline *from where Gregory tells them about it*. `bubbleSwallows(cfg, landmarks)` guards the next centre change for free.

Nobody moved the bridges, so the world went on stamping the crafted material into the one road every player walks. **Measured on the default seed's spine: 1902 free planking (1336 deck + 566 rail) = 951 logs ≈ 127 goldwoods, breakable BY HAND with no tool.** New `MAT.DECK` (54) takes the crossings; shape, position and flush-with-the-banks construction all unchanged.

> - **★ THE PRECEDENT WAS ONE BAND DOWN AND ALREADY RULED IT.** `MAT.PATH` drops subsoil *"because the road is a CONDITION of the ground, not a block you carry home and lay somewhere else."* A bridge is the road where it crosses water. So this is **not two ids meaning one thing** (the objection that kept bridges on PLANKS in the first place): PLANKING is what you MADE, DECK is worn infrastructure that happens to be timber — exactly as PATH is worn ground that happens to be soil.
> - **Decisions:** *(a)* **`drops: []` is the ruling.** A worthless drop has no wood analogue (every wood item is already a craft input, `goldwood_bark` included — the sawmill eats 4). *(b)* **`hardness: Infinity` was REJECTED** even though it closes the hole harder and is what `MAT.CONJURED` does: a conjured wall *looks* temporary, a bridge looks solid, and an identical plank that breaks when you placed it and refuses when the world did **reads as a bug** — registry.ts's own note says a block that was never going to break is the worst version of the mechanic. **The deck breaks. It just does not pay.** Net read: prying up the crossing is pure vandalism — you wreck the road that holds the grey off at night and carry away nothing. *(c)* **54 breaks the 50+ band's stated rule and the RULE was what was wrong** — 51-53's note calls it the "hand-placed" band; this is generated, and 0-13 is full while 14-15/23/31 stay rejected for the ORE-adjacency reason that once turned a wildflower into a mana seam. **It is the OVERFLOW band from here on.** *(d)* **`GENERATOR_VERSION` 16 → 17** — nothing moved, but what the crossings are made of did, same class as the v15→16 canopy reshape.

> **🪨 THE STATION FAMILY IS THREE, AND EACH ONE SELLS SOMETHING DIFFERENT (bench 08-13 `f4afe00` · sawmill 08-14 `572e0e2` · stonecutter 08-15, all deployed :3200, pushed, canon 7 CLEAN).**
> - **Left off:** the stonecutter shipped — the third station, bench-crafted (6 cut stone + 4 planking), 18s a run, stone only. Placed, right-clicked and salvaged exactly like the other two; `stationOf` carried the whole plumbing.
> - **★ THE ONE THING TO NOT RELITIGATE: THE FAMILY HAS THREE AXES, NOT ONE DIAL.** bench = generalist · sawmill = **TIME** (2.4x faster, logs only) · stonecutter = **MATERIAL** (4 rubble → 3 cut stone instead of 2, stone only, and *slower than the bench* for it). "The sawmill for stone" was the obvious build and could not ship: stone's only recipe paid no bonus, so a faster-narrower cutter would have sold nothing but elapsed time — worth zero against instant free hand-crafting, which is the failure the bench itself was designed around.
> - **★ THROUGHPUT PARITY IS DELIBERATE.** 3-per-18s and 2-per-12s are the same stone per second. The cutter does not make stone arrive faster, it makes rubble go further — so there is no dominant answer and neither station retires the other. Asserted by cross-multiplication, so a tuning pass has to make the choice on purpose.
> - **Decisions:** *(a)* the milled bonus is a **STATION × RECIPE pair** (`StationDef.pays`), not a property of the recipe row — otherwise the generalist bench silently matches every specialist. *(b)* `cut_stone` re-granulated **2→1 into 4→2** (identical ratio) purely so the bonus can be a whole block; there is no integer between 1 and 2. *(c)* stone stays a **net loss at every station** and wood a net gain — that asymmetry IS the building grammar, and the cutter narrows the loss without erasing it. *(d)* the cutter costs **stone**, so you cannot buy out of hand-cutting until you have hand-cut a pile.

New strata would be a statement about what a region is MADE of, i.e. canon + worldgen + a version bump; dressing rock the player already holds is Jin's and ships today.
> - **⚠ THE DARK STONE IS ALEX'S CALL, NOT A GAP TO FILL.** Deep stone (dark violet-grey) is the obvious fourth colour, but the 08-13 ruling makes stone and deep stone drop the **same** rubble (*"two rubbles would be two economies for one material"*) and `recipes.test.ts` asserts it. > **⚡ ONE DRAW PER COLUMN PER PASS — AND THE CEILING IT WAS SUPPOSED TO FIX WAS MEASURED WRONG (2026-08-13 night, jin-cc, world lane).** Asked for: *"fix the perf ceiling — merge section meshes per column."* Shipped, correct, and it does what it says. But the premise did not survive being measured, and that is the more useful half.
> - **★ THE "~3219 DRAW CALLS AT 441 COLUMNS" IN THE 08-13 HANDOFF WAS `drawn.current.size` — MESHES BUILT, NOT DRAWS.** The HUD never reported `renderer.info.render.calls`, so the only number on screen was the count of meshes we had *uploaded*, including every one behind the camera. Real post-cull draws at 278 loaded columns: **208**. Extrapolated to a full 441 ring that is ~330 — an order of magnitude below the figure the ceiling was blamed on, and not a 20ms frame on any GPU. **Frustum culling was already doing the work the number implied nobody was doing.**
> - **What shipped anyway, because it is right on its own merits:** the mesher's unit (16³ section) had been silently inherited as the *draw* unit, so a 256-tall column cost up to 16 meshes per pass. `concatAttrs` (attrs.ts) folds a column's sections into one buffer set, lifting each section's positions by its own origin; the mesh then sits at the column origin, y=0. Measured on a real column ring: **meshes 3297 → 694 at 441 columns (4.75x)**, and live at the moonwell glade **1016 → 222 meshes, 208 → 113 draws, geo 217 → 122**.
> - **★ THE COST IS VERTICAL FRUSTUM CULLING, AND IT IS REAL: triangles 106k → 250k, ~2.5x.** A column with one corner on screen now submits its whole height. Those extra triangles are clipped after the vertex shader and never reach a fragment, so on real hardware this is cheap — but it is a genuine trade and not a free win. **The three passes stay separate** (water blends after opaque; leaves need an alpha cutout the block program must not carry) — neither split is about call count, so neither is fixed by counting calls.
> - **Decisions:** *(a)* **Merge at the HOST, not in `voxel/`.** The mesher stays section-local and pure; meshing-per-section and drawing-per-section were two decisions that only looked like one. *(b)* **No band-size knob.** Merging into 64-tall bands would keep some vertical culling at 4x fewer calls, but it is a tuning parameter for a bottleneck we have not confirmed exists — build it when a measurement asks for it. *(c)* **`draws` and `tris` now live in the HUD next to `mesh`**, and `world-shot.mts` scrapes the line (`[data-stats]`) — the counters are hardware-independent, so SwiftShader reports them exactly. Frame *rate* from this box is meaningless and is deliberately not reported.
> - **⏭️ Next — DO NOT BUILD MORE PERF WORK OFF THE OLD NUMBER.** The 50fps needs a profile on Alex's actual GPU. With draws at ~200-330 and triangles at ~250k, neither is an obvious 20ms; the suspects are the fragment shader (the cartoon stack computes `fract`/`smoothstep` block outlines per pixel, over heavy underground overdraw) and per-frame JS. **One capture on real hardware decides it. Everything before that is guessing.**
> - **Files:** `voxel3d/attrs.ts` (`concatAttrs` + `AttrPart`), `voxel3d/VoxelWorld.tsx` (`remesh` emits three merged meshes; HUD `draws`/`tris`; `data-stats`; evict key comment), `voxel3d/merge.test.ts` (NEW, 23 asserts — the central one is that the merged triangle SET equals the union of the section sets in column space, which catches a dropped lift, a doubled lift, an unshifted index and a channel slip at once), `scripts/world-shot.mts` (`WORLD_RADIUS`, stats scrape).
> - **📊 THE INSTRUMENT (`d605173`, Alex asked for it so he wouldn't need DevTools): `O` → Debug → frame meter.** Off by default. `fps · ms · worst` per quarter-second. **`ms` is beside `fps` because ms is what SUBTRACTS across an A/B** — 60→30 and 30→20 are the same 16.7ms of added work and only one pair looks equal, so a slider comparison read in fps alone mis-ranks itself. **`worst` is why it beats the DevTools overlay here:** the remesh queue draining as you walk into new ground is a HITCH, and a mean is exactly the statistic that hides one. ⚠ It samples **`dtRaw`, never the clamped `dt`** — that clamp floors at 0.05s (20fps), so measuring it would erase every hitch worse than 20fps, i.e. the whole population worth finding. ⚠ It publishes on a **250ms timer, not per frame**: a per-frame `setState` re-renders the HUD every frame and costs enough to move the number, and an instrument that changes what it measures is worse than none. `showFps` is **Omitted from `PRESETS`** so a natural↔cartoon flip cannot switch off the meter mid-measurement — same reason it sits under its own **Debug** heading rather than in Render. `world-shot.mts` gains `WORLD_FPS=1` + a `[data-perf]` scrape (the rate from this box is SwiftShader nonsense and says so; that the meter *publishes* is the thing the flag verifies).
> - **⏭️ The profile plan, for whoever reads this next:** all tests standing still in a dense zone (`/goto twilight-thicket`), baseline first. **(1)** halve the window → fps recovers ⇒ **fill/fragment-bound**. **(2)** `outline` slider → 0 ⇒ isolates the per-pixel `fract`/`smoothstep` block outlines. **(3)** `viewRadius` 6→4 (cost is quadratic) moves it while (1) did not ⇒ **CPU/geometry, not fill**. Then walk into unloaded ground and watch `worst` — that number is the remesh drain and it is a separate fix from all three.

> **✅ THE DROP VERB + RETIRED-ITEM SALVAGE (2026-08-13, deployed :3200, salvage 25 / drops 43 / purity 262 / canon 7 CLEAN).** Alex, once the building grammar retired `block_stone`: *"lets clean my player inventory so that it doesnt have these blocks anymore ..or/plus add a drop item function."* Both — **and the drop verb is the half that keeps mattering, because a bag with no way out is a bag that fills with the last balance change forever.**
> - **Q throws the selected stack, Shift+Q throws all of it**, out along the look vector from chest height. HUD legend updated. **`tossDrop` rather than `spawnDrop` with different arguments**, and the two fields that differ ARE the feature: (1) **direction is the LOOK vector, not a hash of a block coordinate** — a mined block throws deterministically because the same block broken twice must behave identically, but a thrown item has no block, it has a player facing somewhere; (2) **`pickupDelay` 0.45s → 1.6s** — mining's delay exists only so the drop is seen leaving the block, and at 0.45 you are standing inside a 1.6 `pickupRadius`, so the item is back in the bag before it lands. ***"Drop this" silently doing nothing is the least debuggable outcome a verb can have.***
> - **★ THE ORACLE CAUGHT THAT MY DEGENERATE-LOOK GUARD WAS HALF A FIX.** A straight-up look has no horizontal direction; stopping the NaN still left the item at zero horizontal speed, landing on the thrower's feet to be vacuumed 1.6s later — **the same dead verb by another route**. The fallback is a real direction now, not a safe zero.
> - **Queued through a ref, resolved in the frame loop — same as `pendingCast` and for the same reason:** a toss needs the camera's facing and the live drops array, which a listener registered once on mount cannot see without going stale. **The draw-lock comes free** (`selItem` is already null while the weapon is out), and Q's other binding cycles weapons **only while drawn**, so the two cases cannot overlap.
> - **SALVAGE (`voxel/salvage.ts`, pure): REMAP, NEVER DELETE.** A save from before a ruling holds items nothing places, crafts or names. **Silently deleting what someone mined is worse than leaving junk in a slot and is unrecoverable**, so every retirement names a SUCCESSOR — rock became rubble, so the hour spent quarrying survives the rename. Runs at the one point a save becomes live state, and says so out loud (*"your bag caught up: 8 block_stone → rubble"*).
> - **⚠ AN UNLISTED ITEM IS LEFT ALONE, DELIBERATELY.** The table is a list of decisions someone made on purpose, **not a whitelist of everything valid** — treating it as a whitelist means any id it has not heard of gets eaten, which is the same silent destruction wearing a different hat. A stray unknown costs one dead slot; a wrong deletion costs a player's evening.
> - **Asserted by name:** every successor must be a real obtainable item (**a typo would rewrite one dead id into a DIFFERENT dead id while the log line claims a fix**), a retired id must NOT still be obtainable (or the table fights the game forever), counts are preserved, the input array is never mutated, and **`goldwood_plank` is explicitly NOT retired** — it stopped being placeable in the same ruling, but *unplaceable is not the same as gone*, and it is the currency every piece is priced in.
> - **NOT A RECIPE, and the distinction is load-bearing:** `recipes.test.ts` asserts nothing crafts FROM raw stone, and a `block_stone → rubble` recipe would contradict it and hand back a farmable loop into the old economy. A migration runs once over what already exists and cannot be re-entered.
> - **Verified on Alex's live save** (`1337:player`, read out of IndexedDB in the browser): zero retired ids left, and the two rubble stacks sit in **separate slots (7 and 1) rather than merged into 8** — which is the salvage's own documented signature, since merging would need a stack limit the pure file must not know about.

While you can put a dug cube straight back, the pieces layer is optional decoration instead of THE way to build. **Turning that off is the ruling.** Far smaller than it sounds.

Re-priced to cut stone; asserted that no recipe and no piece still asks for the dead ids.

Asserted BY NAME, because the way this dies is someone "finishing" the ruling by sweeping every terrain block into it. *"No block is ever placeable" is the Minecraft answer wearing a coat.*

In a cozy game an irreversible mis-swing that permanently scars the garden is the wrong trade — and so is a perfect undo. Both stones drop the SAME rubble on purpose: one broken-rock economy, with the tier living in what it costs to BREAK them, which is where a player already feels it.
