> **✅ THE CANOPY STOPS BEING SEE-THROUGH, AND A FELLED TREE LOSES IT (2026-08-13, `9caa306`, deployed :3200, greedy 132 / decay 17 / trees 29 / canon 7 CLEAN).** Alex, looking at the deployed 08-12 result: *"the foliage is too sparse so the trunk is clearly visible through the leaves.. and also once the trunk is mined the leaves should come down over time."*
> - **★ THE SEE-THROUGH CANOPY WAS THE MESHER, AND IT WAS MY OWN 08-12 OPTIMISATION.** The leaf pass culled any leaf walled in on all six sides, on the written argument that it "sits behind its own neighbours' crosses from every angle". **That premise holds only if a neighbour is OPAQUE, and a crossed cutout quad is roughly half gap** — two vertical planes through a cube cover nowhere near a cube's solid angle. So the cull was not deleting hidden geometry, it was deleting *exactly the depth the eye looks through the rim to find*, and behind that depth is the trunk. Re-measured in the Thicket: **9,796 of 29,393 leaf voxels — a third of the entire canopy — every one of them interior.** Removing it costs **+7.1% of the world's quads** (289,535 → 310,007). **Generalize: a leaf's geometry is not a cube, so every rule written for cubes has to be re-derived rather than inherited** — the same shape as the 08-12 finding one layer up.
> - **The enclosure count STAYS and is now doing its real job alone:** pure depth shading, so an interior leaf draws DARK and the crown reads as a lit shell over a mass rather than a lattice with sky behind it. That was always the useful half.
> - **Second lever, and it is FREE: the crosses now spill past their own cell** (`K` 0.4375 → 0.5, width 0.92–1.34 of a cell). A cross inset inside its cube leaves a gap at every cell boundary and a canopy is a grid of those gaps. Overlapping neighbours closes the seams with **no extra quads** — vertex area, not draw calls. The old inset guarded z-fighting between coplanar crosses, which stopped being possible the moment yaw was hashed per world cell (08-12).
> - **★ THE ORACLE CAUGHT THE CHANGE AND THE ASSERT WAS INVERTED, NOT DELETED.** `only the shell of a solid canopy is meshed` existed precisely to fail if someone reinstated the buried quads — so it did its job, loudly. The number is still worth pinning, just the other way up: a canopy must be exactly 2 quads per leaf voxel, no cull, nothing merged. Plus a new assert that interior and rim shades **both** survive, or the crown goes back to one flat tone.
> - **LEAF DECAY (`voxel/decay.ts`, pure).** Chopping already persists via `Column.overrides`, so before this the reward for felling a tree was a canopy hanging in the air forever — the one edit in the world that visibly refused to finish.
>   - **★ SUPPORT IS RECOMPUTED AT CHOP TIME, NOT STORED PER CELL.** Minecraft keeps a distance-to-log number in every leaf's block state; we cannot, because a voxel here is ONE material id in a flat array and that is what makes sections, saves, the mesher and the worker boundary cheap. **Adding a per-cell counter would change the world's storage format for a feature that fires a few times a minute.** So it is a multi-source BFS out of the surviving logs, **through leaves only** — through air, support would leak across a clearing and a severed crown would be propped up by the tree opposite.
>   - **Chopping the BASE of a trunk takes nothing**; the canopy comes down when the last log near it is gone. Deliberately Minecraft's rule, for a reason that is ours: it makes felling a tree an act with an ending instead of every mis-click raining leaves. Asserted both directions, plus **"not one leaf of the STANDING tree is taken"** when two crowns touch.
>   - **The box searched is LARGER than the answer it may give** (span 10, reach 7): a leaf at the box edge may be held by a log one step further out, and reporting it would eat a bite out of the untouched tree next door every time you fell its neighbour.
>   - **ABSOLUTE TIMESTAMPS IN A SEED-KEYED SIDECAR, not countdowns** — that is the whole persistence story. Come back an hour later and every entry is already due, so the canopy you felled is simply gone. A countdown pauses whenever the game is not running and the tree is still standing when you return. Sidecar (like the pot clock) rather than the column record (like a chest's contents), because the queue is only a note about the FUTURE: losing it costs one canopy that stays up, never an item.
>   - **Hooked into `setVoxel`** — the same funnel the chest record uses — so any future path that removes a log (explosion, console verb, deconstruct) drops its leaves too, not only the mining branch. ⚠ It must run AFTER the section write or the log being felled counts as its own support and nothing ever decays.
>   - **★ ONE LEAF PER FRAME, AND THE CAP IS THE POINT.** `setVoxel` remeshes its column inline — right for a player mining a block per click, ruinous here: a felled goldwood orphans **~100 leaves at once** (measured against the real generator, seed 1337), which would be ~100 column remeshes in one frame against 16.7ms and a **3.4ms warm mesh cost**. That is the slump regression's exact shape — *fine per block, catastrophic per canopy*. Draining at one per frame bounds it to what mining already costs and still clears a tree in under two seconds. The sidecar save is throttled to 2s for the same reason: `localStorage.setItem` is synchronous and this drains at 60Hz.
>   - **Re-chopping keeps the EARLIEST fall time.** The scan re-runs on every swing, so the same leaf is re-orphaned repeatedly while a trunk comes down; taking the newest time each pass means a fast chopper outruns the decay forever — a bug that only appears when someone plays *well*.
> - **⚠ `leaf-census.mts` OUTLIVED ITS QUESTION FOR THE SECOND TIME IN TWO DAYS.** The 08-12 rewrite carries a warning about exactly this, and the very next edit to the leaf pass falsified it again: it printed **"buried leaves culled … 0 quads saved (0%)"** — confident, and an answer to a question nobody is asking. Rewritten to the live one. **If you change the leaf pass, change that block in the same commit.**
> - **`scripts/world-shot.mts` gained `WORLD_GOTO` + `WORLD_PITCH`.** The player always spawns in the GLADE, which is a clearing, so every headless shot was photographing the one place in the world with the fewest trees. The console is the only mover a script can reach. ⚠ Pitch needs a real click first — the camera only turns while the pointer is LOCKED, and a scripted `requestPointerLock()` has no user activation.
> - **★ TWO THINGS THE BROWSER CANNOT DO FROM THIS SEAT, worth knowing before planning around it:** Chrome (the extension) runs on Alex's machine, so **`localhost:3201` — a lane's `devwin` server — is unreachable from it**; only `ather.games` is. And the extension's synthetic click **does not earn pointer lock**, so CC can teleport with `/goto` and read the HUD but cannot turn the camera or mine. Headless `world-shot.mts` is the iterate loop; Chrome is for confirming what shipped.
> - **⏳ OPEN, AND IT IS ALEX'S CALL:** **`starwillow`'s log is lavender-grey and reads as poured concrete.** Confirmed in real GL next to saturated grass, so it is not a software-GL artifact — and the icon sheet shows its bark tile also carries visibly less grain contrast than the other three, which is the half that makes it read as painted rather than as pale bark. **It is starwillow, not goldwood** (goldwood is warm brown, shimmeroak grey-brown, dawnwood rust) — worth knowing because starwillow crowds LOW GROUND, so the glade and the moonwell are full of it and it reads as "the world's trees are purple".
> - **⏳ ALSO OPEN, MINE, NOT DONE:** the **tall species have thin crowns** — dawnwood at max height is 17 blocks tall with **127 leaf voxels**, against goldwood at *minimum* height, 8 tall with **101**. The rarest, tallest tree is barely denser than the smallest common one and spreads it over twice the height. And **starwillow's fork does not read short**: at h=8 the two limb canopies overlap into one blob, so the one species that justifies a second trunk placer looks like the others about half the time.
> - **⚠ NOT HAND-PLAYED: nobody has swung an axe at a tree since decay shipped.** It is proven pure (17 asserts) and against the real generator (base-chop → 0 orphans, full fell → 99 of the 119 leaves in range, neighbour untouched, fall spread 0.95–2.00s), and the mining path provably routes through the hooked `setVoxel` — but the feel of the fall is unmeasured. **Alex: fell a goldwood and call the timing.**

> **✅ THE TREES STOP BEING UMBRELLAS (2026-08-12, `d79b341`, deployed + pushed, trees 29 / mesher 131 / column 20 / canon 7 CLEAN).** Alex, after the crossed-quad round shipped: *"the trees still look like the old umbrellas."* He was right, and **two of the three causes were mine from that same morning** — I had fixed the leaf MATERIAL and called the canopy done without ever looking at the canopy's SHAPE.
> - **★ THE METHOD IS THE FINDING: I read a cross-section, not a screenshot.** A headless shot said "much better" and I nearly stopped there. Printing the actual voxel profile of one goldwood showed the crown was **77 sparse, visibly LOPSIDED voxels** and that my new droop strands were leaving **single leaves floating two blocks under a nibbled hole** — a defect I had just introduced, invisible at screenshot distance and dead obvious in ASCII. Same family as the 08-12 duplicate-layer lesson: *the cheap direct readout beats the impressive indirect one.* `scratchpad/tree-profile.mts` is 30 lines and should be the first thing anyone touching `trees.ts` runs.
> - **`squash` was a hardcoded 2.1 shared silently by every blob species.** It divides the crown's vertical semi-axis, so a radius-3 goldwood — **58% of the forest by weight, i.e. the world's tree silhouette** — resolved to a crown 6-7 wide and **3 tall**. That is a parasol. Now a species parameter: goldwood 1.15, shimmeroak 1.25. minHeight 5→6 with it, because at 5 the taller crown swallowed the trunk and it read as a bush.
> - **★ THE NIBBLE WAS HOLLOWING THE CROWN, NOT FRAYING ITS EDGE.** `d > r²*0.55 && g() < 0.4` sounds like a rim; past 55% of r² is most of the **volume**, and at radius 3 that is every cell but a handful. 0.72/0.3 confines it to the true rim. **And the mesher now carries this load** — per-cell jitter makes the surface irregular on its own, so the generator no longer buys raggedness by deleting foliage. *Two systems were paying for the same effect and the geometry could least afford it.*
> - **The underside is the other half of it.** An ellipsoid's bottom is a clean horizontal disc however tall the crown above it, and that disc at eye level IS the umbrella. Droop strands hang under the rim — anchored **at** the shell cell, not below it, or a nibbled hole detaches them.
> - **EVERY CROSS WAS IDENTICAL — fixed 45°/135°, full width, dead centre.** So a canopy was a **lattice of the same X on a perfect grid**, which the eye reads as a textured slab. Yaw/width/offset now hash per **WORLD** cell (new `origin` arg on `greedyMesh`, defaulted so every existing caller stays byte-identical — same reason `atlas.ts` hashes world position: a local hash trades a 1-block repeat for a 16-block one, which is *more* visible).
> - **★ A LEAF WALLED IN ON ALL SIX SIDES NOW DRAWS NOTHING, and that is the entire budget for the fuller crown.** It sits behind its own neighbours' crosses from every angle and cost two quads anyway. **Measured, not hoped** (`leaf-census.mts`, Thicket, radius 6): leaf voxels **17,388 → 28,290 (1.63× foliage)**, leaf quads **34,776 → 37,862 (1.09×)**, world **285,957 → 289,083 (1.01×)**. The cull returns **33%** of the canopy's quads.
> - **Fixed a test a CORRECT cross could fail:** it compared the two quads' `normal.x`, and two perpendicular quads share an x component at exactly 45° — precisely where the old fixed-yaw pass put every one of them. It was passing on a *sign*, not an orientation. Now compares the full normal + asserts unit length.
> - **⚠ `leaf-census.mts` WAS LYING and I nearly trusted it.** It still asked *"should leaves become cross-quads"* — a decision that shipped that morning — so it compared the live mesher against itself and printed **"1.26× the current leaf cost"** for a change that cost 1.09×. Rewritten to report the cull's saving. *A measurement script that outlives its question does not go quiet; it reports a wrong number confidently.*
> - **★ AND THE PROFILE SCRIPT IMMEDIATELY EARNED ITSELF A SECOND TIME — the LAYERED species were pagoda roofs (`f0e0a94`).** Having fixed the blob species I nearly stopped, because starwillow + dawnwood are only **16% of the forest by weight**. The cross-section said otherwise: `tiers = max(2, round(r))` at one block per tier gave dawnwood a **4-block crown on a 10-15 block trunk (27% of its height)**, and the radius shrank **monotonically from the bottom tier** — so the widest disc was the lowest one, which is a parasol by definition. Making it merely taller would have built a taller parasol. Profile now peaks a third of the way up and tapers to a point, base sunk into the trunk, strands under the base tier. Dawnwood 27% → **47%**. *Rare trees are the ones players stop and look at; 16% by weight is not 16% by attention.*
> - **⏳ STILL OPEN, AND IT IS AN ART CALL, NOT A GEOMETRY ONE:** the log **colour** reads pale grey-lavender — concrete, not bark — which is now the loudest remaining "that is not a tree" cue. `MATERIAL_COLOR[*_LOG]` + the log tile. **Alex's domain; not touched.**
> - **Tool kept: `scripts/tree-profile.mts`.** Prints any species' cross-section at min and max height with its crown-to-height ratio. Run it before AND after any `trees.ts` change.

> **✅ THE CANOPY STOPS BEING A GREEN BOX — leaves are crossed cutout quads (2026-08-12, deployed, mesher oracle 126, render-audit 71 CLEAN).** Second lever off Alex's *"does our world have to be blocky?"* list, after AO. Leaf-cubes were the biggest remaining silhouette offender because a canopy is the one place the world puts a big opaque cube where the eye expects a ragged edge.
> - **★ I RECOMMENDED THE WRONG PLAN FIRST AND CAUGHT IT BEFORE BUILDING.** The 08-11 note said "real tree models through the unused prop layer". `world/prop-models.tsx` is a **play3d** GLB loader for STATION props (alchemy station, bench, chest) — static placed objects. Trees in voxel3d are not that: **logs carry the entire forestry economy** (drops, skill XP, tier gates, every plank/blade/spade recipe), leaves are breakable, and `Column.overrides` exists *specifically* so a chopped tree stays chopped. Swapping them for meshes would have killed chopping, collision and the light BFS. **Trees stay voxels; only the geometry changes** — the AO split again: *the grid is load-bearing, the READ is not.*
> - **★★ THE SCARY NUMBER WAS THE WRONG NUMBER (`scripts/leaf-census.mts`).** Instance count looked fatal — **59,270 exposed leaf voxels** at max radius in the Thicket against the flora renderer's proven ~17k. But quads are what cost, and **the greedy mesher was never winning on leaves**: a blob of radius 3-5 has almost nothing coplanar to merge. Meshed for real at radius 6: canopy already emits **31,481 quads (11.1% of the world's 283k)** against **34,776** as crossed quads — **1.10× the leaves, 1.01× the world**, and the bench is unchanged at **49.0 ms/column**. *Measure the thing that costs, not the thing that sounds big.*
> - **★ THE CUTOUT IS THE FEATURE, NOT THE CROSS.** Crossed quads of solid colour are two intersecting cards — arguably worse than a cube, which at least looks deliberate. The ragged silhouette comes from **alpha**. Tile is procedural (overlapping blobs + a chewed border so no quad ends in a straight edge) and **painted WHITE** so the vertex colour carries the species tint × canopy-depth shade — **one texture for all four woods**, same trick as the flower head.
> - **`alphaTest`, never `transparent`:** a cutout writes depth and needs no sorting, so a canopy composes with itself from any angle. Transparent would drag thousands of quads into the blended pass and make a tree order-dependent — the exact bug water is split out to avoid, on a far bigger surface. Leaves take a **third partition** beside water (`buildAttrsSplit`), which is one extra program for the world; the per-chunk-material rule forbids a program per CHUNK, not a second pass. Leaves are also the **only** partition carrying UVs — every other quad is axis-aligned so the shader derives them, but a diagonal has no face to key off.
> - **Depth shading from ENCLOSURE**, since corner AO cannot describe a non-face quad: count the six neighbours, bury it, darken it. **The oracle caught the first thresholds darkening at 3+ neighbours — which a blob CORNER already has** — so nothing in an entire canopy came out lit and it read as mud rather than depth. Now only genuine burial (4+) darkens.
> - 126 asserts, including that **a leaf beside a log hides none of the log** (leaves read as AIR to the sweep, so trunks draw the bark a canopy used to bury) and that **meshing never consumes the leaf** — the assertion that would catch someone "cleaning up" by deleting leaf voxels and taking forestry with it.
> - ⏭ **What the fix REVEALED, now the limiting factor:** canopies read as flat wide umbrellas. That is the generator's foliage shape (`trees.ts` SPECIES radius vs height), which the solid cube-mass used to hide — a shape/design call, not a render one. ⏭ Trunks still read pale lavender: the face-shading tint in `mesh-bridge.ts`, still open with live sliders.

> **✅ THE CAMERA GRAB WAS MINING, AND A FIST WAS COLLECTING THE SPADE'S DISCOUNT (2026-08-12, deployed, mining oracle 45→49).** Alex reported both as feel; both were bugs.
> - **★ CLICKING TO TAKE THE CAMERA BROKE THE BLOCK YOU WERE FACING.** While unlocked, a canvas click means *give me the mouse* — but `mousedown` set `mouse.left` before anything asked whether the world was listening, and the frame loop read that as start-mining. So every Escape cost you a block on the way back in. **Same shape as yesterday's bag slot-click bug, one layer out:** that gate asked *is a cursor SURFACE open*, and a free pointer with no panel up is the case it structurally could not see. The honest question is not which UI is open but **whether the mouse belongs to the world at all**, and the pointer lock is the only thing that answers it. Press refused, **release still recorded** — the same asymmetry as the menu gate, because a button held across a lock change must not strand `mouse.left` true.
> - **★★ THE `fastSkill` DISCOUNT WAS GOING TO BARE HANDS.** The mining block passed the block's wanted skill to `breakSeconds` *whether or not a tool was equipped*, and on an ungated block that IS the discount (`toolSkill === fastSkill` → `hardness * 0.55`). Soil, sand, grass and path dug at full spade rate from the first second of the game. **The tell is what it did to the SPADE, not to the dirt:** `tools.ts` calls the spade "a SPEED tier on top" of hands and the first tool a new keeper should reach for — but hands already had that tier, so a Goldwood Spade bought its 0.9 `speedBonus` and nothing else, **10% instead of ~50%**. The upgrade was invisible, which is exactly what Alex felt. **A mechanic can be perfectly implemented in the registry and still be dead because a caller hands it the wrong argument.** Gated blocks unaffected (`ensureBasicTools` guarantees blade/spike/rinstick); farming is deliberately toolless so hands can always dig.
> - **⏭ `/mine <rate>` IS THE DIAL, and the number is Alex's.** Whether the *intended* times are right is taste, and guessing a multiplier on top of a fresh bug fix is how you overshoot and retune twice. Owner-gated, session-only, live. ⚠ Scaled **at the tick, not through `toolSpeed`** — `breakSeconds` deliberately drops `toolSpeed` on the bare-hand branch, so a dial riding on it would silently not touch hands, which is most of what a new keeper digs and the exact case being judged. Post-fix reference: topsoil bare-hand **0.55s** (was 0.30), with a Goldwood Spade **0.27s**; stone with a Worn Spike **1.6s**; deep stone **2.4s**.

> **✅ AMBIENT OCCLUSION — THE WORLD STOPS READING AS LEGO (2026-08-12, `ac8e873` + `1d42730`, deployed, mesher oracle 118, render-audit 72 CLEAN).** The #1 item off Alex's *"does our world have to be blocky?"* question, and the one that needed neither art nor a canon ruling: there was **no AO anywhere in the mesher — not weak, none.** Corner darkening is most of what makes stacked cubes read as sharing a space.
> - **★ AO RIDES IN THE MASK KEY, WHICH IS WHY MERGING STAYS CORRECT FOR FREE.** The greedy sweep merges while `mask[n] === c`; a second array would put a second compare in the hottest loop in the mesher. The mask is `Int32Array` and materials occupy 10 bits, so four corners at 2 bits park at bit 16 and the **existing equality test** separates cells that differ only in shading. A flat field still merges to one quad; merging only breaks where a merged quad would have been wrong anyway.
> - **★★ PERF WAS THE WHOLE STORY AND TOOK THREE ATTEMPTS.** Sampling the world 8× per face with a coordinate array per sample: **27.3 → 153.9 ms/column (5.6×).** Flattening the allocations: **53.4, still 2×.** **The AO arithmetic was never the cost at any point — the SAMPLING was.** Fix: materialise each slice ONCE into a ringed grid, then note that **consecutive planes share a slice** (plane k's upper is plane k+1's lower) and swap buffers — `(S+2)²` samples per plane where the old loop did `2·S²`, i.e. **1156 vs 2048, fewer lookups than before AO existed.** Final **29.6 → 49.7 ms/column** on a clean A/B, and nearly all the remainder is real work: AO's merge splits raise quads (surface 408→743, caves 4683→11603, greedy win 4.4×→1.8×). **Meshing is in a worker, so this is latency on a block break, not a frame hitch.** ⚠ The swap only holds while planes are contiguous — the uniform fast path jumps, so `filled` tracks residency; getting it wrong looks fine except at section boundaries.
> - **★ THE ORACLE PASSED A MUTATION OF THE EXACT BUG ITS OWN COMMENT WARNS ABOUT.** Front and back quads wind corners in different orders, so shading must reorder with them; writing the canonical order onto both mirrors every back face. **116 asserts stayed green with that bug injected** — counts, splits and inside-corners are all too symmetric to notice. Found by mutating the line on purpose. Added a POSITIONAL assert (occluder on +x ⇒ the dark corners are at world x=5, not their mirror) and confirmed it fails on the mutation. **A green oracle is a claim; mutate it before believing it.** Now 118.
> - Verified by rendering the live world and looking: the leaf mass reads as a mass with corner depth instead of flat identical tiles, trunks are grounded. `AO_CURVE` in `attrs.ts` is the dial (0.62 darkest); AO folds into **vertex colour**, so no new attribute, no worker buffer, **no shader change**.
> - **✅ Also fixed — `render-audit` was crying wolf.** Its memo check tested whether `useMemo(` appeared **within four lines**, i.e. distance standing in for *are we inside the memo*. A memo returning >3 entries broke it: the Hollow material table's first entry passed and the other two reported as unmemoised GPU allocations. **Two false alarms on correct code, and this audit's own header tells you not to widen the allowlist when it fails** — so a false positive spends the only thing a lint has, and the next real finding arrives looking like the noise. Now walks back to the nearest `useMemo(` and counts parens (containment, the same reasoning its factory check already used). Verified it still flags a genuine per-render material. `6a47587`.

> **✅ ITEM ART — IT WAS ALREADY DRAWN, AND IT WAS SHIPPING AS CONFETTI (2026-08-12, `8dac447`, deployed, canon 7 CLEAN).** Asked for "non-block item art plus a checklist to track it". The checklist is the deliverable; building it is what exposed three faults, each invisible for the same reason — **every reader agreed with every other, so there was no second opinion to disagree with.**
> - **★ THE TASK WAS MOSTLY ALREADY DONE AND NOBODY COULD SEE IT.** `sprites/items.ts` holds 76 hand-painted icons from the 2D game; **34 are items voxel3d can hold** — every crystal, plank, blade, spike and rinstick. `voxel3d/tex/item-icon.ts` only ever derived icons from block textures, so the bag drew its "no art yet" chip for art Alex painted months ago. Fallback is now **block faces → flat sprite → chip**, block ALWAYS first (an item with a block behind it must wear that block's real faces or the two drift, which is this file's founding argument). The chip survives as tier three and its meaning is finally true when it shows.
> - **★★ 65 OF 96 SPRITE LITERALS WERE 16×16 ART DECLARED AS 32×32.** `px(S, S, …)` allocates 1024 slots and fills the first 256 **sequentially**, so 16 rows of 16 land as 8 rows of 32-wide garbage. Every consumer derives the edge as `sqrt(length)`, reads 32, and draws the scramble — `drawSprite` and the editor alike. **The file's own first line says "16x16 pixel art icons" and line 7 sets `S = 32`**: it was migrated 16→32 and the data never came with it. `violet_crystal`, every blade, spike, rinstick, potion and mana seed has been rendering as scattered dots **in the shipped 2D game**. Found by rendering the contact sheet and LOOKING — no test states this, and the editor showed the identical scramble, which is exactly why it survived.
> - **Alex ruled 2× upscale over centring** (both recover the art; they differ in scale): it matches the visual weight of the 12 icons genuinely authored at 32, and it hands him a full 32×32 canvas already carrying the art when he opens one to refine. `scripts/migrate-item-sprites.mjs`, one-shot, idempotent, touches only literals with **exactly 256 digits AND declared `px(S, S, …)`** — verified first that no literal legitimately declares 16×16, since upscaling one of those would break art that was already correct.
> - **★ `ITEM_PALETTES` WAS WRITTEN BY THE EDITOR, READ BY THE EDITOR, AND BY NOTHING THAT RENDERS IN A GAME.** `ItemIcon` — the only component that draws an item in play — read `SEED_PALETTES` and never `ITEM_PALETTES`, so 13 items previewed in their hand-tuned colours and **shipped in the default palette** (`goldwood_plank`'s index 1 is dark bark in its own table and **magenta** in the fallback). The fix is not adding the table to the second reader, it is deleting the second opinion: one **`paletteForItem()`**, called by both. Seeds outrank on purpose — three ids sit in both tables, `SEED_PALETTES` is what ships today, so the order makes the diff land only on the 13 that were plainly broken. Restyling the seed line is a LOOK call and stays Alex's; `PALETTE_COLLISIONS` prints it rather than letting it settle in as folklore.
> - **THE CHECKLIST IS GENERATED, NOT KEPT** — `npm run item:art` → `ITEM-ART.md`, and it classifies each item by **calling the shipped icon path** instead of describing it, so it cannot claim art the game is not drawing. **58 reachable items: 26 derived · 20 painted · 10 need art · 2 wired-to-blank.** `--sheet` renders every icon as it ships (same law as `icon-sheet.mts`: the sheet and the game are one function).
> - **★ IT REPORTS, IT DOES NOT GATE, and the first run is why.** It found `pure_spike` + `moonkoi_rinstick` — the tier-3 prospecting and rinning tools — wired into `ITEM_ICONS` with **all-zero frames**: listed as drawn in the editor, drawing nothing. That is real and it is ART, which no build-runner can fix, so failing on it would put the repo permanently red and the script permanently unread. `--strict` exists for the day CI wants it. The in-game half is handled where it belongs: **`flatIcon` refuses a blank frame**, so those fall through to the honest chip instead of rendering an invisible sprite.
> - ⏭ **Alex — 10 items need art** (`/shimmer/dev?mode=item`, 32×32): the 3 **spades** + 3 **worn** starter tools, **grass_tuft · tall_grass · wild_flower · mana_seed**, plus the 2 blank tier-3 tools above. ⏭ **And a colour call:** the four elemental crystals share one shape with no palette of their own, so **violet and water both render as plain white diamonds** — the element is unreadable. ⚠ Left alone deliberately: `ATHER_SOIL_NODE`/`ATHER_SOIL_PLANTED` are **992 digits** (31 rows), neither size, so they render skewed — a separate small fix in the node sprites.

> **✅ MOVEMENT FEEL + THE NIGHT GETS TEETH — 2026-08-11 late (`0a33338` · `54cca0d` · `6ef08c4` · `b672525` · `7d652d4`, all deployed).** Four passes, one thread: things that were BUILT but did not land.
> - **HALF-SLAB STEPS, BOTH WAYS.** Alex: walking up slabs "feels jagged". `stepped()` teleports the feet +0.5 in one frame and the camera is `py + eye`, so the whole rise hit one frame. The snap must stay (a body halfway inside a slab fails the next `bodyFree` and the walk stutters) — so physics stays exact and a render-only `stepSmooth` debt drains on a half-life through the one `eyeY()`. **★ The debt CAP was a second bug only a whole staircase revealed:** capping at one slab jerked 0.16 at every stair, because each rise lands while ~0.07 of the last is owed and the clamp discards it — **discarded height IS the pop**. Then Alex ruled the descent too: `FALL_OFF` 0.32→0.55 in voxel3d only (surfaces sit at whole/half blocks, so the widened band can only contain a slab; a 1-block drop still falls, coyote untouched). That killed the grounded `py += (floorTop-py) * 0.25` — **two bugs in one line**: feet hovering above the floor they stood on, and a per-frame factor that settled 2.4× faster at 144Hz.
> - **THE TOOL ARC WAS THE MYSTERY BLOB.** The "odd cluster of translucent green shapes" in the first world shot was `ToolSocket`'s `opacity: active ? 1 : 0.4` on the WRAPPER — it dimmed the socket's own plate (`bg-black/45` × 0.4 = an 18% film), so over grass the plate vanished and four ghost rings floated on the world. Our own rule ("text never sits raw on a scene") lost to its sibling ("inactive ~40% opacity") applied to the wrong layer. Plate is opaque; **the CONTENT carries state contrast**. Diagnosed and verified through the render harness, not by asking Alex to squint.
> - **THE HOLLOW'S TOUCH LANDS.** One caught you and glided THROUGH you — the light field, spawn cycle, pack walk and the lantern's safe room all existed to price the dark and the dark was free. **It DRAINS, it does not damage, and that is canon** (nothing in it to free, nothing in it that strikes) — which also routes around the open cozy-vs-peril gap, since a drain needs no ruling on whether a keeper can die.

> - **GUNS (`827519b`) — an EXTRACTION, not a port.** `WEAPONS` was a bare literal at `Shimmer3D.tsx:1804` and everything using it lived in `FiringRange`, a ~650-line component that is **five systems in one `useFrame`** (gunplay + cast layer + fields + conjured terrain + status bag + hunter orbs). **★ And the half a copy could never bring is collision — every check reads `gridRef.current[cz][cx]`, a tile grid this world has not got.** So `engine/weapons.ts` holds the shared half (table + tuning + pure ballistics, values VERBATIM); **play3d imports it too**, so two walkers can never disagree about what a Lance is. Voxel owns hit detection via the voxel DDA already used for mining. Projectiles not hitscan (the table defines `projSpeed` per model; also a projectile can be led/dodged once mobs land). Each round raycasts the **segment travelled, not its endpoint** — a Lance covers ~0.9 units/frame and endpoint sampling tunnels through thinner walls. **One shared tracer geo+material**: a material per projectile is a shader program per projectile = the exact allocation that got this page BLOCKED from WebGL on 08-06, and full-auto would hit it in a second. 52 asserts; two target the cone sampler because it is invisible when wrong — the degenerate-basis NaN on axis-aligned forward (reads in-game as *"the gun sometimes does nothing"*) and the missing `sqrt(r1)` that makes every gun shoot tighter than its cone claims.
> - **LIGHT FIELD (`7dade45`)** — prerequisite for darkness-gated mobs. There was **no light model at all** (flat `ambientLight 0.4`, no day/night), so "dark" could not be asked. **★ TWO CHANNELS, NOT ONE, IS THE WHOLE DESIGN:** sky floods down and is stored *once*, scaled by the clock only when READ; block light BFSes from emitters and never scales. Collapse them and you lose a cave dark at noon AND a surface that darkens at dusk, both of which come free because only the multiplier moves — one value means re-flooding the world every time the sun does. It also gives the torch its meaning: block light ignores the clock, so a lit room is safe at midnight. **★ It drives SPAWNING, not rendering, deliberately** — per-voxel light as a vertex attribute breaks greedy meshing exactly as per-block texture variation would have (a flat lit floor goes 1 quad → 1024), the same trap in a third disguise. Minecraft's modern rule verbatim: **block light must be 0** (not the old ≤7), which is literally Alex's "complete darkness"; block light is an absolute **VETO**, not a contribution, because a sum would let a bright day mask an unlit corner and a dark night overwhelm a torch. Sky falling straight DOWN does not decay. Flat `Int32Array` BFS queue — 16×256×16 = 65,536 cells, recursion blows the stack on the first deep cave. Out-of-box reads dark AND solid, never open air (the 08-06 absence-is-never-air rule). **Canon fit:** the night-tide line *"tended light holds grey off; when it banks, untended grey has range"* **IS** `dayFactor` scaling sky light — and `shimmer-geography.md` already rules that what spawns at night is Jin's, so the mechanic needed no ruling.

> **✅ ⑤ TERRAIN SLUMP — SHIPPED 2026-08-11 (`2628001`, deployed :3200, canon 7 CLEAN).** The parked big rock, on Alex's ruling **"garden strolls, wilds clamber"** — and the framing that made it buildable is that **the wall is QUANTIZATION, not terrain.** `columnHeight` rounds a continuous field to whole voxels, so two columns whose real altitudes are 10.49 and 10.51 — a fifth of a block apart in the field — become 10 and 11 on the ground. Locomotion's ruling is that a 1-block rise BLOCKS and must be vaulted, so every one of those artefacts is a vault the terrain never asked for, in country the plains pass already measured as gentle (mean |dh| 0.44). · **THE RULE IS THE LIP.** A column one above a neighbour, **with nothing higher beside it**, gives up the top half of its top voxel; the 1.0 rise then walks as 0.5 + 0.5 on the half-step locomotion already shipped with the slabs. **The nothing-higher clause is the whole safety argument** — shaving helps every neighbour below and hurts every neighbour above, so without it a 2-block wall becomes 2.5 and leaves mantle range. Nothing is flattened: a hillside that genuinely climbs a block per column has no horizontal run to spend two half-steps on and stays a clamber **in the garden too**, which is honest. Measured seed 1337 over the garden: **19% of columns slump, 68% of the invented vaults gone.** · **★ THE ORACLE CORRECTED THE DESIGN'S OWN CLAIM.** The first safety assert demanded no rise ever grow and failed on **11797 pairs — every one the same 0 → 0.5**: the flat ground behind a slumped lip. That is not a bug, it is what the feature LOOKS like (a terrace edge worn down) and it costs the player nothing, since ≤0.5 auto-steps. So the property shipped as **"never turns a walkable rise into a vault, never deepens a wall"**, with a third assert pinning 0 → 0.5 as the ONLY growth allowed — because collapsing them back to one "never larger" line is exactly how the nothing-higher clause gets deleted as dead weight later. · **STRENGTH RIDES `tended`, DITHERED.** Same `t * tended` product `greyAllowance` reads (kindness and difficulty are the same axis). A hard threshold would put the change on an iso-contour of a wobbled ellipse — **a visible ring where the ground stops being kind**, the per-biome seam this stack refuses everywhere else — so the gate is dithered against a small blobby field: heart softens everything, Outfields (tended 0.45) soften in patches, wilds never. Asserted by demanding both answers inside every fringe radial. · **MESHER:** a slumped cell **leaves the greedy sweep** (it is not a unit cube, so it cannot join a merge that assumes one — same exclusion piece occupancy already uses) and a half pass draws it: top at +0.5, sides only where a neighbour does not already cover them, **no bottom** (the sweep already emitted the cell below's top face at that exact plane; drawing one would z-fight it). No merging on purpose — lips come in strings, never fields. · **`isHalfCell` is the ONE definition** the mesher and the walker both read: a cell drawn at 0.5 that collides at 1.0 is an invisible lip you trip on, the reverse is a floor you sink through, and both are silent (the sprite pipeline's three-copies-of-a-frame-map lesson). It requires **AIR above**, which is what makes the feature self-healing — a trunk, ruin wall, waystone or block the player sets down restores full height, so nothing ever floats half a voxel up, and no bank softens below its waterline. · **★ THE TRAP THAT WOULD HAVE SHIPPED IT DEAD: the worker sends VOXELS, NOT THE COLUMN.** `voxel-gen.worker` posts packed section data and the main thread rebuilds the Column — recomputing `surface` but, in the first cut, **not `slump`**. The worker is the NORMAL path, so terrain slump would have passed its entire 25-assert oracle and done **nothing in the actual game**. Caught only by reading the build's own artifact churn (`public/voxel-gen.worker.*.js` rotating) and following it. **Anything DERIVED from the height field must be rebuilt on adoption**; `slumpMask` now returns surface+mask together from one ring sample, so the two ways into a Column cannot disagree. · Oracles: slump 25 (incl. a mesh-geometry assert that nothing is drawn in a lip's empty upper half), greedy 103, column 20, locomotion 58, purity 236, canon 7 CLEAN. ⏭ **Alex walks the garden and calls the feel** — does tended ground read as strollable, and does the wild/garden boundary announce itself? Sister item still parked: stair corner variants via the fence-arm trick. *Last touched 2026-08-11.*

> **✅ ⑥ GROUND COVER BECOMES BLOCKS + THE SLUMP PERF REGRESSION (2026-08-11, `344b6b1` + `bc6cbd2`, deployed, canon 7 CLEAN).** Alex playtested slump, hit lag, and made the better call on the fix: *"the player cant enteract with the grass or flowers so they are more of an asthetic which isnt where id like it to go.. everything should be collectable."* Two threads. · **THE LAG, HALF MINE.** Slump had put a per-cell `half()` callback in the greedy sweep's inner loop (3·(S+1)·S² per section). **Warm, per column: 3.5ms pre-slump → 6.6ms as shipped → 3.8ms fixed.** The sweep is **CALL-bound**, so the fix is handing it DATA not a question: `meshColumn` strips the lips out of a COPY of the section and passes a small map (plus the one-cell ring) for the half pass to draw from; the inner loop is byte-identical to the pre-slump mesher again. **Two fixes that look obviously right and do nothing, both recorded in greedy.ts:** gating the callback to sections that can hold a lip (19.3ms — those ARE the sections doing the work) and folding the test into the `sample` closure (19.3ms — two calls per sample became three; **the indirection WAS the cost**). ★ **MEASUREMENT LESSON: my first numbers (10.5→22.2ms) were COLD-START JIT** and overstated the absolute scale ~3×. The ratio held so the fix was right, but I nearly chased the wrong magnitude — **warm the bench before believing a per-frame number.** · **THE OTHER HALF WAS ALEX'S READ, AND IT WAS CORRECT: flowers.** `DRIFT_EDGE` 0.60 put **30% of the garden inside a drift**, so the carpet that is supposed to be a place you FIND was simply the ground — 7728 flowers in a 224-block view, each **two alpha quads**, which is the overdraw profile that swamps a GPU. Fixed by **rarity, not dilution** (0.60→0.72 = 9.4% of ground; `FLOWER_DENSITY` stays high so a drift is still a carpet): garden flowers **−67%**, total flora **−39%**. · **★ THEN THE REAL FIX — PLANTS ARE VOXELS.** `MAT.TUFT/TALL_GRASS/FLOWER`, so collectability falls out of systems that already exist: `raycast` stops at any non-AIR material, `tickBreak`/`dropsFor` read the registry, `recordEdit` diffs the save. **THE PICK HAD TO STICK, AND THAT DECIDED THE ARCHITECTURE:** `recordEdit` stores an edit only when the material DIFFERS from the generated one, so had plants been a later stage (**the way trees are — chopped trees regrowing on reload is the same latent bug, unfixed**), picking a flower would compare AIR to AIR, store nothing, and the flower returns on reload. So "what the generator would have put here" is now ONE function, **`generatedAt`**, and `setVoxel` asks it. ⚠ Plants can NOT go in the depth rule — **mist.ts imports depth, so depth→flora closes a cycle** — hence the assembly layer. · **The instanced renderer STAYS** (crossed quads cannot merge; routing 17k plants through greedy = ~34k unmergeable quads for what is already 4 draw calls) but now **reads the voxel grid**: existence is world state, the LOOK (jitter/turn/colour) stays a pure function of position, so picking one plant cannot restyle its neighbour and no per-plant appearance is stored. · **★ THE ORACLE CAUGHT AN ID COLLISION THAT NOTHING ELSE COULD:** first ids were 14-16 because MAT stops at 13 — and **`ORE.RAW_MANA` is 16**, so a wildflower WAS a mana seam (ore hardness, shard drops) and `isPlant` matched ore and logs all through the underground. The four id enums are separate `const` objects in four files that never see each other; **depth.ts now carries the map** (MAT 0-13 · ORE 16-22 · PLANTS 24-26 · WOOD 32-39 · STRUCTURE 48-49). Also: `isHalfCell` had to accept a plant above a lip or **slump would have silently died on the ~20% of tended ground that carries flora** — a feature disabled by another feature. · Oracles: plants 32 (new), slump 25, greedy 103, mine, drops, edits, purity 242, canon 7 CLEAN. Mesh cost with plants: **3.4ms/col, quads unchanged** — they cost the mesher nothing. ⏭ **Alex: is the lag actually gone, and does breaking grass feel right?** Next suspects if not: the flora resync rebuilds every instance matrix for every loaded column at the end of each streaming burst, and the remesh budget is 12ms of every frame. *Last touched 2026-08-11.*

> **✅ ⑦ THE 08-11 LATE RUN — COLLECTABLES, SLABS, THE POT, INVENTORY, AND EYES (2026-08-11, `344b6b1`..`2dc165b`, deployed, canon 7 CLEAN).** One long chain, each link found by Alex playtesting the last. **Ground cover became BLOCKS** (`MAT.TUFT/TALL_GRASS/FLOWER`) so everything is collectable — and the architecture was decided by one requirement, **the pick must STICK**: `recordEdit` stores an edit only when the material differs from the generated one, so a later-stage write would compare AIR to AIR and the flower returns on reload. Hence **`generatedAt`**, one definition of "what the generator would have put here". · **The same bug one layer out killed CHOPPING: 99.9% of tree/leaf voxels compared against AIR**, so chopped trees regrew. Trees can't use the plant fix (`plantTrees` scans neighbouring chunks), so the generator now **snapshots bare terrain and diffs itself** → `Column.overrides`, exact for carving/ore/trees/ruins/waystones at once, **sparse** because a full pristine copy is 82MB at max view radius. ⚠ It must **travel with the voxels across the worker boundary** — same trap the slump mask hit that morning: *anything DERIVED during generation must be shipped or rebuilt on adoption*. · **★ ALEX REJECTED MY FIRST SLAB FIX** ("that just went around the issue") and was right: half-ness lived on the (x,z) COLUMN, so it described the GROUND, not the block in it. **Now it is a bit on the MATERIAL** — mining a lip drops a slab ITEM, stone placed in a lip is a whole stone block, a stone slab is half wherever you put it, and persistence is free. Then slabs learned to **stack, merge and hang**; **top slabs cost locomotion NOTHING** (the open lower half is 0.5 tall and the player is 1.8, so nothing can stand there) and **coverage became a SPAN not a boolean**, or every slab staircase gets see-through gaps. · **The pot** turns a Mana Seed into a spirit — three MATERIALS, not a growth record, so a planted pot survives reload/evict with no new persistence; bloom reuses the canon-flat `rollBloomSpecies` (*the spirit chooses you*, no prompt, no pick). Seed rate **1/2500** after 1/1,000,000 measured out at ~11.6 days of continuous breaking. · **INVENTORY:** Alex stepped back — and the work was never lost, it was **never wired**. `engine/inventory.ts` (24 slots, chests, stacks) shipped for the 2D game and voxel3d used four functions from it. **★ Every voxel item had `maxStack` 1** because `getMaxStack` reads the *2D game's* tables — **the bag filled at 24 ITEMS and everything mined after was destroyed in silence**, hidden perfectly by a count-derived hotbar. Fixed with a `give()` wrapper; the bar became the **first 8 real SLOTS** (slot 3 was not a place before); a full bag now **refuses the pickup**; **stack size became a lever** (99 ground · 16 made things · **4 a Mana Seed**); and the **satchel** (`I`) is one window onto the same grid, click-to-lift not HTML5 drag. · **★ AND THEN I COULD SEE.** Alex: *"what can we set up so that you can see it?"* — the answer was **not a screenshot harness** but making the generator **pure**, so the code that ships and the code anyone inspects are the same. `scripts/icon-sheet.mts` (sharp, no browser) — **its first run found two bugs no test could:** `tiles.put` **defaults alpha to 0 and the atlas uses that channel as a GLOW MASK**, so icons drew only the parts of a block that emit light; and ground cover had **no painter case**, so `paintFor`'s ORE default rendered grass as **magenta gemstones**. `scripts/world-shot.mts` (system chromium + swiftshader + seeded birth gate + settle time — **all three fail silently**) now screenshots the live 3D world. · **⛔ CANON GAP LOGGED** (athernyx `1d6d713`): Alex's biome-owned-spirits idea collides with *spirits have NO home-regions* and the flat 1/10 bloom — **a biome-keyed seed doesn't remove the choice, it relocates it**. Parked for Magii; per-biome terrain/flora/trees is unblocked build and is the next thing. ⏭ **Next session:** per-biome character · Alex to eyeball the first world shot (**blue-grey wash**, and **no ground cover visible in the glade** — possible regression) · chests · non-block item art. *Last touched 2026-08-11.*

> **✅ ⑧ CHESTS — THE FIRST BLOCK THAT HOLDS SOMETHING (2026-08-11, `4cd6636`, deployed :3200, canon 7 CLEAN, chest oracle 43 + satchel 16).** Closes the last written-but-unused piece of the inventory lane. `MAT.CHEST` + registry row + an **8-plank hand recipe** (by hand and cheap on purpose: a chest is what makes a 24-slot bag survivable, so gating it behind the bench would mean the first hours are spent throwing things away — the bench's own bootstrap argument) + `paintChest` (⚠ a `TILE_MATERIALS` append with no `paintFor` case falls to the ORE painter — that is how every tree once rendered as crystal). · **★ CONTENTS LIVE IN THE COLUMN'S SAVE RECORD**, beside its block edits and pieces, **not** in a global sidecar like the pot clock: a chest's block and what is inside it have to arrive and leave in **one transaction**, or a refresh lands between two loads and a break in that window destroys the contents. Same argument `ColumnSave`'s own header makes for blocks and pieces sharing a record; it also means a hundred chests cost nothing until you walk to them. Kept in memory across an evict for exactly the reason edits are. · **⚠ A CHEST WRITE DOES NOT GO THROUGH `setVoxel`**, so `touchChest()` marks the column dirty explicitly — without it a session that only sorted its storage saves **nothing**. And `setVoxel` drops the record whenever a cell stops being (or becomes) a chest, so no future path (explosion, deconstruct, console verb) can strand contents at a cell and hand the next chest built there somebody else's items. · **★ ONE MOVE FUNCTION:** `moveBetween(gridA, i, gridB, j, maxStack)` is the only implementation and the satchel is it **called with one array twice** — a bag→bag and a bag→chest move differ in nothing, and written twice they agree today and drift the first time one is fixed, silently. `satchel.ts` was **deleted** rather than left as a wrapper nobody calls. **Shift-click** sends a whole stack across (a container costing 24 pairs of clicks to fill is one nobody fills), merging into existing stacks before taking an empty slot — the same function a pickup uses, so putting a thing away by hand and walking over it land it in the same slot. **A chest is the SAME `BagPanel` with a second grid on top**, not a screen of its own: the bag half of a chest screen and the satchel are the same 24 slots. **Breaking spills** rather than refusing to break — the pile is visible and `tickDrops`' capacity gate already leaves what will not fit on the ground. · **★ FOUND ON THE WAY IN, A LIVE ITEM-DESTRUCTION BUG:** `chest` is **already an id in the 2D game's `FURNITURE` table**, so `engine/inventory.addItems` silently refused to put one past slot 15 while `roomFor` knew nothing of that rule — `tickDrops` consumed the drop, `give` returned a leftover nobody surfaced, and **a walked-over chest was destroyed while the HUD said "bag full"**. Same family as this morning's every-item-`maxStack`-1 find: **the 2D tables are another game's balance**, and voxel3d's `give` no longer routes through them (`addToGrid` in chest.ts). Asserted by name so it cannot come back. · Chest art is a procedural placeholder painter like the bench and the pot — **looked at** through the icon sheet, latch resized to read at 16px rather than only blown up. · **⚠ AND IT SHIPPED INERT — FIXED SAME DAY (`fd07331`, deployed, interact oracle 17).** Alex crafted a chest, placed it, right-clicked, and **nothing happened**. The entire use-chain (chest + all three pot states) sat behind `selItem &&` — something in hand. Placing needs that; **using does not**, and nothing said so out loud. So the very first thing anyone does with a chest failed: you place your **only** chest, the slot empties, `selItem` goes null, and the click that should open it fell through the whole block. **Two chests in the slot and it works perfectly**, which is exactly why it shipped green past a 43-assert oracle. **★ A DEAD CLICK IS THE LEAST VISIBLE BUG A GAME CAN HAVE** — nothing throws, nothing logs, no state changes, so there is no evidence to read afterwards and a player cannot tell a missing feature from a broken one. The fix is therefore not `&&` deletion but moving the decision **out of the render loop** into pure `rightClickIntent` (`voxel3d/interact.ts`), which the component **calls** rather than keeping a second copy of the chain beside it — a preview that re-derives the maths can be right while the game is wrong (the icon-rasteriser lesson). Empty-handed-opens-a-chest is asserted **by name**. The fallback stays `place` deliberately: it is the only outcome that **consumes** something, so an unrecognised block drops a block (visible, undoable) instead of swallowing the click. · **Next in the lane:** item ART for non-block items (mana seed, raw shard, tufts, flowers) = **Alex-domain pixel work**.

> **✅ ⑨ SPLITTING A STACK (2026-08-11, `fe2eea5`, deployed :3200, canon 7 CLEAN, chest oracle 43 → 67, satchel 16 → 25).** Right-click lifts **half**, left-click places it; right-click **while anything is lifted drops ONE** and keeps the lift, so a stack can be dealt out as well as halved. Works in the bag alone — a chest is where you **put** things, not what makes a stack divisible, and a gate slipped in there would be invisible until someone tried it one-handed (asserted in the satchel oracle for that reason). · **★ NOTHING LEAVES THE GRID AT LIFT TIME, not even a half.** The items sit in their slot until the placing click, so closing the panel, refreshing or crashing mid-split loses **exactly nothing** — there is no floating carried stack to strand. Same reason drag here is click-then-click rather than HTML5 drag-and-drop, one level in; a `Lift` is a slot ref plus *how* it was lifted, not a stack in limbo. · **★ THE AMOUNT IS READ AT PLACE TIME, NOT FROZEN AT LIFT.** The grid is a live array — a drop walked over while the panel is open grows the stack under the lift — and a number frozen a click ago would take *half of what it used to be*, a quiet theft nobody would ever trace. The lifted slot **shows the number it will take**, because half of 7 is 4 here and 3 in other games and a player should not have to find that out. · **★ `moveCount` IS A SECOND FUNCTION BESIDE `moveBetween` ON PURPOSE, NOT A DUPLICATE** — and that is the interesting call, given ⑧'s whole lesson was *one move function*. It is the one move that must **never swap**: `moveBetween` may swap because it carries a whole stack, but a **partial** stack landing on a different item has no honest outcome (destroy the target, or invent the carried stack we just refused). So it moves nothing and returns **0**, and the caller **keeps the lift alive on a 0** — which is what makes the refusal *visible* rather than the click evaporating. Folding it in as a `want` parameter would mean one function whose swap branch is live for some argument values and forbidden for others: **the same `X && useX()` shape that hid the dead chest click that morning**. Two functions, each total over its own inputs. · **`want` is clamped, not trusted** — both callers derive it from a count read a moment earlier, so conservation is enforced at the only place that can see both sides, not asked of every caller; the item's own ceiling binds a split exactly as it binds a merge. · **⚠ `preventDefault` on the slot AND the backdrop** — right-click is a game verb inside this panel now, and a browser menu opened by a near-miss covers the grid and swallows the click that follows, so the lift would look stuck. · Oracle covers both grids, both directions, the swap refusal, the ceiling, negative and oversized wants, and dealing ones until dry. · ⏭ **Alex to call:** whether right-click-half + right-click-drops-one is the right pair of verbs, and whether the sky-blue lift + count badge reads apart from the amber whole-stack lift at a glance.

> **✅ ⑩ DRAG, AND THE PANEL STOPS FLINCHING (2026-08-11→12, `a31f336` + `c005dd8`, deployed :3200).** Alex: *"when you select to move an item the chest menu gets a little smaller"* and *"no drag to move yet i see."* · **★ THE PANEL WAS RESIZING BECAUSE ITS WIDTH WAS SET BY A SENTENCE.** It is a shrink-to-fit flex item, so the widest thing inside it wins — and that was the **hint text**, not the grid of slots. Lifting swapped in a shorter hint, the panel narrowed, and every slot moved out from under the cursor **mid-action**; ⑨ made it worse by lengthening the idle hint. Every hint is now always in the DOM, **stacked in one grid cell**, only the live one visible — `invisible`, never `hidden`, which is the whole trick because it keeps the box. **Self-maintaining:** a future hint cannot reintroduce the jump without also being in the list, because the list IS the layout; a hardcoded width would have fixed the symptom and rotted the first time a sentence grew. · **DRAG: left-drag carries a stack and drops it where you release; right-drag DEALS ONE into each slot you cross**, landing them on the way rather than on release, which is the point of the gesture. Right-drag-lifts-half was the symmetric choice and is the wrong one — it adds nothing over right-click-then-left-click, whereas the sprinkle is a verb the panel did not have. · **★ THE POINTER OWNS THE WHOLE INTERACTION, and the reason is a bug that reproduces on one desk and not the next: `contextmenu` fires at DIFFERENT TIMES per platform** — mousedown under X11/Mac, mouseup under Windows. Layering pointer handlers beside the click verbs would have fired the right-CLICK verb before a right-DRAG began on *some* machines. Deriving both from pointerdown/up makes the menu's timing irrelevant; `contextmenu` now only `preventDefault`s. Second reason: a drag ends over a **different element** than it began on and `click` only fires on the common ancestor, so a drag between slots fires no click while one ending where it started does — not relying on that is less code than suppressing it. **Keyboard kept** via `onClick` gated on `detail === 0`. · **`half: boolean` became `LiftMode` (`whole`/`half`/`one`)** — the third verb arrived and a boolean would have had to answer *"is a sprinkle half?"*, a question with no true answer, so either the badge or the highlight lies about one of them. Three modes, three looks, in **one table** so a fourth cannot ship invisible. · **`visited` is what makes the sprinkle one-per-slot** (a pointer wobbling inside one slot would otherwise pour the whole stack in), source pre-seeded so it never feeds itself; **`pointercancel`** clears the drag because on touch a system gesture steals the pointer and no `pointerup` ever arrives, leaving the panel permanently mid-drag; **`touch-none`** stops the browser claiming the drag as a scroll. · Every verb still routes through `moveBetween`/`moveCount` — oracles unchanged and green, which is the point.

> **✅ ⑪ A MENU TAKES THE CONTROLS WITH IT (2026-08-12, `4369cc6`, deployed :3200, oracles chest 67 · satchel 25 · interact 17, canon 7 CLEAN).** Alex: *"the controls are still having the player crouch and stuff, plus it needs a close or esc so the mouse goes back to camera mode."* · **★ THREE PLACES NEEDED TO KNOW WHETHER A MENU WAS UP AND EACH HAD ITS OWN IDEA.** The canvas re-lock gate carried a list; the verb handler inferred it from whichever flags its own `if` happened to name; **the world's raw key/mouse listeners did not know menus existed at all.** So Shift crouched the player under the open bag — and, the half nobody would have reported, **a `mousedown` on a SLOT set `mouse.left`, which the frame loop reads as *start mining*, so clicking around your inventory broke the block you were facing.** That one leaves damage behind and nothing on screen says it happened. · **One `cursorUIOpen` const, read by all three.** A list like that drifts the moment a surface is added and it drifts **silently** — the new panel simply fails to suppress the world, which reads as a physics bug rather than a missing entry. It also picked up `consoleOpen`, missing from the re-lock gate: a canvas click while typing a command **seized the mouse back mid-sentence**. · **★ A MENU SWALLOWS THE PRESS, NEVER THE RELEASE.** Gate `keyup` as well and a key that was DOWN when the menu opened is stranded `true` forever — open the bag mid-sprint, close it, and the player walks into a wall **with no key left to press that would stop them**, because the physical release already happened behind the gate. **Down is a request the world may refuse; up is a fact it has to record.** The frame loop also clears held input while a surface is up, covering the same case from the other side (held at open time, never released at all). · **The surface keys C/I/E/O and Escape moved ABOVE the world-verb gate** — they are the doors, and a door that only works when nothing is open is not a door. Past that line every key changes the world, so a surface stops all of them, **including the scroll wheel**, which had been walking the hotbar under the open bag. · **A visible × on the panel.** I and Escape both closed it already, but neither is discoverable from inside it: a free mouse and no button to press reads as **the game having hung**. · **The framing (play window's, and it is the better one): a surface that does not own what it is covering** — the same class as a tool arc dimming its own plate. · ⏭ **Alex to confirm on playtest** that Shift and clicks no longer reach the world through an open bag.

A roster is a list of NAMES; nothing in it fights. · Order mattered: extract the range's ground hunter into **`engine/hunter-ai.ts`** along the same seam as `cast-dispatch`/`vitals` (a pure fn returning an **INTENT the host applies**), **wire the RANGE to it first** so the extraction is proven faithful against the thing it came from, then join roster+brain in `crucible-fleet.ts`, then hook the live zone. · **★★ THE EXTRACTION FOUND THE BUG THAT WOULD HAVE BROKEN THE FEATURE.** The range hunter called **`Math.random()` three times** (spawn bearing, spawn distance, strafe phase). Fixed seed, so the match is re-runnable while tuning. · ⏭ **Next:** Alex flip CRUCIBLE BOTS in the Crucible and call the feel · **`crucible-phases.ts` is STILL unwired** — the match clock (floors, ascent windows, the seal) exists and is tested at 42 asserts and *nothing drives the game from it*; same shape as everything else found today.
> **✅ ⑫ THE BAG BECOMES ONE SCREEN OF FIVE — THE KEEPER PANEL (2026-08-12, `f8fef8c` + `e80692f` + `1a35744` + hub `0113adf`, deployed :3200, canon 7 CLEAN, oracles loadout 25 · satchel 25 · chest 67 · render-audit 71).** Alex: *"expand it to have tabs for the player satchel, runebook, grimoire, tools, and loadout."* `I` now opens **Satchel · Runes · Grimoire · Tools · Loadout**. · **★ THE FRAME IS SIZED ONCE AND NO TAB MAY SET IT.** `BagPanel` was shrink-to-fit — its width was the widest thing inside it, which is *why* every hint sentence is kept in the DOM behind `invisible` rather than `hidden`. I wrote *"cast.ts still maps a birth rune straight to an archetype"* into the Loadout placeholder off the stale row and **it was live on production for an hour**. Third planning-tense trap of the day, and the only one that shipped a false sentence to a player. **Grep `src/` for the implementation before believing a spec's tense** — the SOP that morning's duplicate-piece-layer wrote (`21706ec`). · What was *actually* missing: nothing stored a **CHOICE** (`Shimmer3D` recomputed `defaultLoadout` on every load). `play3d/loadout.ts` persists it and **validates rather than trusts**: no save → the default kit; a save that exists → honoured exactly, **nulls included** (an emptied slot is a decision, not a hole to refill); a bind whose rune is gone resolves to **EMPTY**, never reaching the frame loop as a cast that silently does nothing; one move cannot hold two slots. · **★ THE ORACLE NEARLY SHIPPED UNABLE TO FAIL.** 25 asserts, all three invariants mutation-verified red — but the duplicate rule came back **green** under a mutation that deleted it outright: the fixture drew its slot pair from whatever `defaultLoadout` bound first, got the *passive*, found no second passive slot and passed itself through an `else` branch I had written as a free pass. The same fixture named a rune **`storm` that does not exist**, so the file had quietly been testing a one-rune keeper with no tactical at all. **An assert that cannot fail is worse than no assert: it reports coverage it does not have.** · **GRIMOIRE = a second VIEW, not a second grimoire.** `components/Grimoire.tsx` exists (269 lines) and is good, but it stands on the 2D pipeline (`drawSprite`/`sprites/palette`/`SpriteAnim`) which this world does not load — mounting it meant dragging the whole 2D sprite path into the voxel bundle to draw thumbnails. Entries are a **lit cube face** instead (element colour, bright top-left, dark bottom-right = the read the mesher's AO gives a block corner), so it needs **zero art**. Both canon-ruled faces: what a spirit IS (10 species rows → 4 second forms, the element chips doubling as a completion column) and who YOURS are. **Until this, the only view of your own party was an owner console printing a text table.** · **★ NO "BANK" ANYWHERE, AND THAT IS CANON NOT TASTE.** `glossary.md`: there is no spirit-bank, box or depot in the Ather, because a keeper knows spirits and never stores them. `Spirit.inParty`'s comment **said** *"false = stored in bank"* — mechanic right, framing wrong, and **a wrong word in a shared type is how it reaches a HUD**. Tab says *With you* / *In your garden*; hub fixed the comment at source with the citation. · **★ WHAT IT CANNOT KNOW IS STATED, NOT FAKED:** no persisted `SpiritIndex` exists in voxel3d (`engine/spirit-index.ts` is complete and instantiated by **nothing**), so a spirit merely met leaves no trace and knowledge is derived from spirits actually **raised**; and awakened forms are excluded outright because `Spirit` carries no `branch`. A **"0 / 210" that can never move** would have hidden both gaps. · ⏭ **Next in this lane:** wire `markSeen` at the encounter site so the grimoire index becomes real rather than derived (hub takes it inside #294) · Loadout binds take effect where the cast layer lives until #294 ports it here.

Remaining work: half-height flag in the section encoding (Uint16 has spare bits), mesher emits half-cuboids for flagged natural cells (greedy currently full-cube only), a gen pass, probe maps flag→CELL_HALF, mining strips flag→base material. **★ The design twist to keep: slump strength rides `zone.tended`** — the garden STROLLS, the wilds stay stepped, greyfields sharpen; terrain personality on the axis the world already uses for safety and color. **⚖ Ruling Alex owes before build: stroll-vs-clamber** — slumped country means the vault press stops being how you climb hills (it stays for built walls / 2-highs / cliffs). Sister item, cheaper: stair CORNER variants via the same derived-state trick as fence arms (3 shapes, straight/inner/outer, from neighbour stair facings).
>
> **Decision (2026-08-07):** a **world reset is a client-side epoch stamp, not a server delete**. A Shimmer character lives in localStorage; `accounts.db` only mirrors it. Deleting the `saves` rows loses a race — a browser still holding the old save re-uploads it (measured: a row verified deleted was back minutes later, and the pull then *closed the birth modal*). So the epoch travels **inside** the save: `cloud-sync.ts` stamps on push, `pullCloudSave` refuses unstamped. Bump `ATHER_EPOCH` to reset everyone, including accounts that have not logged in yet.
>
> ### ✅ BLOCK TEXTURE SPIKE DONE 2026-08-06 (`4b65965`→`2fc15c4`, jin-cc texture lane) — **texture arrays, not an atlas**
> Route **`/shimmer/voxel3d/tex`** — one terrain patch rendered TWICE from the SAME `BufferGeometry`, 32px tiles left / 64px right, so tile size is the only variable. Keys: `1` flat · `2` textured · `V` per-block variation · `M` mipmaps · `T` tiles. `?cam=x,y,z&look=x,y,z` pins a viewpoint (an A/B from two different spots is not an A/B).
> - **★ THE ANSWER: a `sampler2DArray` textures blocks at ZERO cost to the greedy mesher.** Each material is its own layer, so `RepeatWrapping` tiles across a merged quad with no bleed. Measured intact: **67,629 quads from 244,685 faces (3.6×)**. An **atlas cannot do this** — wrapping walks into the neighbour tile, and the usual escape is one-quad-per-block, which throws the entire mesher win away. Costs **one float per vertex**; UVs are derived in-shader from position + normal (axis-aligned unit cubes), so there is **no UV buffer at all**.
> - **`voxel/` was never touched.** Face direction comes from the per-vertex NORMAL the mesher already emits, which is exact for axis-aligned quads — so top/side/bottom variants work today with the pure core untouched.
> - **★ PER-BLOCK VARIATION MUST BE PER-FRAGMENT, NOT PER-VERTEX.** The obvious attribute-based version silently destroys the mesher: two adjacent blocks that differ can no longer merge, and a flat 32×32 floor goes from **1 quad back to 1024** — the atlas mistake in a new hat. Instead the block coord is recovered per-fragment (`floor(worldPos - normal*0.5)`), so variation happens INSIDE a merged quad. **World** position, not object: object space restarts at every section origin, so hashing it stamps the same 16-block pattern into every section. Value only, never hue; ore exempt via the emissive mask.
> - **★ AND IT WORKS WHERE DECORATION CANNOT.** Grass tufts and flowers break up a *surface*; nothing scatters flowers 60 blocks down, which is where mining / Prospecting / the ten strongholds live.
> - **★ THE V AXIS IS NEGATED ON SIDE FACES — this is the art contract, not a hack.** Texture row 0 is the TOP of an image file, but `v` grows with world Y, so without the flip **every hand-painted tile imports upside down.**
> - **★ ALPHA IS AN EMISSIVE MASK, NOT OPACITY** — only the crystal inside an ore block glows, not the whole block. The HUD swatch must force alpha opaque or every non-glowing tile blits transparent. One byte, two consumers, two meanings.
> - **Ore, art-directed by Alex over two passes:** soft radial blobs read as **gumballs** → **Manhattan distance = a DIAMOND silhouette** (at 32px the silhouette does the work: circle = bubble, diamond = cut stone) + **three FLAT tones on a diagonal, no gradient** (a smooth ramp is what makes a shape look inflated) + dark rim seating it in rock + single-texel flecks. Then: shards **clipped at the tile edge** → contained, inset per-axis by `r*sx`/`r*sy` (inset by `r` alone lets the wider ones clip out = the same bug disguised). The toroidal wrap I started with was only half-right — halves DO complete across *adjacent* ore blocks, but ore is scattered singles, so the common case was one isolated block showing two clipped halves.
> - **✅ TILE SIZE RULED 2026-08-06 (Alex): 64.** Overrides the 32 recommendation below, which stands as the reasoning rather than the answer. **Consequence to accept, stated once:** 1 texel = 1 screen px only out to **~11 blocks** (vs ~22 at 32px), so past that the GPU is showing a mip and the extra resolution is not on screen — and each tile is **4× the pixels to hand-paint**. Alex's call; look is his. **There is no TILE_SIZE constant yet** — the spike hard-codes `makeTileArray(32)`/`(64)` for the A/B, so the wiring job must introduce one rather than inherit 32 by accident.
> - **Tile size: 32 recommended, not yet ruled — SUPERSEDED, kept for the reasoning.** At fov75/1080p a block covers ~`704/d` screen px, so 1 texel = 1 screen px out to **~22 blocks @32px · ~11 @64 · ~5.5 @128** — past that the GPU shows a mip level and the extra resolution is *not on screen*. **128 rejected:** 16× the pixels to hand-paint per tile and it stops reading as pixel art. **Memory is not the constraint** (43 layers @64px = 688KB).
> - **⚠ KNOWN, DELIBERATELY UNFIXED:** every ore block shows the identical cluster, so a large vein reads as a stamped repeat. Fix is variant layers selected per-block by the same `hashBlock` the jitter uses — no geometry, no meshing cost. Not worth the layers until a real vein looks wrong.
> - **⛔ MESHY IS NOT FOR VOXEL FLORA (ruled 2026-08-06, jin).** Asked directly whether flowers and
>   similar should come from Meshy. **No, and it would fight the aesthetic three ways.** (1) Meshy
>   makes *organic* meshes — smooth geometry in a blocky, 64px pixel-art world reads as an import
>   from another game. (2) Every generated mesh is its own geometry **and material**, which is
>   precisely the per-object allocation that got this page BLOCKED from WebGL today; thousands of
>   flowers as individual meshes is that bug at scale. (3) It costs credits, against a free-first
>   standing preference. **Flora is a CROSS-PLANE: two intersecting quads with a cutout texture,
>   drawn from the same tile array that already exists** — near-zero cost, matches Minecraft, and
>   reuses the texture work rather than opening a second pipeline. ⚠ One real gotcha: alpha in this
>   shader is an **emissive mask, not opacity**, so cutout flora needs its own material or an
>   explicit flag — do not assume the ore alpha channel means transparency.
>   **Meshy keeps its existing lane** (the arcade / pre-render prop path, per the art-medium law:
>   living things stay live-glow, only dead grey things get pre-rendered). Voxel flora is not that.
> - **Tiles are generated from code** off the placeholder palette so the render path could be judged before anything is painted. **They are not a look call.**
>
> ### ✅ MESHER SPIKE DONE 2026-08-06 (`d018c68`) — **section size = 16**
> Voxel core's first files, pure from the start: `voxel/section.ts` (flat `Uint16Array`, never object-per-voxel, + the single-value-section check), `voxel/greedy.ts` (3-axis slice sweep), `voxel/greedy.test.ts` (**100 asserts**), `voxel/purity.test.ts` (**walks the import graph, fails on any react/three/DOM dep — port rule 4, the only one of the four that can rot**). Browser reading at `/shimmer/dev?mode=meshbench` (owner-gated).
> - **The deciding number is the WORST case, not the average:** a block broken on a section *corner* dirties its own section + up to 7 neighbours. **16³ = 2.0ms · 32³ = 13.4ms · 64³ = 106ms** (8³ = 0.87ms but **57.8% of blocks land on a boundary** vs 33% at 16, and column cost nearly doubles). 32 already eats most of a 16.7ms frame on a desktop-class box.
> - **Column cost is FLAT above 16** (28.9 / 27.6 / 26.8ms) — kills the last argument for going bigger.
> - **★ The first run was measuring my own waste.** Sizing output buffers for the checkerboard worst case = **~626KB of typed arrays allocated and thrown away EVERY call** — precisely the GC pressure that kills browser voxel games. Reusable scratch → **2.5–5× faster**. All figures post-fix.
> - **Greedy earns its place on OUR world shape specifically:** 20–31× fewer quads on surface/underground, 5.3× in caves, 1.0× on checkerboard. Flat ground over solid rock is its best case and that's most of the world.
> - **We derived Minecraft's 16 rather than copying it.**
>
> ### ✅ PHONE DROPPED AS A HARD TARGET 2026-08-06 (Alex)
> Carried in from 2.5D cozy Shimmer (phase 3 sized the whole streaming budget around not killing a phone tab, ~23MB) and never re-checked against the voxel rework. **It never decided the section size anyway** — 32³ fails a frame on a desktop-class box with no phone in the argument.
> - **Unchanged:** section size 16, typed arrays / no object-per-voxel (that's GC + the Rust port path), all 4 port rules, greedy meshing, palette packing. The **Worker** moves from *required* to *headroom* — scheduling, not architecture.
> - **★ RELAXES — worth acting on: world height.** 128 was partly a phone-memory number, and § 8(b) already flagged the datum sketch left only ~32 blocks below surface, shallow for a mining loop. **256 = ~7.8MB packed vs ~3.9MB at 128** — nothing on desktop, doubles the depth for ore tiers / mineshafts / big caverns. **Recommend 128 → 256 now caverns are a headline feature.**
> - Also relaxes: the memory ceiling stops driving decisions (not unlimited — a 500MB tab is still bad), and `DEFAULT_RADIUS = 3` (182 units + fog, already flagged as maybe too close) has room to open.

No placement table to author.

They don't die — **they become authored PIECES the generator places** (Minecraft's village model), not the world itself. Alex's art ships, everything stays generated.

> - **✅ RULED 2026-08-06 (Alex) — all three § 8 calls, as recommended.** **1 voxel = 1 tile** (every sprite/sculpt/coordinate stays valid unchanged — this is *why* the canvases and the sculpt survive) · **world height 128** · **the seven painted canvases survive**, extruded per § 5. ⚠ **The datum split is NOT part of the ruling** — 128 is the format, where y=0 sits vs sea level is a tuning constant; the ~96/~32 sketch is shallow for mining and should be moved freely during the mesher spike.
> - **★ Chunk width is a RE-MESH decision, not a memory decision.** For a fixed footprint the totals are identical at 16/32/64 wide; what changes is how much rebuilds when one block breaks (524k voxels at 64×64×128 vs 4k at 16³ sections). Pick width from re-mesh cost, memory follows.
> - **★ Typed arrays are a 4× win before voxels enter the picture.** Today's 2.5D world spends **~8 bytes/cell** because it's JS `number[][]` (23MB for ~2.9M cells). At 2 bytes + palette packing a **128-deep voxel world is cheaper than the flat grid we ship now.**
